proof.html: Theorem [fnd:generalrelativeinterioropen] proves ordinary openness for arbitrary analytic spaces, and The boundary identity gives locality on admissible analytic-domain covers of the base. Proposition [fnd:generaldomainordinaryinterior] identifies the relative interior of every analytic-domain inclusion with its ordinary topological interior. Theorem [fnd:affinoidboundarylessfinite] proves the affinoid finite criterion, including the canonical finite-module topology and hence admissibility over trivially valued fields. Finally, Proposition [fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange] identifies a finite affinoid base change with its finite tensor algebra equipped with that topology. Applying this on affinoid charts of an arbitrary base change and using the analytic-domain gluing theorem proves stability of finite morphisms.

statement.html: Relative interior is open and behaves locally on the base under analytic-domain covers. proof.html:
A formal model of the given XX includes the identification of its analytic generic fibre with XX, as in the definition in Section [fnd:formalmodels]. Work on that realization. In particular the generic affinoids of the formal charts give an admissible atlas, with the affinoid structures of the formal restriction rings. On a formal affine, a formal function and the inverse of a formal unit are evaluated in the residue valuation ring by Theorem [fnd:affineformalspecializationsurjective]. Refine the frame-trivializing opens of that affine by finitely many principal opens: its topological Noetherianity is the formal-topology clause of NAG-001944. Their generic traces are the actual closed rational domains of Proposition [fnd:formalprincipalopenflat]. On this actual affine the specialization centre is obtained by contraction: a formal element ff avoids the centre of xx exactly when |f(x)|=1|f(x)|=1. Thus the rational trace of each principal open is the full inverse image of that open. The principal opens cover the formal affine, so their traces cover its generic affine. Thus on their actual overlaps, the two frames differ by a formal unit uu, with |u|≤1|u|\leq1 and |u−1|≤1|u^{-1}|\leq1. Consequently |u|=1|u|=1. In an analytic trivialization the local norm of a section is continuous on each of these chart domains. The quasi-net refinement and topology tests in Lemma [fnd:quasinetcalculus] and Lemma [fnd:nettopologyboundedgluing] give continuity on the realized analytic space. This gives the frame-independent metric.

For pullback between formal models, construct the compatible generic map on their actual analytic realizations as follows. On a formal source affine, take a finite principal refinement subordinate to the inverse images of the formal target affines. This is possible by quasi-compactness, since the inverse images are ordinary formal opens. The homomorphism on each piece gives the bounded analytic map on its generic trace by Proposition [fnd:affineformalpresentations]. If two choices are made on overlapping source charts, use specialization to choose a formal affine neighbourhood of the common image inside the intersection of their two target charts. Refine the source at its centre inside the inverse image of that neighbourhood and inside both source pieces. The restrictions of the two bounded maps come from the same formal ring map. These refinements cover the actual analytic overlap because centres contract under the formal arrow, and principal traces are full inverse images of the corresponding formal opens by Proposition [fnd:formalprincipalopenflat] and the centre calculation above. Finite principal refinements on each formal affine give finite closed rational coverings of its generic affine. By Lemma [fnd:quasinetcalculus] these refine the realized atlas admissibly. Theorem [fnd:generalnetmorphismgluing] now glues the local maps and shows independence of the chosen refinements. Restricting to a formal open uses these same local maps on its principal traces. For composable arrows of realized models, refine a source chart subordinate to the intermediate and target restrictions. Both the map for the composite and the composite of the maps are induced there by the composite of the same formal ring homomorphisms, so they agree by uniqueness. The pulled-back frame is again given norm one, proving the pullback equality.

Let b:𝔛′→𝔛b:\mathfrak X'\to\mathfrak X be an admissible formal blowup. By the formal restriction clause of NAG-001945, its restriction over each formal affine is the blowup of the restricted ideal. Use its finite standard affine charts from Theorem [fnd:formalblowupcharts]. By Theorem [fnd:affineblowupgenericinvariance], their generic fibres and transitions are the actual rational domains and restrictions on the corresponding affinoid of XX. On common formal principal restrictions these descriptions are the restrictions of the same blowup, by its formal universal property (Proposition [fnd:formalblowupuniversal]). This checks the cross-chart agreement on the actual generic traces. Each finite rational covering is admissible on its original affinoid. By the transitivity in Lemma [fnd:quasinetcalculus] these rational domains form an admissible refinement of the already realized atlas of XX, even for an infinite original atlas. They give an actual generic realization of 𝔛′\mathfrak X' on XX, with the map bηb_\eta the identity in this realization. Apply the pullback equality in this realization to obtain the blowup assertion.

\begin{proof}
A formal model of the given \(X\) includes the identification
of its analytic generic fibre with \(X\), as in the definition
in Section~\ref{fnd:formalmodels}. Work on that realization.
In particular the generic affinoids of the formal charts give
an admissible atlas, with the affinoid structures of the formal
restriction rings. On a formal affine, a formal function and
the inverse of a formal unit are evaluated in the residue
valuation ring by Theorem~\ref{fnd:affineformalspecializationsurjective}.
Refine the frame-trivializing opens of that affine by finitely
many principal opens: its topological Noetherianity is the
formal-topology clause of
\hyperref[fnd:formalglobalgenericfaithful]{NAG-001944}. Their generic traces are
the actual closed rational domains of
Proposition~\ref{fnd:formalprincipalopenflat}. On this actual
affine the specialization centre is obtained by contraction:
a formal element \(f\) avoids the centre of \(x\) exactly when
\(|f(x)|=1\). Thus the rational trace of each principal open
is the full inverse image of that open. The principal opens
cover the formal affine, so their traces cover its generic
affine.
Thus on their actual overlaps, the two frames differ by a
formal unit \(u\), with \(|u|\leq1\) and \(|u^{-1}|\leq1\).
Consequently \(|u|=1\). In an analytic trivialization the
local norm of a section is continuous on each of these chart
domains. The quasi-net refinement and topology tests in
Lemma~\ref{fnd:quasinetcalculus} and
Lemma~\ref{fnd:nettopologyboundedgluing} give continuity on
the realized analytic space. This gives the frame-independent
metric.

For pullback between formal models, construct the compatible
generic map on their actual analytic realizations as follows.
On a formal source affine, take a finite principal refinement
subordinate to the inverse images of the formal target affines.
This is possible by quasi-compactness, since the inverse images
are ordinary formal opens. The homomorphism on each piece
gives the bounded analytic map on its generic trace by
Proposition~\ref{fnd:affineformalpresentations}. If two choices
are made on overlapping source charts, use specialization to
choose a formal affine neighbourhood of the common image
inside the intersection of their two target charts. Refine the
source at its centre inside the inverse image of that
neighbourhood and inside both source pieces. The restrictions
of the two bounded maps come from the same formal ring map.
These refinements cover the actual analytic overlap because
centres contract under the formal arrow, and principal traces
are full inverse images of the corresponding formal opens by
Proposition~\ref{fnd:formalprincipalopenflat} and the centre calculation above.
Finite principal refinements on each formal affine give finite
closed rational coverings of its generic affine. By
Lemma~\ref{fnd:quasinetcalculus} these refine the realized atlas
admissibly. Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalnetmorphismgluing} now glues
the local maps and shows independence of the chosen refinements.
Restricting to a formal open uses these same local maps on its
principal traces. For composable arrows of realized models,
refine a source chart subordinate to the intermediate and
target restrictions. Both the map for the composite and
the composite of the maps are induced there by the composite
of the same formal ring homomorphisms, so they agree by
uniqueness. The pulled-back frame is again given norm one,
proving the pullback equality.

Let \(b:\mathfrak X'\to\mathfrak X\) be an admissible formal
blowup. By the formal restriction clause of
\hyperref[fnd:formalglobalblowupcalculus]{NAG-001945}, its
restriction over each formal affine is the blowup of the
restricted ideal. Use its finite standard affine charts from
Theorem~\ref{fnd:formalblowupcharts}. By
Theorem~\ref{fnd:affineblowupgenericinvariance}, their generic
fibres and transitions are the actual rational domains and
restrictions on the corresponding affinoid of \(X\). On
common formal principal restrictions these descriptions are
the restrictions of the same blowup, by its formal universal
property (Proposition~\ref{fnd:formalblowupuniversal}).
This checks the cross-chart agreement on the actual generic
traces. Each finite rational covering is admissible on its
original affinoid. By the transitivity in
Lemma~\ref{fnd:quasinetcalculus} these rational domains form an
admissible refinement of the already realized atlas of \(X\),
even for an infinite original atlas. They give an actual
generic realization of \(\mathfrak X'\) on \(X\), with the
map \(b_\eta\) the identity in this realization.
Apply the pullback equality in this realization to obtain
the blowup assertion.
\end{proof}

proof.html:
The ordinary chart construction supplies ℛ0\mathscr R_0, its independence of strict charts and ordinary neighbourhoods, and its comparison with the graded reduction. Proposition [fnd:nag001985:strict-subdomains-functoriality] gives functoriality and the order correspondence, including its compatibility with intersections and finite unions. Theorem [fnd:formalmodelgermrealization] identifies this ordinary space with the pointed residual construction for the given admissible formal models of the compact strict neighbourhoods in that construction. The reduced pointed closures are compared by Proposition [fnd:formalmodificationspecialproper] and Lemma [fnd:properpointedvaluationcomparison] over the same ordinary completed residue field.

By Lemma [fnd:gradeddegreeonevaluation], ordinary and graded affineness agree for the two compared reductions. The ordinary affinoid neighbourhood criterion proves the forward implication and Theorem [fnd:nag001982:affine-to-good] the reverse implication for the same germ.

For the separation and interior criteria write Q0,P0Q_0,P_0 for the ordinary source and target reductions with respective fields G0,E0G_0,E_0, and Q,PQ,P for their graded reductions. The map Q0→P0×𝒫K̃(E0)𝒫K̃(G0)Q_0\longrightarrow P_0 \times_{\mathscr P_{\widetilde K}(E_0)} \mathscr P_{\widetilde K}(G_0) pulls back along $\mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}}(G) \to\mathscr P_{\widetilde K}(G_0)$ to $$Q\longrightarrow P \times_{\mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}}(E)} \mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}}(G).$$ This follows from the natural pullback comparison and the commutative square of degree-one and field restrictions. The comparison on source valuation spaces is surjective, so the map on each ordinary fibre is injective, respectively bijective, if and only if all of its graded pullbacks have that property. By the definitions of separation and properness of the birational morphisms, the corresponding ordinary and graded properties are equivalent. Proposition [fnd:gradedgermseparation] and Theorem [fnd:generalproperreductioninterior] now give separation at the point and the original all-target-domain criterion for relative interior.

\begin{proof}
The
\hyperref[fnd:ordinarystrictgermreductionconstruction]{ordinary chart
construction} supplies \(\mathscr R_0\), its independence of strict
charts and ordinary neighbourhoods, and its comparison with the
graded reduction. Proposition~\ref{fnd:nag001985:strict-subdomains-functoriality}
gives functoriality and the order correspondence, including
its compatibility with intersections and finite unions.
Theorem~\ref{fnd:formalmodelgermrealization} identifies this ordinary
space with the pointed residual construction for the given
admissible formal models of the compact strict neighbourhoods
in that construction. The reduced pointed closures are compared
by Proposition~\ref{fnd:formalmodificationspecialproper} and
Lemma~\ref{fnd:properpointedvaluationcomparison} over the same
ordinary completed residue field.

By Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradeddegreeonevaluation}, ordinary and
graded affineness agree for the two compared reductions. The
\hyperref[fnd:nag001886:good-affine-forward]{ordinary affinoid
neighbourhood criterion} proves the forward implication and
Theorem~\ref{fnd:nag001982:affine-to-good} the reverse
implication for the same germ.

For the separation and interior criteria write \(Q_0,P_0\) for the
ordinary source and target reductions with respective fields
\(G_0,E_0\), and \(Q,P\) for their graded reductions. The map
\[
 Q_0\longrightarrow P_0
   \times_{\mathscr P_{\widetilde K}(E_0)}
               \mathscr P_{\widetilde K}(G_0)
\]
pulls back along
\(\mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}}(G)
    \to\mathscr P_{\widetilde K}(G_0)\)
to
\[
 Q\longrightarrow P
   \times_{\mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}}(E)}
               \mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}}(G).
\]
This follows from the natural pullback comparison and the
commutative square of degree-one and field restrictions. The
comparison on source valuation spaces is surjective, so the
map on each ordinary fibre is injective, respectively bijective,
if and only if all of its graded pullbacks have that property.
By the definitions of separation and properness of the
birational morphisms, the corresponding ordinary and graded
properties are equivalent. Proposition~\ref{fnd:gradedgermseparation}
and Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalproperreductioninterior} now give

\end{proof}

NAG-000186.scope: Full original strict analytic germ wrapper under the standing complete nontrivially valued field, locally bounded strict atlas, and actual admissible model hypotheses.

statement.html: For strictly analytic spaces, germ reduction is functorial and independent of the model and neighborhood. Germ subdomains correspond to birational subspaces, compatibly with inclusions, intersections and finite unions. A germ is good precisely when its reduction is affine in the birational category. A morphism is separated at a point precisely when the corresponding reduction morphism is separated; the point lies in relative interior precisely when that reduction morphism is proper.

NAG-000186.title: Reduction of strict analytic germs

proof.html: Theorem [fnd:jacobianflatregularcriterion] gives the criterion for quasi-smoothness with all complete-extension tests on the analytic fibre and all good analytic base changes for flatness. Its domain-local formulation gives the assertion for arbitrary analytic spaces. For good spaces Theorem [fnd:goodsmoothquasismoothinterior] gives the comparison with ordinary-open local étale smoothness at the point. Theorem [fnd:alldomainanalyticflatness] proves flatness for analytic-domain inclusions. Finally, for the ordinary stalks in Definition [fnd:analyticflatness], Theorem [fnd:generalinnercoherentflatness] gives the naive-to-analytic implication for the coherent sheaf at the given interior point of the morphism of good spaces.

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{fnd:jacobianflatregularcriterion} gives the criterion
for quasi-smoothness with all complete-extension tests on the
analytic fibre and all good analytic base changes for flatness.
Its domain-local formulation gives the assertion for arbitrary
analytic spaces. For good spaces
Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodsmoothquasismoothinterior} gives the comparison
with ordinary-open local \'{e}tale smoothness at the point.
Theorem~\ref{fnd:alldomainanalyticflatness} proves flatness for
analytic-domain inclusions. Finally, for the
ordinary stalks in Definition~\ref{fnd:analyticflatness},
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalinnercoherentflatness} gives the
naive-to-analytic implication for the coherent sheaf at the
given interior point of the morphism of good spaces.
\end{proof}

statement.html: A morphism f:Y→Xf:Y\to X is quasi-smooth at yy if and only if it is analytically flat there and its ℋ(f(y))\mathcal H(f(y))-analytic fibre is geometrically regular at yy. For morphisms between good spaces, it is smooth at yy if and only if it is quasi-smooth and boundaryless there. Analytic-domain inclusions are flat. For a morphism between good spaces, naive flatness of a coherent sheaf at an interior point implies analytic flatness there.

NAG-000209.title: Quasi-smooth morphisms

\noindent\textbf{Erratum to NAG-001761.}\quad
In the \hyperref[fnd:separablenormalizationregularlocus]{original regular-locus proof},
the comparison with the algebraic finite tensor product requires the
finite-module norm condition in
\hyperref[fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange]{finite base change}. Boundedness
and algebraic finiteness alone do not imply this condition. The
\hyperref[fnd:charzerouniformregularopen]{strict-normalization application}
uses the previously established guarded case over the nontrivially valued
free strictification, with its actual strict finite Tate normalizer.

\smallskip
\noindent\textit{Failure of the comparison after localization.}
In the \hyperref[fnd:trivialfinitewrongnorm]{two-disc example}, let \(K\)
be trivially valued, take \(0<s<r<1\), and put
\(D=K\{r^{-1}T\}\) and \(A=K\{s^{-1}T\}\). These are both \(K[[T]]\)
as rings. The identity \(D\to A\) is bounded and finite, and induces a
degree-one extension of fraction fields. Its inverse is unbounded
because the ratio of the two norms of \(T^n\) is \((r/s)^n\).

Give \(L=K((\lambda))\) the \(\lambda\)-adic absolute value with
\(s<|\lambda|<r\). Every nonzero \(d\in D\) can be written \(T^m u(T)\)
with \(u(0)\ne0\). The constant term dominates the other terms of
\(u(\lambda)\), so \(d(\lambda)\ne0\). Evaluation at \(T=\lambda\) therefore
extends from \(D_L=L\{r^{-1}T\}\) to \(D_L[1/d]\), where \(T-\lambda\)
is a nonunit. It is a unit in \(A_L=L\{s^{-1}T\}\) by the geometric
series. Since \(A\otimes_D D_L\simeq D_L\) as rings, the map
\[
       (A\otimes_D D_L)[1/d]\longrightarrow A_L[1/d]
\]
fails to be an isomorphism for every nonzero \(d\in D\).

\smallskip
\noindent\textit{Uniform regularity for analytically separable extensions.}
Keep the hypotheses on \(D\to A\) in the original statement, and test
only \hyperref[fnd:analyticseparabilitydefinition]{analytically separable}
complete extensions \(L/K\). Write \(X_L=\mathcal M(A_L)\). There is a
single nonzero \(d\in D\) such that, for every such extension and every
\(y\in X_L\), the rings
\[
        A_L[1/d],\qquad
        \mathcal O_{X_L,y}[1/d],\qquad
        \widehat{\mathcal O_{X_L,y}}[1/d]
\]
are regular. The completion here is at the maximal ideal of the ordinary
local ring.

The \hyperref[fnd:generalanalyticseparableregularopen]{uniform regular-open result}
gives \(0\ne a\in A\) such that \(A_L[1/a]\) is regular for all these
\(L\). Choose a monic equation for \(a\) over \(D\) of least degree.
Its constant term \(d\) is nonzero, since otherwise cancellation of \(a\)
in the domain \(A\) gives a monic equation of smaller degree. The
equation gives \(d\in aA\cap D\), so \(a\) is invertible wherever \(d\)
is inverted.

Fix \(L\) and \(y\), put \(\mathfrak p=\ker(y)\) and
\(R=\mathcal O_{X_L,y}\), and let \(\widehat R\) denote its completion.
The \hyperref[fnd:generalizedordinaryregularcomparison]{ordinary comparison}
gives regular maps of Noetherian rings
\[
        (A_L)_{\mathfrak p}\longrightarrow R\longrightarrow \widehat R.
\]
For a prime of \(R\) avoiding \(a\), localize the first map at that prime
and its contraction. The resulting local map is flat with regular closed
fibre, and its source is a localization of the regular ring \(A_L[1/a]\).
Thus its target is regular by \cite[Tag 031E]{StacksAlg}. For a prime of

Apply the same argument to the second map. This proves the regularity
of \(R[1/a]\) and \(\widehat R[1/a]\), and inverting \(d\) gives further

\(y\), including \(d(y)=0\).

By definition every complete extension in characteristic zero is
analytically separable. If \(K\) is perfect of characteristic \(p>0\),
then \(K^p=K\) and the defining multiplication is the isometric

of \(p\)-th powers have Cauchy sequences of \(p\)-th roots:
\(|u^p-v^p|=|u-v|^p\). Thus the conclusion holds for all complete
extensions of a perfect base field as well.

is regular for every complete \(L/K\) by
\hyperref[fnd:affinespacedomainregular]{regularity of affine-space domains}.

germ conclusions. This example refutes the proof comparison only.

extensions that are not analytically separable and lie outside the
established norm guard remains unresolved here.

proof.html:
All the ordinary local rings below are Noetherian by Theorem [fnd:ordinaryanalyticstalknoetherian]. In the smooth case, use the ordinary-open local étale factorization through a relative analytic affine space. Proposition  [fnd:relativeaffinespaceordinaryregular] makes the map from the base ordinary local ring to the ordinary stalk of the affine-space chart regular. Lemma [fnd:etaleordinaryregular] makes the next ordinary local homomorphism regular, on the actual étale map. Their composition is regular by . Every composite fibre ring is a localization of a quotient of the target Noetherian local ring.

For the quasi-smooth map, use Theorem [fnd:quasismoothsmoothenvelope] on the actual original germ. It gives an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood VV of yy in YY, over an ordinary neighbourhood of xx, as an affinoid domain in a smooth ambient space TT. Write tt for the image of yy in TT. On the ordinary local rings the map is 𝒪X,x→𝒪T,t→𝒪V,y=𝒪Y,y.\mathcal O_{X,x}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{T,t} \longrightarrow\mathcal O_{V,y}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}. The first arrow is regular by the smooth case. The second is regular by Corollary [fnd:analyticdomainordinaryregular], applied to the actual good domain and good ambient space. Apply again. The composite fibres are Noetherian by the same localization and quotient argument.

For the separate affinoid assertion put 𝔭=ker(x)\mathfrak p=\ker(x) and 𝔮=ker(y)\mathfrak q=\ker(y). By Theorem [fnd:generalizedordinaryregularcomparison], A𝔭→𝒪X,xA_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{X,x} and B𝔮→𝒪Y,yB_{\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y} are regular. The map A𝔭→𝒪X,x→𝒪Y,yA_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y} is regular by ; its fibres are again localizations of quotients of the target Noetherian ring. It factors through B𝔮B_{\mathfrak q} by the compatible evaluation maps. The flat map B𝔮→𝒪Y,yB_{\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y} is local, so its closed fibre is nonzero and makes it faithfully flat and surjective on spectra. proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
All the ordinary local rings below are Noetherian by
Theorem~\ref{fnd:ordinaryanalyticstalknoetherian}. In the smooth case,
use the ordinary-open local \'etale factorization through a relative
analytic affine space. Proposition~
\ref{fnd:relativeaffinespaceordinaryregular} makes the map from the
base ordinary local ring to the ordinary stalk of the affine-space
chart regular. Lemma~\ref{fnd:etaleordinaryregular} makes the next
ordinary local homomorphism regular, on the actual \'etale map.
Their composition is regular by \cite[Tag 07QI]{StacksAlg}.
Every composite fibre ring is a localization of a quotient of the
target Noetherian local ring.

For the quasi-smooth map, use
Theorem~\ref{fnd:quasismoothsmoothenvelope} on the actual original
germ. It gives an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood \(V\) of \(y\)
in \(Y\), over an ordinary neighbourhood of \(x\), as an
affinoid domain in a smooth ambient space \(T\). Write \(t\) for
the image of \(y\) in \(T\). On the ordinary local rings the map
is
\[
 \mathcal O_{X,x}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{T,t}
     \longrightarrow\mathcal O_{V,y}=\mathcal O_{Y,y}.
\]
The first arrow is regular by the smooth case. The second is
regular by Corollary~\ref{fnd:analyticdomainordinaryregular}, applied
to the actual good domain and good ambient space. Apply
\cite[Tag 07QI]{StacksAlg} again. The composite fibres are
Noetherian by the same localization and quotient argument.

For the separate affinoid assertion put
\(\mathfrak p=\ker(x)\) and \(\mathfrak q=\ker(y)\). By
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedordinaryregularcomparison},
\(A_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\) and
\(B_{\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}\) are regular. The map
\(A_{\mathfrak p}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}\) is
regular by \cite[Tag 07QI]{StacksAlg}; its fibres are again
localizations of quotients of the target Noetherian ring.
It factors through \(B_{\mathfrak q}\) by the compatible evaluation
maps. The flat map \(B_{\mathfrak q}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}\) is local,
so its closed fibre is nonzero and
\cite[Tag 00HP(4) to (1) and (3)]{StacksAlg} makes it faithfully
flat and surjective on spectra. Apply \cite[Tag 07NT]{StacksAlg}
to this factorization to obtain regularity of
\(A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}\).
\end{proof}

NAG-001795.title: Ordinary regularity of quasi-smooth morphisms

proof.html:
Write R=𝒪X,xR=\mathcal O_{X,x} and S=𝒪Y,yS=\mathcal O_{Y,y}. Theorem [fnd:quasismoothordinaryregular] applied to these ordinary stalks makes R→SR\to S a regular homomorphism of Noetherian local rings. In particular it is flat and S/𝔪RSS/\mathfrak m_R S is regular. If RR is regular, makes SS regular; if SS is regular, makes RR regular.

If RR is normal, every algebraic fibre is regular by the regular-map assertion and thus normal by . Now applies to R→SR\to S and all these fibre rings, giving normality of SS. Conversely, assume SS is normal. The map is local, so the closed fibre is nonzero. Since it is flat, gives faithful flatness. For any RR-module MM, the natural map M→S⊗RMM\to S\otimes_R M is injective: after tensoring with SS it is split by multiplication on the two SS factors, and faithful flatness reflects injectivity. In particular RR embeds into the normal local domain SS and is a domain. If a/b∈Frac(R)a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}(R) is integral over RR, its image is integral over SS and lies in SS. Apply the same module injection to R/bRR/bR: it gives bS∩R=bRbS\cap R=bR, so a/b∈Ra/b\in R. This proves normality of RR.

Taking every yy gives the asserted normality on good spaces. After any stated analytic base change or complete extension, Theorem [fnd:jacobiansmoothdomainbasechange] gives quasi-smoothness on the actual new morphism. When its spaces are good the same proof applies to its ordinary local rings. The comparison is with the local ring of the new base.
proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Write \(R=\mathcal O_{X,x}\) and \(S=\mathcal O_{Y,y}\).
Theorem~\ref{fnd:quasismoothordinaryregular} applied to these
ordinary stalks makes \(R\to S\) a regular homomorphism of
Noetherian local rings. In particular it is flat and
\(S/\mathfrak m_R S\) is regular. If \(R\) is regular,
\cite[Tag 031E]{StacksAlg} makes \(S\) regular; if \(S\) is
regular, \cite[Tag 00OF]{StacksAlg} makes \(R\) regular.

If \(R\) is normal, every algebraic fibre is regular by the
regular-map assertion and thus normal by
\cite[Tag 0567]{StacksAlg}. Now \cite[Tag 0C22]{StacksAlg}
applies to \(R\to S\) and all these fibre rings, giving normality
of \(S\). Conversely, assume \(S\) is normal. The map is local,
so the closed fibre is nonzero. Since it is flat,
\cite[Tag 00HP(4) to (1)]{StacksAlg} gives faithful flatness.
For any \(R\)-module \(M\), the natural map \(M\to S\otimes_R M\)
is injective: after tensoring with \(S\) it is split by
multiplication on the two \(S\) factors, and faithful flatness
reflects injectivity. In particular \(R\) embeds into the
normal local domain \(S\) and is a domain. If
\(a/b\in\operatorname{Frac}(R)\) is integral over \(R\), its image
is integral over \(S\) and lies in \(S\). Apply the same module
injection to \(R/bR\): it gives \(bS\cap R=bR\), so \(a/b\in R\).
This proves normality of \(R\).

Taking every \(y\) gives the asserted normality on good spaces.
After any stated analytic base change or complete extension,
Theorem~\ref{fnd:jacobiansmoothdomainbasechange} gives
quasi-smoothness on the actual new morphism. When its spaces
are good the same proof applies to its ordinary local rings.
The comparison is with the local ring of the new base.
\end{proof}

proof.html:
Suppose first that yy is interior. Choose finitely many affinoid domains Xi⊂XX_i\subset X, all containing xx, whose union is a neighborhood of xx. Write Yi=f−1(Xi)Y_i=f^{-1}(X_i). Conversely, suppose the reduction is proper and let U⊂XU\subset X be any affinoid domain containing xx. Put V=f−1(U)V=f^{-1}(U). proof.html:
Suppose ff is boundaryless. The analytic base-change clause makes every point of the actual Y′Y' interior over X′X' for the given L/KL/K and X′→XX'\to X. Fix y′∈Y′y'\in Y', and let x′x' be its image. The forward interior criterion gives a proper morphism of their graded reductions. The target reduction is affine by the good-to-affine implication of Theorem [fnd:goodgermiffaffinereduction], since X′X' is good. By properness in the graded birational category its source is the pullback of that affine reduction along the extension of the graded residue fields. This pullback is affine, as in the reverse interior calculation. The affine-to-good implication then supplies an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood of y′y'. Thus Y′Y' is good, and we already proved it boundaryless over X′X'.

Conversely, take L=KL=K and test with each affinoid domain U⊂XU\subset X and its inclusion. This is a good analytic space. Its actual inverse image is good and boundaryless over UU by hypothesis. At every inverse-image point the relative-interior definition over the affinoid target UU gives an affinoid neighbourhood with that point interior. These are the witnesses for every target affinoid in Definition [fnd:alltargetrelativeinterior]. Hence ff is boundaryless.

good. By properness in the graded birational category its
source is the pullback of that affine reduction along the
extension of the graded residue fields. This pullback is
affine, as in the
\hyperref[fnd:nag001808:proper-to-interior]{reverse interior calculation}.
The \hyperref[fnd:nag001982:affine-to-good]{affine-to-good implication}

over \(U\) by hypothesis. At every inverse-image point the

These are the witnesses for every target affinoid in

proof.html:
The identity base change gives the reverse implication. For the forward implication set x=f(y)x=f(y) and F=ℋ(x)F=\mathcal H(x), and assume that ℱy\mathcal F_y is flat over 𝒪X,x\mathcal O_{X,x}. In this proof FF is nontrivially valued. A zero coherent stalk gives zero on an ordinary neighbourhood by finite generation, and then gives zero near all points over yy in each test. We treat nonzero stalks.

Strict fibre and coherent support. Use Proposition [fnd:innerstrictfibrerefinement] to choose ordinary affinoid neighbourhoods of x,yx,y with strict FF-fibre. Proposition [fnd:goodinteriorlocaltesting] preserves innerness on these representatives. Ordinary neighbourhood restriction preserves the stalks at the indicated points, also after pullback in each analytic test. On the source write ℱ=M̃\mathcal F=\widetilde M, for a finite module MM over its affinoid algebra BB, by the finite equivalence in Theorem [fnd:fullgkiehltheoremb]. Let II be its annihilator, and put Z=ℳ(B/I)Z=\mathcal M(B/I). Use the actual quotient norm on B/IB/I, the finite algebra of Theorem [fnd:generalizedfinitealgebras]. If CC is the original affine fibre algebra, then the actual source fibre algebra after the cut is C/ICC/IC, by Theorem [fnd:allpointaffinoidfibres] and Proposition [fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange], applied to the finite quotient after pulling it back to the original fibre. Its norm is equivalent to the finite quotient norm. This is a quotient of a strict FF-affinoid algebra, so it is strict over FF: compose a unit Tate presentation of CC with the closed quotient. The point set of this closed fibre support is the support of the actual pulled-back module by Lemma [fnd:coherentsupportbasechange]. We keep the annihilator quotient, with its scheme structure.

The closed immersion is inner: its affinoid presentation is a quotient with no relative variables. It preserves innerness over the base by the composition inclusion of Proposition [fnd:affinoidinteriorcalculus]. Regard MM as a finite B/IB/I-module. Its coherent sheaf pushes forward to the original one and Theorem [fnd:finitepushforwardflatness] identifies both flatness conditions. Induct on an upper bound nn for the dimension of this strict fibre support. If ordinary neighbourhoods are further restricted, their actual fibre domains cannot increase the support dimension by Corollary [fnd:affinoiddimensiondomaincover].

Projection and the ordinary quotient comparison. Set d=dimZx≤nd=\dim Z_x\leq n. Use Theorem [fnd:strictfibrefiniteprojection] and Lemma [fnd:finiteanalyticbranchseparation] to get a finite map π:Z′→T\pi:Z'\to T on ordinary affinoid neighbourhoods with singleton fibre over t=π(y)t=\pi(y). The target is an affinoid domain of 𝔸Xd,an\mathbb A_X^{d,\mathrm{an}}, with tt in its ordinary interior. The relative affine-space projection is smooth by its ordinary-open definition. Thus the actual map T→XT\to X is smooth at tt and tt is inner by Theorem [fnd:goodsmoothquasismoothinterior]. The projection is quasi-smooth throughout TT, by the same theorem on affine space and the domain restriction criterion of Theorem [fnd:jacobiansmoothdomainbasechange]. Still at the same tt, use Proposition [fnd:innerstrictfibrerefinement] to take a stricter fibre representative. The actual fibre is an affinoid domain of 𝔸Fd,an\mathbb A_F^{d,\mathrm{an}}. Use Theorem [fnd:affinespacedomainregular] and Lemma [fnd:regularaffinoidcomponents] on that fibre and Lemma [fnd:originalfiberidempotentcut] to retain its integral factor through tt by an ordinary restriction over KK. Pull the finite map back at each restriction. The FF-fibre of the resulting TT has a nonzero integral strict algebra CTC_T with dimCT≤d\dim C_T\leq d by Lemma [fnd:affinespacedomaindimensionbound].

The singleton formula of Theorem [fnd:finitepushforwardflatness] makes NtN_t flat over R=𝒪X,xR=\mathcal O_{X,x}, for N=π*(ℱ|Z′)N=\pi_*(\mathcal F|_{Z'}). Use Lemma [fnd:originalgenericbasisdimensiondrop] on the actual finite module over the algebra of TT. From its original generators choose u:L=𝒪Tr→Nu:L=\mathcal O_T^r\to N with analytic-fibre map injective and ordinarily dense bijectivity locus on TxT_x. Its cokernel QQ has fibre support of dimension at most dimCT−1\dim C_T-1 when nonempty, and zero fibre when dimCT=0\dim C_T=0. The finite coherent presentation computes the fibre map by tensoring with the actual analytic fibre stalk.

Put S=𝒪T,tS=\mathcal O_{T,t} and 𝔪=𝔪R\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R. At this inner chart, Corollary [fnd:generalclosedfiberfaithfulflat] gives faithful flatness of S/𝔪S→𝒪Tx,tS/\mathfrak mS\to\mathcal O_{T_x,t}. It applies to the same T→XT\to X, with both spaces good, and compares the ordinary quotient with the actual analytic fibre. Equivalently, at this free-source application it suffices that a vector in (S/𝔪S)r(S/\mathfrak mS)^r which vanishes in 𝒪Tx,tr\mathcal O_{T_x,t}^{\,r} was zero. The injective analytic-fibre map therefore gives injectivity of utmod𝔪u_t\bmod\mathfrak m. Use Lemma [fnd:generalinnerflatcokernel], with the inner tt, NtN_t flat over RR and the actual injective analytic-fibre map, to obtain utu_t injective and QtQ_t flat over RR. The lemma supplies the local flatness step on the actual coherent modules.

Dimension drop and all analytic tests. If the fibre of QQ is zero at tt, the support formula of Lemma [fnd:coherentsupportbasechange] gives Qt=0Q_t=0. This includes the case n=0n=0. If Qt≠0Q_t\ne0, pass to its closed annihilator support on TT. Its actual fibre quotient is strict as above. To see its dimension bound, at any prime of CTC_T its residue field extends the residue field of the contracted prime of the algebra of TT. By the residue-vector-space argument of Lemma [fnd:coherentsupportbasechange], the pulled-back finite module is supported at the prime exactly when the contracted prime contains the original annihilator. Thus the fibre annihilator and the extended original annihilator have the same radical, which gives the bound n−1n-1. The closed support is inner at tt, and the finite pushforward equivalence preserves naive and analytic flatness. Apply induction there. In either case QQ is analytically XX-flat at tt. Here LL is finite free, T→XT\to X is quasi-smooth, and tt is in the ordinary closure of the fibre bijectivity locus. It tests all points over tt in each good analytic base change over every complete extension. In these tests the free source remains flat over the new base, since the quasi-smooth projection is analytically flat by Theorem [fnd:jacobianflatregularcriterion]. The pulled-back cokernel is the cokernel of the pulled-back map. Thus NN is analytically flat, and the finite pushforward equivalence gives the conclusion for ℱ\mathcal F at yy.

\(\pi:Z'\to T\) on ordinary affinoid neighbourhoods with singleton
fibre over \(t=\pi(y)\). The target is an affinoid domain of
\(\mathbb A_X^{d,\mathrm{an}}\), with \(t\) in its ordinary interior.
The relative affine-space projection is smooth by its ordinary-open
definition. Thus the actual map \(T\to X\) is smooth at \(t\)
and \(t\) is inner by Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodsmoothquasismoothinterior}.
The projection is quasi-smooth throughout \(T\), by the same theorem
on affine space and the domain restriction criterion
of Theorem~\ref{fnd:jacobiansmoothdomainbasechange}.
Still at the same \(t\), use Proposition~\ref{fnd:innerstrictfibrerefinement}
to take a stricter fibre representative. The actual fibre is an
affinoid domain of \(\mathbb A_F^{d,\mathrm{an}}\).
Use Theorem~\ref{fnd:affinespacedomainregular} and
Lemma~\ref{fnd:regularaffinoidcomponents} on that fibre and
Lemma~\ref{fnd:originalfiberidempotentcut} to retain its integral
factor through \(t\) by an ordinary restriction over \(K\).
Pull the finite map back at each restriction. The \(F\)-fibre
of the resulting \(T\) has a nonzero integral strict algebra \(C_T\)
with \(\dim C_T\leq d\) by
Lemma~\ref{fnd:affinespacedomaindimensionbound}.

The singleton formula of Theorem~\ref{fnd:finitepushforwardflatness}
makes \(N_t\) flat over \(R=\mathcal O_{X,x}\), for
\(N=\pi_*(\mathcal F|_{Z'})\). Use
Lemma~\ref{fnd:originalgenericbasisdimensiondrop} on the actual
finite module over the algebra of \(T\). From its original
generators choose \(u:L=\mathcal O_T^r\to N\) with analytic-fibre
map injective and ordinarily dense bijectivity locus on \(T_x\).
Its cokernel \(Q\) has fibre support of dimension at most
\(\dim C_T-1\) when nonempty, and zero fibre when \(\dim C_T=0\).
The finite coherent presentation computes the fibre map by
tensoring with the actual analytic fibre stalk.

Put \(S=\mathcal O_{T,t}\) and \(\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_R\).
At this inner chart, Corollary~\ref{fnd:generalclosedfiberfaithfulflat}
gives faithful flatness of \(S/\mathfrak mS\to\mathcal O_{T_x,t}\).
It applies to the same \(T\to X\), with both spaces good, and
compares the ordinary quotient with the actual analytic fibre.
Equivalently, at this free-source application it suffices that a
vector in \((S/\mathfrak mS)^r\) which vanishes in
\(\mathcal O_{T_x,t}^{\,r}\) was zero. The injective analytic-fibre
map therefore gives injectivity of \(u_t\bmod\mathfrak m\).
Use Lemma~\ref{fnd:generalinnerflatcokernel}, with the inner \(t\),
\(N_t\) flat over \(R\) and the actual injective analytic-fibre
map, to obtain \(u_t\) injective and \(Q_t\) flat over \(R\).
The lemma supplies the local flatness step on the actual coherent
modules.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Dimension drop and all analytic tests.}
If the fibre of \(Q\) is zero at \(t\), the support formula
of Lemma~\ref{fnd:coherentsupportbasechange} gives \(Q_t=0\).
This includes the case \(n=0\). If \(Q_t\ne0\), pass to its
closed annihilator support on \(T\). Its actual fibre quotient is
strict as above. To see its dimension bound, at any prime of \(C_T\)
its residue field extends the residue field of the contracted prime
of the algebra of \(T\). By the residue-vector-space argument of
Lemma~\ref{fnd:coherentsupportbasechange}, the pulled-back finite
module is supported at the prime exactly when the contracted prime
contains the original annihilator. Thus the fibre annihilator and
the extended original annihilator have the same radical, which gives
the bound \(n-1\). The closed support is inner at \(t\), and the
finite pushforward equivalence preserves naive and analytic flatness. Apply induction there. In either case \(Q\) is
analytically \(X\)-flat at \(t\).
Here \(L\) is finite free, \(T\to X\) is quasi-smooth, and \(t\)
is in the ordinary closure of the fibre bijectivity locus.
Apply the cokernel-to-target implication of
Corollary~\ref{fnd:genericfibreflatcokernel}, with the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:genericfibreuniversalinjectivity}. It tests all
points over \(t\) in each good analytic base change over every
complete extension. In these tests the free source remains flat
over the new base, since the quasi-smooth projection is analytically
flat by Theorem~\ref{fnd:jacobianflatregularcriterion}.
The pulled-back cokernel is the cokernel of the pulled-back map.
Thus \(N\) is analytically flat, and the finite pushforward
equivalence gives the conclusion for \(\mathcal F\) at \(y\).
\end{proof}

erratum.html:
NAG-001944. Admissibility of the generic atlas.

The unrestricted gluing assertion of the historical proposition fails in the category of strict analytic GG-spaces used here. Ordinary formal affine opens can glue even when their prescribed generic affinoids fail the admissibility condition.

Take a complete discretely valued field KK, with uniformizer π\pi and residue field kk. Glue countably many copies 𝔛i=SpfK∘⟨T⟩\mathfrak X_i=\operatorname{Spf}K^\circ\langle T\rangle by identifying their principal formal opens D(T¯)D(\overline T) via the identity on the common completed localization. These maps satisfy the cocycle identity. On an open of the quotient, take chart sections that agree on the common open. This glues the locally ringed spaces to an admissible formal scheme 𝔛\mathfrak X because its charts are the original topologically finitely presented, π\pi-torsion-free affines.

Every nonempty formal open contains the common residual generic point. Its intersection with at least one residual affine line is a nonempty open in that line. Thus a finite-incidence open cover would have only finitely many nonempty members. Each quasi-compact formal open is covered by finitely many of its intersections with the original charts. The origin of each chart belongs to that chart alone, so finitely many quasi-compact formal opens cannot cover all the origins.

By the principal-open calculation, the common overlap of the prescribed generic discs is S={|T|=1}S=\{|T|=1\}. In each disc the Gauss points of real radii 0<r<10<r<1 tend to the unit Gauss point ξ\xi as r↑1r\uparrow 1. For a Tate series ∑nanTn\sum_n a_nT^n the radius-rr evaluation is maxn|an|rn\max_n |a_n|r^n. A coefficient attaining the radius-one maximum gives a lower bound tending to that maximum, which is also an upper bound. Thus continuity of each prescribed chart inclusion implies that every neighbourhood of the shared ξ\xi meets {|T|<1}\{|T|<1\} in every disc. Points in these private parts of different discs remain distinct because the identifications are exactly along SS. A finite family of the discs therefore cannot contain a neighbourhood of ξ\xi. Any quasi-compact formal affine used in a refinement is covered by finitely many original formal charts. Under the required specialization trace identity its generic affinoid lies in the union of their generic discs. A finite family of such refinements still cannot contain a neighbourhood of ξ\xi. The prescribed generic cover fails the quasi-net condition.

Valid scopes. Under the standing nontrivial valuation, a principal formal open has generic trace {|f|=1}\{|f|=1\} with its actual rational affinoid algebra and flat restriction, as proved in the principal-open proposition. The affine formal topology is Noetherian, and intersections of quasi-compact formal opens are quasi-compact. See the formal-topology paragraph of the historical proof, starting with the radical equality for πA0\pi A_0 and K∘∘A0K^{\circ\circ}A_0.

An admissible formal scheme with an ordinary open cover by quasi-compact opens, each meeting only finitely many of the others, has a canonical quasi-separated, quasi-paracompact strict analytic generic fibre. The construction is functorial for formal arrows between such schemes. Specialization is natural and surjective. The generic fibre of a formal open identifies with its specialization inverse image as an analytic domain, with its restricted charts and bounded restriction maps. See the full finite-incidence proof. On an actual supplied formal-affine generic atlas these inverse images detect equality, coverage and disjointness of formal opens and preserve intersections, by the supplied-atlas trace proof. For two given formal arrows with actual compatible generic charts, equality of their generic maps implies equality of the formal arrows, by the supplied-arrow proof.

NAG-001945. Formal blowups and generic comparison.

In the formal-disc example, put (π,T)(\pi,T) on one chart and the unit ideal on every other chart. They agree on the common open, where TT is a unit. On the chosen chart, πa+Tb=0\pi a+Tb=0 implies b=πcb=\pi c by reduction modulo π\pi, since TT is a nonzerodivisor in k[T]k[T]. Cancelling π\pi then gives a=−Tca=-Tc. The two generators thus have the finite presentation with relation (−T,π)(-T,\pi). The same argument applies on principal restrictions: the reduction is the corresponding localization of k[T]k[T] and the formal ring is π\pi-torsion-free. The glued ideal is coherent and contains π\pi, so is open. The formal blowup exists. The generic-isomorphism assertion of the historical lemma requires a generic realization of the base, which fails in this example. This is an obstruction to existence of the generic comparison on arbitrary formal schemes. The comparison between actual compatible realizations remains valid.

Valid scopes. For a coherent open ideal on an admissible formal scheme, the formal admissible blowup exists, commutes with restriction to formal opens, and has the invertible-ideal universal property. The blowup of a finite product of coherent open ideals makes the factors invertible and dominates each individual blowup. For a formal arrow, blowing up the pulled-back centre dominates the target blowup over the target. See the formal gluing and product paragraphs of the historical proof. For such a blowup b:𝔛′→𝔛b:\mathfrak X'\to\mathfrak X, assume actual compatible formal-affine generic atlases for source and target, including the affine blowup charts and their principal refinements. Then bηb_\eta is an isomorphism of the realized analytic GG-spaces. The full bounded-overlap and inverse-map argument is the supplied-atlas comparison proof.

\begin{proposition}[Formalizing a finite-type analytic covering]
\label{fnd:nag001947:whole-original}
Let $\mathfrak X$ be quasi-paracompact and admissible,

\begin{theorem}[Lifting a global analytic morphism]
\label{fnd:nag001948:whole-original}
Let $\mathfrak X,\mathfrak Y$ be quasi-paracompact
admissible formal schemes. Every analytic morphism
$f:\mathfrak X_\eta\to\mathfrak Y_\eta$ lifts to a formal
morphism $f':\mathfrak X'\to\mathfrak Y$ after a finite
composition $s:\mathfrak X'\to\mathfrak X$ of admissible
blowups, with $f'_\eta=f\circ s_\eta$. Two stages suffice.
\end{theorem}

proof.html:
Suppose first that the given map is finite and admissible. Choose a single finite iterated Gauss tower L/KL/K for the actual pair A,BA,B by Lemma [fnd:spectralvaluenormalizinggauss]. The field LL is nontrivially valued, the two extended algebras are strict, and all the supported degrees of both their graded reductions lie in |L×||L^\times|. Lemma [fnd:gaussfiniteadmissibledescent] ascends the bounded lifts of a finite AA-module presentation on the actual scalar extension. Thus AL→BLA_L\to B_L is finite, and Theorem [fnd:strictcanonicalfinitecriterion] gives a finite map of canonical reductions. For either upper algebra E=AL,BLE=A_L,B_L, the affinoid spectral formula (Corollary [fnd:generalizedspectralradiusformula]) and the power bound at radius 11 in Theorem [fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound] identify the power-bounded elements with ρE≤1\rho_E\leq1. For ρE(e)<1\rho_E(e)<1, the same bound at a positive ss with ρE(e)<s<1\rho_E(e)<s<1 gives en→0e^n\to0. Conversely, if en→0e^n\to0, some power has norm less than 11, which by the spectral formula implies ρE(e)<1\rho_E(e)<1. Thus the canonical reduction is exactly the degree-one spectral quotient E≤1/E<1E_{\leq1}/E_{<1}. Lemma [fnd:gradedscalardescent] then gives finiteness of the full upper graded map: every supported degree is normalized by a homogeneous unit of $\widetilde L^{\rm gr}$. By Theorem [fnd:generalgaussgradedbasechange] the map is the scalar extension of the original graded map. The identification commutes with the given bounded map, since it sends a homogeneous scalar times a representative to the class of the same product upstairs. Finite module generation descends by Lemma [fnd:gradedscalardescent], by collecting the finitely many original entries of the upper generators and testing the quotient by faithful graded scalar extension. This proves the forward implication for the actual weighted source and target.

Suppose now that the graded map is finite. Fix an admissible absolute weighted Tate presentation Q=K{r−1T}↠AQ=K\{r^{-1}T\}\twoheadrightarrow A. The fixed absolute presentation result gives finiteness of $\widetilde A^{\rm gr}$ over the graded image of QQ. Finiteness is transitive for these modules, after taking their images in $\widetilde B^{\rm gr}$. Hence $\widetilde B^{\rm gr}$ is finite over the graded image of QQ. Apply the absolute reverse finite-admissibility result to the actual composite Q→A→BQ\to A\to B. It gives finitely many bi∈Bb_i\in B and a constant CC such that every b∈Bb\in B can be written b=∑iqibib=\sum_i q_i b_i with maxi∥qi∥Q≤C∥b∥B\max_i\|q_i\|_Q\le C\|b\|_B. Send the coefficients through the bounded map Q→AQ\to A. The same generators and a uniform coefficient bound now give finite admissibility over the actual AA. This supplies the Banach lifting condition in the reverse implication.

Finally the fixed absolute presentation result gives $\widetilde A^{\rm gr}$ finite over the image of the weighted polynomial source $\widetilde Q^{\rm gr}=\widetilde K^{\rm gr}[t_1,\ldots,t_m]$, where deg(ti)=ri\deg(t_i)=r_i. Its finite module generators together with the images of the polynomial variables generate it as a graded algebra over $\widetilde K^{\rm gr}$. Zero algebras give the same conclusions directly.
proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Suppose first that the given map is finite and admissible.
Choose a single finite iterated Gauss tower \(L/K\) for
the actual pair \(A,B\) by
Lemma~\ref{fnd:spectralvaluenormalizinggauss}. The field
\(L\) is nontrivially valued, the two extended algebras
are strict, and all the supported degrees of both their
graded reductions lie in \(|L^\times|\).
Lemma~\ref{fnd:gaussfiniteadmissibledescent} ascends the
bounded lifts of a finite \(A\)-module presentation on
the actual scalar extension. Thus \(A_L\to B_L\) is
finite, and Theorem~\ref{fnd:strictcanonicalfinitecriterion}
gives a finite map of canonical reductions. For either
upper algebra \(E=A_L,B_L\), the affinoid spectral formula
(Corollary~\ref{fnd:generalizedspectralradiusformula}) and
the power bound at radius \(1\) in
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound} identify
the power-bounded elements with \(\rho_E\leq1\).
For \(\rho_E(e)<1\), the same bound at a positive
\(s\) with \(\rho_E(e)<s<1\) gives \(e^n\to0\).
Conversely, if \(e^n\to0\), some power has norm less than
\(1\), which by the spectral formula implies \(\rho_E(e)<1\).
Thus the canonical reduction is exactly the degree-one
spectral quotient \(E_{\leq1}/E_{<1}\).
Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedscalardescent} then gives finiteness
of the full upper graded map: every supported degree is
normalized by a homogeneous unit of
\(\widetilde L^{\rm gr}\). By
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalgaussgradedbasechange} the map is
the scalar extension of the original graded map. The
identification commutes with the given bounded map,
since it sends a homogeneous scalar times a representative
to the class of the same product upstairs. Finite module
generation descends by Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedscalardescent},
by collecting the finitely many original entries of the
upper generators and testing the quotient by faithful
graded scalar extension. This proves the forward implication
for the actual weighted source and target.

Suppose now that the graded map is finite. Fix an
admissible absolute weighted Tate presentation
\(Q=K\{r^{-1}T\}\twoheadrightarrow A\). The
\hyperref[fnd:gradedfixedabsolutepresentation]{fixed absolute presentation result}
gives finiteness of \(\widetilde A^{\rm gr}\) over
the graded image of \(Q\). Finiteness is transitive for
these modules, after taking their images in
\(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\).
Hence \(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\) is finite over the
graded image of \(Q\). Apply the
\hyperref[fnd:gradedabsolutereversefinite]{absolute reverse finite-admissibility result}
to the actual composite \(Q\to A\to B\).
It gives finitely many \(b_i\in B\) and a constant \(C\)
such that every \(b\in B\) can be written
\(b=\sum_i q_i b_i\) with \(\max_i\|q_i\|_Q\le C\|b\|_B\).
Send the coefficients through the bounded map \(Q\to A\).
The same generators and a uniform coefficient bound now
give finite admissibility over the actual \(A\). This
supplies the Banach lifting condition in the reverse implication.

Finally the
\hyperref[fnd:gradedfixedabsolutepresentation]{fixed absolute presentation result}
gives \(\widetilde A^{\rm gr}\) finite over the image of
the weighted polynomial source
\(\widetilde Q^{\rm gr}=\widetilde K^{\rm gr}[t_1,\ldots,t_m]\),
where \(\deg(t_i)=r_i\). Its finite module generators
together with the images of the polynomial variables generate
it as a graded algebra over
\(\widetilde K^{\rm gr}\). Zero algebras give the same
conclusions directly.
\end{proof}

NAG-001959.scope: Original generalized finite-and-admissible equivalence and graded finite algebra-generation corollary.

statement.html: A bounded homomorphism A→BA\to B of generalized affinoid algebras is finite and admissible if and only if $$\widetilde A^{\rm gr}\longrightarrow\widetilde B^{\rm gr}$$ is finite. In particular $\widetilde A^{\rm gr}$ is a finitely generated graded $\widetilde K^{\rm gr}$-algebra.

NAG-001959.title: The general graded finite-map criterion

For the commutative Banach algebra DD use the spectral radius filtration, with ρD(z)=limm∥zm∥1/m\rho_D(z)=\lim_m\|z^m\|^{1/m}. It is ultrametric: for any ss strictly above the two spectral radii of x,yx,y, bound their powers by CxsmC_xs^m and CysmC_ys^m. The binomial expansion gives ∥(x+y)m∥≤CxCysm\|(x+y)^m\|\le C_x C_y s^m. Products are bounded by multiplying powers, using commutativity. Taking roots proves the seminorm inequalities. Bounded homomorphisms decrease spectral radii by applying their fixed bound to powers and taking roots. In particular the maps A→B→DA\to B\to D induce the stated graded maps, with no point-evaluation assumption. Write RA,RBR_A,R_B for their images in $\widetilde D^{\rm gr}$.

For a series ∑νaνTν\sum_\nu a_\nu T^\nu in a relative presentation at radii ss, lift each aνa_\nu to pν∈Pp_\nu\in P with ∥pν∥≤M∥aν∥\|p_\nu\|\leq M\|a_\nu\|, taking zero for a zero coefficient. Conversely assume RBR_B is finite over RAR_A, and take relative coordinates bjb_j for BB. By Lemma [fnd:spectralgeneratorradii], shrink each radius to sj=ρB(bj)s_j=\rho_B(b_j) if this is positive and to a positive radius at most the original one otherwise. Write βj\beta_j for the initial class in that degree. The image of βj\beta_j is integral over RAR_A by the determinant trick for a finite algebra. The positive power bounds of Theorem [fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound] in BB give the bounded substitution C=A{t−1U}→BC=A\{t^{-1}U\}\to B, Uj↦wjU_j\mapsto w_j. In $\widetilde B^{\rm gr}$ each βj\beta_j satisfies the monic equation obtained by subtracting the initial class of wjw_j in degree tjt_j from p¯j(βj)\overline p_j(\beta_j). The coefficients belong to the graded image of CC. The finiteness for the shrunk relative presentation just proved, together with these monic equations, makes $\widetilde B^{\rm gr}$ finite over the graded image of CC.

For the absolute presentation Q=P{t−1U}↠CQ=P\{t^{-1}U\}\twoheadrightarrow C, lift the coefficients of each series in C=A{t−1U}C=A\{t^{-1}U\} through P→AP\to A with the same bound MM. The weights tνt^\nu give decay of the lifted coefficients and the uniform weighted-supremum bound for this second map. By the fixed absolute presentation result, $\widetilde C^{\rm gr}$ is finite over the graded image of QQ; transitivity makes $\widetilde B^{\rm gr}$ finite over the image of QQ. Apply absolute reverse finite admissibility to the actual composite Q→BQ\to B. Take its finite module generators viv_i with uniformly bounded coefficient lifts. The bounded map Q→CQ\to C gives the same property over CC for those viv_i. Choose ui>ρB(vi)u_i>\rho_B(v_i). The positive-radius power bound of Theorem [fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound] in BB at uiu_i makes the substitution C{u−1V}→BC\{u^{-1}V\}\to B bounded; the linear polynomials in ViV_i with these bounded lifts are a uniformly bounded right lifting of elements of BB in the sense of norm admissibility. proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
For the commutative Banach algebra \(D\) use the spectral
radius filtration, with \(\rho_D(z)=\lim_m\|z^m\|^{1/m}\).
It is ultrametric: for any \(s\) strictly above the two
spectral radii of \(x,y\), bound their powers by \(C_xs^m\)
and \(C_ys^m\). The binomial expansion gives
\(\|(x+y)^m\|\le C_x C_y s^m\). Products are bounded by
multiplying powers, using commutativity. Taking roots
proves the seminorm inequalities. Bounded homomorphisms
decrease spectral radii by applying their fixed bound
to powers and taking roots. In particular the maps
\(A\to B\to D\) induce the stated graded maps, with no
point-evaluation assumption. Write \(R_A,R_B\) for their
images in \(\widetilde D^{\rm gr}\).

Fix an admissible absolute presentation \(P\twoheadrightarrow A\)
over \(K\), with a uniform lift bound \(M\). For a series
\(\sum_\nu a_\nu T^\nu\) in a relative presentation at radii \(s\),
lift each \(a_\nu\) to \(p_\nu\in P\) with
\(\|p_\nu\|\leq M\|a_\nu\|\), taking zero for a zero coefficient.
Then \(\|p_\nu\|s^\nu\to0\), and the lifted series has weighted
supremum at most \(M\) times the original weighted supremum.
Composing this coefficientwise lift with the lifts for the
given admissible relative presentation
\(A\{s^{-1}T\}\twoheadrightarrow B\) gives the admissible
absolute presentation \(P\{s^{-1}T\}\twoheadrightarrow B\).
The \hyperref[fnd:gradedfixedabsolutepresentation]{fixed absolute presentation result}
makes \(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\) finite over the image of its
graded polynomial source. An initial class of a coefficient
coordinate of \(P\) that survives at its assigned degree in
\(B\) already survives at that degree in \(A\), by spectral
contraction. Its image therefore lies in the image of
\(\widetilde A^{\rm gr}\). Thus
\(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\) is finite over the algebra generated
by that image and the degree-\(s_j\) initial classes of the
relative coordinates. If the relative presentation is inner,
all the latter classes map to zero in
\(\widetilde D^{\rm gr}\). The images of the finite generators
then generate \(R_B\) over \(R_A\).

Conversely assume \(R_B\) is finite over \(R_A\), and take
relative coordinates \(b_j\) for \(B\). By
Lemma~\ref{fnd:spectralgeneratorradii}, shrink each radius
to \(s_j=\rho_B(b_j)\) if this is positive and to a positive
radius at most the original one otherwise. Write \(\beta_j\)
for the initial class in that degree. The image of \(\beta_j\)
is integral over \(R_A\) by the determinant trick for a
finite algebra. Taking the homogeneous component of a monic
equation of degree \(s_j^{d_j}\) gives coefficients of degree
\(s_j^i\) for the terms of exponent \(d_j-i\). Lift these
coefficients to \(a_{ji}\in A\) with
\(\rho_A(a_{ji})\leq s_j^i\). Use the linear monic equation if
the evaluated class is zero. Set
\[
 p_j(Z)=Z^{d_j}+\sum_{i=1}^{d_j}a_{ji}Z^{d_j-i},\qquad
 w_j=p_j(b_j),\qquad t_j=s_j^{d_j}.
\]
The two filtrations give \(\rho_B(w_j)\le t_j\) and
\(\rho_D(\varphi(w_j))<t_j\): in the latter the relation
vanishes in degree \(t_j\). The positive power bounds of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound} in \(B\)
give the bounded substitution \(C=A\{t^{-1}U\}\to B\),
\(U_j\mapsto w_j\). In \(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\) each
\(\beta_j\) satisfies the monic equation obtained by
subtracting the initial class of \(w_j\) in degree \(t_j\)
from \(\overline p_j(\beta_j)\). The coefficients belong to
the graded image of \(C\). The finiteness for the shrunk
relative presentation just proved, together with these
monic equations, makes \(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\) finite over
the graded image of \(C\).

For the absolute presentation \(Q=P\{t^{-1}U\}\twoheadrightarrow C\),
lift the coefficients of each series in \(C=A\{t^{-1}U\}\)
through \(P\to A\) with the same bound \(M\). The weights
\(t^\nu\) give decay of the lifted coefficients and the
uniform weighted-supremum bound for this second map. By the
\hyperref[fnd:gradedfixedabsolutepresentation]{fixed absolute presentation result},
\(\widetilde C^{\rm gr}\) is finite over the graded image of
\(Q\); transitivity makes \(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\) finite over
the image of \(Q\). Apply
\hyperref[fnd:gradedabsolutereversefinite]{absolute reverse finite admissibility}
to the actual composite \(Q\to B\).
Take its finite module generators \(v_i\) with uniformly
bounded coefficient lifts. The bounded map \(Q\to C\) gives
the same property over \(C\) for those \(v_i\). Choose
\(u_i>\rho_B(v_i)\). The positive-radius power bound of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound} in \(B\) at
\(u_i\) makes the substitution \(C\{u^{-1}V\}\to B\)
bounded; the linear polynomials in \(V_i\)
with these bounded lifts are a uniformly bounded right
lifting of elements of \(B\) in the sense of norm
admissibility. The two successive weighted series algebras form the joint
weighted series algebra over \(A\), by the product weights
and the coefficient decay condition. The resulting relative
presentation has coordinates \(w_j,v_i\), with spectral radii in \(D\)
strictly below \(t_j,u_i\), respectively. It is inner, as claimed.
\end{proof}

NAG-001962.scope: Original relative innerness equivalence with arbitrary commutative Banach target and the actual admissible relative presentation.

statement.html: Let AA be affinoid, let BB be an AA-affinoid algebra, and let φ:B→D\varphi:B\to D be a bounded AA-homomorphism to a commutative Banach AA-algebra. Call φ\varphi inner over AA if some admissible surjection A{r−1T}↠BA\{r^{-1}T\}\twoheadrightarrow B has ρD(φ(Ti))<ri\rho_D(\varphi(T_i))<r_i for every coordinate. Then φ\varphi is inner over AA if and only if $$\operatorname{im}(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\to\widetilde D^{\rm gr}) \quad\hbox{is finite over}\quad \operatorname{im}(\widetilde A^{\rm gr}\to\widetilde D^{\rm gr}).$$
statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[The graded innerness criterion]
\label{fnd:gradedinnernesscriterion}
Let $A$ be affinoid, let $B$ be an $A$-affinoid algebra,
and let $\varphi:B\to D$ be a bounded $A$-homomorphism to a
commutative Banach $A$-algebra. Call $\varphi$ inner over $A$
if some admissible surjection $A\{r^{-1}T\}\twoheadrightarrow B$
has $\rho_D(\varphi(T_i))<r_i$ for every coordinate.
Then $\varphi$ is inner over $A$ if and only if
\[
 \operatorname{im}(\widetilde B^{\rm gr}\to\widetilde D^{\rm gr})
 \quad\hbox{is finite over}\quad
 \operatorname{im}(\widetilde A^{\rm gr}\to\widetilde D^{\rm gr}).
\]
\end{theorem}

These cuts contain all of WW, because the original vj,uiv_j,u_i have the stated spectral bounds there; they are neighbourhoods of xx because the values at xx are strictly smaller than the bounds. Thus the overlap and its exact Weierstrass descriptions are unchanged. The two presentations now have coordinate lists (f1,…,fm,u1,…,ul,v′1,…,v′h),(g1,…,gm,u′1,…,u′l,v1,…,vh).(f_1,\ldots,f_m,u_1,\ldots,u_l,v'_1,\ldots,v'_h),\qquad (g_1,\ldots,g_m,u'_1,\ldots,u'_l,v_1,\ldots,v_h). Use radii (ri,ai,bj)(r_i,a_i,b_j) for these lists and p<t<qp<t<q for the annulus coordinate. Appending the cut coordinates can only decrease the induced quotient norm on AA, since every old lift is still a permitted lift of the same norm. Hence all strict difference estimates above remain valid in the new, actual overlap quotient norm. These are exactly the hypotheses of Theorem [fnd:doublelaurentaffinoidgluing].
proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Set $t=\deg(\lambda)$ and write
$\mathscr R(X,x)=\mathscr P(F_x)\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m\}$,
with homogeneous nonzero $\alpha_i$ of degree $r_i$.
All shrinkings below are neighbourhood shrinkings inside
$Y$ and $Z$. Their union remains a neighbourhood in $X$:
the two domains form a finite closed cover of a compact
neighbourhood, and this is the quasi-net topology criterion
of Lemma~\ref{fnd:nettopologyboundedgluing}.

\emph{Step 1: an exact common annular overlap.}
Lift $\lambda$ to invertible functions $f$ on a neighbourhood
in $Y$ and $g$ on a neighbourhood in $Z$.
The cut $|f|\le t$ in $Y$ has the same reduction as $Y$,
and $|g^{-1}|\le t^{-1}$ in $Z$ has the same reduction as
$Z$. By Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodgermdomainclassification}
these cuts are neighbourhoods of $x$.
Choose affinoid neighbourhoods inside them, so
\[
           \rho_B(f)\le t,\qquad \rho_C(g^{-1})\le t^{-1}.
\]
Their intersection $W$ is affinoid by
Lemma~\ref{fnd:separatedaffinoidintersections}.
At $x$ we have $|(f-g)(x)|<t$. Shrink the two neighbourhoods
so that $\rho_W(f-g)<t$; continuity on the old intersection,
and the relative-open-set definition, permit one common
shrinking. Thus on $W$ one has $|f|=|g|=t$, and
\[
 W\subset Y\{|f|\ge t\},\qquad W\subset Z\{|g|\le t\}.
\]
The three domain germs in this display have reduction
$\mathscr R(X,x)\{\lambda,\lambda^{-1}\}$.
The domain classification gives affinoid neighbourhoods
$Y'\subset Y$, $Z'\subset Z$ with
\[
 Y'\cap Z=Y'\{|f|\ge t\},\qquad
 Y\cap Z'=Z'\{|g|\le t\}.
\]
Choose a strict Laurent neighbourhood $W'$ of $x$
inside $Y'\cap Z'$ in the old affinoid $W$.
Write it using finitely many conditions
$|u_i|\le a_i$ and $|v_j|\ge b_j$, strict at $x$.
The first displayed overlap is a Weierstrass domain of
$Y'$ (its defining function is the analytic function $f^{-1}$),
and the second is a Weierstrass domain of $Z'$.
Restriction to a Weierstrass domain has dense image:
truncate its Tate series in the adjoined functions, which
are already functions on the source.
Approximate $u_i,v_j$ from each side, with errors respectively
less than $a_i,b_j$ on that overlap.
The non-Archimedean inequality makes the resulting cuts
have exactly $W'$ as their intersections with the old
overlap. They are neighbourhoods of $x$ because the
inequalities there are strict. Replacing $Y,Z,W$ by these
two cuts and $W'$ gives the exact identities
\[
 W=Y\{|f|\ge t\}=Z\{|g|\le t\},\qquad
 A=B\{t f^{-1}\}=C\{t^{-1}g\}.
\]

\emph{Step 2: presentations with small extra coordinates.}
Lift each $\alpha_i$ to an invertible analytic function
$f_i$ near $x$ in $Y$, and impose $|f_i|\le r_i$.
Every such cut has full reduction in $Y$, since every
valuation of $\mathscr R(Y,x)$ contains $\alpha_i$.
It is therefore a neighbourhood. Perform the first step
again if needed to retain the exact overlap identities.
Choose $p<t$ with $\rho_B(f^{-1})<p^{-1}$, and set
\[
       D_B=K\{r_1^{-1}T_1,\ldots,r_m^{-1}T_m,
                                    t^{-1}S,pS^{-1}\}.
\]
Send $T_i$ to $f_i$ and $S$ to $f$. The Weierstrass cuts
give power bounds at $r_i,t$, and the strict inequality for
$f^{-1}$ gives the power bound at $p^{-1}$ by
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound}.
Thus $D_B\to B$ is bounded. Evaluate both graded reductions
in $F_x$ and write their images as $R_{D_B}$ and $R_B$.
The exact initials give
$\widetilde K^{\rm gr}[\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m,\lambda]
 \subset R_{D_B}\subset R_B$.
The \hyperref[fnd:gradedfixedabsolutepresentation]{fixed absolute}
presentation result applied to a weighted Tate quotient presenting
the actual $B$ makes $R_B$ finitely generated over $\widetilde K^{\rm gr}$.
Its valuation set is $\mathscr R(Y,x)$, so
Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedvaluationintegrality} gives finiteness over
the displayed coordinate subalgebra, hence over $R_{D_B}$.
The reverse \hyperref[fnd:gradedrelativepointevaluation]{relative point criterion}
for $D_B\to B$ at $x$ gives an admissible epimorphism
\[
       D_B\{a_1^{-1}U_1,\ldots,a_l^{-1}U_l\}
                  \twoheadrightarrow B,\qquad |u_j(x)|<a_j.
\]
Give $A=B\{t f^{-1}\}$ the quotient norm from the
corresponding boundary presentation in which $|S|=t$.
By density of $C\to A$, choose $g_i,g'\in C$ with
\[
                  \|f_i-g_i\|_A<r_i,\qquad \|f-g'\|_A<t.
\]
On $W$ one has $|g'-g|<t$. Restrict $Z$ to
$|g'-g|\le d<t$, where $d$ is larger than the supremum on
$W$; this cut contains $W$ and is a neighbourhood of it.
Then $|g'|=|g|$ throughout the new $Z$, so $g'$ is invertible,
has inverse bounded by $t^{-1}$, and defines the same
overlap. Replace $g$ by $g'$.
Impose also $|g_i|\le r_i$. These cuts contain $W$ and
are neighbourhoods of $x$, since their reductions are full:
the initial value of $g_i(x)$ is $\alpha_i$.
Choose $q>t$ and $q>\rho_C(g)$. Repeating the relative
innerness argument with
\[
       D_C=K\{r_1^{-1}T_1,\ldots,r_m^{-1}T_m,
                                    q^{-1}S,tS^{-1}\}.
\]
Send $T_i$ to $g_i$ and $S$ to $g$.
The cuts give $\rho_C(g_i)\le r_i$ and $\rho_C(g^{-1})\le t^{-1}$,
and $\rho_C(g)<q$. The positive-radius power bounds of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound} make $D_C\to C$ bounded.
In $F_x$ the two reduced images satisfy
$\widetilde K^{\rm gr}[\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m,\lambda^{-1}]
 \subset R_{D_C}\subset R_C$:
the inverse coordinate gives $\lambda^{-1}$ and the direct coordinate
at radius $q$ evaluates to zero. A weighted Tate quotient for the
actual $C$ and the
\hyperref[fnd:gradedfixedabsolutepresentation]{fixed absolute}
presentation result give finite generation of $R_C$ over
$\widetilde K^{\rm gr}$. Its valuation set is $\mathscr R(Z,x)$,
so Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedvaluationintegrality} gives finiteness over
the displayed subalgebra and then over $R_{D_C}$.
The reverse \hyperref[fnd:gradedrelativepointevaluation]{relative point criterion}
for $D_C\to C$ at $x$ gives an admissible epimorphism
\[
 D_C\{b_1^{-1}V_1,\ldots,b_h^{-1}V_h\}
                  \twoheadrightarrow C,\qquad |v_j(x)|<b_j.
\]

\emph{Step 3: match all coordinates.}
Density of $C\to A$ and $B\to A$ gives elements
$u_i'\in C$, $v_j'\in B$ with
\[
                 \|u_i-u_i'\|_A<a_i,\qquad
                 \|v_j-v_j'\|_A<b_j .
\]
Cut $Y$ by $|v_j'|\le b_j$ and $Z$ by $|u_i'|\le a_i$.
These cuts contain all of $W$, because the original $v_j,u_i$
have the stated spectral bounds there; they are
neighbourhoods of $x$ because the values at $x$ are strictly
smaller than the bounds. Thus the overlap and its exact
Weierstrass descriptions are unchanged.
The two presentations now have coordinate lists
\[
 (f_1,\ldots,f_m,u_1,\ldots,u_l,v'_1,\ldots,v'_h),\qquad
 (g_1,\ldots,g_m,u'_1,\ldots,u'_l,v_1,\ldots,v_h).
\]
Use radii $(r_i,a_i,b_j)$ for these lists and $p<t<q$
for the annulus coordinate. Appending the cut coordinates
can only decrease the induced quotient norm on $A$, since
every old lift is still a permitted lift of the same norm.
Hence all strict difference estimates above remain valid
in the new, actual overlap quotient norm.
These are exactly the hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:doublelaurentaffinoidgluing}.
\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{lemma}[Preparing a two-sided Laurent neighbourhood]
\label{fnd:gradedlaurentpairpreparation}
Suppose a separated germ $(X,x)$ is covered by good
subdomain germs $Y,Z$, and its reduction is affine. Suppose,
for a nonzero homogeneous $\lambda\in F_x$, that
\[
 \mathscr R(Y,x)=\mathscr R(X,x)\{\lambda\},\qquad
 \mathscr R(Z,x)=\mathscr R(X,x)\{\lambda^{-1}\}.
\]
Then one can choose affinoid neighbourhood representatives
$Y=\mathcal M(B)$, $Z=\mathcal M(C)$, whose union is a
neighbourhood of $x$, and elements and radii satisfying every
hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{fnd:doublelaurentaffinoidgluing}.
\end{lemma}

NAG-001981.title: Preparing a two-sided Laurent neighbourhood

proof.html: For the forward implication, apply the affinoid-neighbourhood criterion to the given germ over its complete field. For the reverse implication, apply the affine-to-good clause to the same germ and its affine graded birational reduction.

statement.html: An analytic germ over an arbitrary complete non-Archimedean field is good if and only if its graded birational reduction is affine.

NAG-001982.title: Goodness is detected by graded reduction

proof.html:
Use the strict ordinary chart construction on the given strict germ. This constructs ℛ0(X,x)\mathscr R_0(X,x) over the valuation space of ℋ(x)̃\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)} from the actual finite strict chart refinements. It gives independence of strict charts and ordinary neighbourhood representatives, and identifies ℛ(X,x)\mathscr R(X,x) with the displayed fibre product. The strict subdomain and functoriality proposition gives the nonempty quasi-compact open correspondence, functoriality, and naturality of that fibre product under every morphism of strict germs. In particular the construction and the morphism comparison use the strict chart net of the given analytic spaces.

Lemma [fnd:gradeddegreeonevaluation], applied to the actual graded completed residue field of the germ, identifies the affineness of ℛ0(X,x)\mathscr R_0(X,x) and of its graded pullback. Theorem [fnd:goodgermiffaffinereduction] for the same analytic germ then gives the goodness criterion. Here goodness is the existence of an affinoid ordinary neighbourhood in the analytic germ.

For a strict germ morphism (Y,y)→(X,x)(Y,y)\to(X,x), let G,EG,E be the graded reductions of ℋ(y),ℋ(x)\mathcal H(y),\mathcal H(x), and write G0,E0G_0,E_0 for their degree-one fields. Set PG,PEP_G,P_E equal to the corresponding graded valuation spaces and PG0,PE0P_{G_0},P_{E_0} to their ordinary ones. Write Q0,R0Q_0,R_0 for the ordinary germ reductions of Y,XY,X. Pull the ordinary canonical comparison Q0→R0×PE0PG0Q_0\to R_0\times_{P_{E_0}}P_{G_0} back along PG→PG0P_G\to P_{G_0}. Its target becomes R0×PE0PGR_0\times_{P_{E_0}}P_G. The square of valuation restrictions commutes because contraction along E→GE\to G commutes with taking degree one, so this target is also (R0×PE0PE)×PEPG(R_0\times_{P_{E_0}}P_E)\times_{P_E}P_G. The naturality above therefore identifies the pulled-back map with the graded canonical comparison, including its points on every chart sheet.

For each point of PG0P_{G_0}, choose a lift in PGP_G by Lemma [fnd:gradeddegreeonevaluation]. The ordinary map on that fibre is identified with the graded map on the lifted fibre. Consequently injectivity and bijectivity of the ordinary comparison are equivalent to injectivity and bijectivity of the graded comparison, respectively. These are the two comparison-map conditions for separatedness and properness of birational spaces. Apply Proposition [fnd:gradedgermseparation] for separation. For relative interior use the forward and reverse graded criteria on the same germ morphism, with the all-target-domain definition. This gives both remaining detection equivalences.

\begin{proof}
Use the \hyperref[fnd:ordinarystrictgermreductionconstruction]
{strict ordinary chart construction} on the given strict germ.
This constructs \(\mathscr R_0(X,x)\) over the valuation space of
\(\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)}\) from the actual finite strict chart
refinements. It gives independence of strict charts and ordinary
neighbourhood representatives, and identifies \(\mathscr R(X,x)\)
with the displayed fibre product. The
\hyperref[fnd:nag001985:strict-subdomains-functoriality]
{strict subdomain and functoriality proposition} gives the nonempty
quasi-compact open correspondence, functoriality, and naturality
of that fibre product under every morphism of strict germs. In
particular the construction and the morphism comparison use the
strict chart net of the given analytic spaces.

Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradeddegreeonevaluation}, applied to the actual
graded completed residue field of the germ, identifies the
affineness of \(\mathscr R_0(X,x)\) and of its graded pullback.
Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodgermiffaffinereduction} for the same analytic
germ then gives the goodness criterion. Here goodness is the
existence of an affinoid ordinary neighbourhood in the analytic
germ.

For a strict germ morphism \((Y,y)\to(X,x)\), let \(G,E\)
be the graded reductions of \(\mathcal H(y),\mathcal H(x)\), and
write \(G_0,E_0\) for their degree-one fields. Set \(P_G,P_E\)
equal to the corresponding graded valuation spaces and
\(P_{G_0},P_{E_0}\) to their ordinary ones. Write \(Q_0,R_0\)
for the ordinary germ reductions of \(Y,X\). Pull the ordinary
canonical comparison \(Q_0\to R_0\times_{P_{E_0}}P_{G_0}\)
back along \(P_G\to P_{G_0}\). Its target becomes
\(R_0\times_{P_{E_0}}P_G\). The square of valuation restrictions
commutes because contraction along \(E\to G\) commutes with
taking degree one, so this target is also
\((R_0\times_{P_{E_0}}P_E)\times_{P_E}P_G\).
The naturality above therefore identifies the pulled-back map
with the graded canonical comparison, including its points on
every chart sheet.

For each point of \(P_{G_0}\), choose a lift in \(P_G\) by
Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradeddegreeonevaluation}. The ordinary map on that
fibre is identified with the graded map on the lifted fibre.
Consequently injectivity and bijectivity of the ordinary comparison
are equivalent to injectivity and bijectivity of the graded
comparison, respectively. These are the two comparison-map
conditions for separatedness and properness of birational spaces.
Apply Proposition~\ref{fnd:gradedgermseparation} for separation.
For relative interior use the
\hyperref[fnd:nag001808:interior-to-proper]{forward}
and \hyperref[fnd:nag001808:proper-to-interior]{reverse}
graded criteria on the same germ morphism, with the all-target-domain
