NAG-001985.scope: Canonical ordinary reduction, chart and neighbourhood invariance, strict subdomains, functoriality, graded pullback and all three detection equivalences under the original strict germ hypotheses.

statement.html: For a strictly KK-analytic germ, with KK nontrivially valued, there is a canonical ordinary birational reduction ℛ0(X,x)\mathscr R_0(X,x) with field ℋ(x)̃\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)}. It is functorial and independent of strict affinoid charts and neighbourhoods. Its nonempty quasi-compact open subspaces classify strict subdomain germs. It is related to the graded reduction by $$\mathscr R(X,x)= \mathscr R_0(X,x) \times_{\mathscr P_{\widetilde K} (\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)})} \mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}} (\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)}^{\rm gr}).$$ Goodness, separation of germ morphisms, and relative interiority are detected by affineness, separatedness, and properness of this ordinary reduction, respectively.
statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Ordinary reduction on the strict category]
\label{fnd:ordinarystrictgermreduction}
For a strictly $K$-analytic germ, with $K$ nontrivially
valued, there is a canonical ordinary birational reduction
$\mathscr R_0(X,x)$ with field $\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)}$.
It is functorial and independent of strict affinoid charts
and neighbourhoods. Its nonempty quasi-compact open
subspaces classify strict subdomain germs.
It is related to the graded reduction by
\[
 \mathscr R(X,x)=
 \mathscr R_0(X,x)
   \times_{\mathscr P_{\widetilde K}
                       (\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)})}
   \mathscr P_{\widetilde K^{\rm gr}}
                       (\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)}^{\rm gr}).
\]
Goodness, separation of germ morphisms, and relative
interiority are detected by affineness, separatedness,
and properness of this ordinary reduction, respectively.
\end{theorem}

NAG-001985.title: Ordinary reduction on the strict category

proof.html:
Choose ordinary affinoid neighbourhoods of xx in XX and of yy in its inverse image, keeping the given rank-zero germ. Write F=ℋ(x)F=\mathcal H(x) and E=ℋ(y)E=\mathcal H(y). Lemma [fnd:rankzeroquasismoothseparableresidue] gives a finite separable extension E/FE/F. The essential-surjectivity assertion of Theorem [fnd:goodetalegermresidueequivalence] gives a finite étale morphism T→UT\to U over an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood UU of xx, with its finite affinoid source and unique point tt over xx. It gives the specified identification ℋ(t)=E\mathcal H(t)=E over FF. Take an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood YUY_U of yy mapping into UU.

In the actual finite base change YU×UT→YUY_U\times_U T\to Y_U, the fibre at yy has algebra E⊗FEE\otimes_F E by Theorem [fnd:allpointaffinoidfibres] and Proposition [fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange]. The multiplication map to EE defines a point y′y' over y,ty,t and induces the identity of EE on the two completed residue fields. The projection to YUY_U is finite étale: the finite algebra is the ordinary tensor product with the finite norm and finite étaleness is preserved by that base change, using the finite algebra calculation in Proposition [fnd:finiteetalequasismooth]. Apply Corollary [fnd:etalesameresiduelocalisomorphism] at y′y' to obtain a lift g:(Y,y)→(T,t)g:(Y,y)\to(T,t) on an ordinary neighbourhood of yy. This lift is quasi-smooth of rank zero, since the map to TT before the local identification is a base change of ff. Use Theorem [fnd:jacobiansmoothdomainbasechange] and the actual differential base change in Proposition [fnd:analyticdifferentialbasechange].

Theorem [fnd:goodgermiffaffinereduction] makes the reductions of these two good germs affine. The completed-residue-field map of gg is the given identity, so their structural maps place both reductions in the same graded valuation space over $\widetilde K^{\rm gr}$. Functoriality in Theorem [fnd:allgradedgermreduction] identifies the reduction morphism with inclusion of the first affine open in the second. Theorem [fnd:goodgermdomainclassification] realizes that open as the reduction of a subdomain germ (W,t)(W,t) of (T,t)(T,t). It is good by the affine-to-good implication of Theorem [fnd:goodgermiffaffinereduction]. Choose an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood of tt in this subdomain representative.

The actual inverse-image germ under gg of this affinoid domain has full source reduction, by Theorem [fnd:allgradedgermreduction]. Order reflection in Theorem [fnd:allgermdomainclassification] makes it the whole source germ. Restricting an ordinary neighbourhood gives the lifted map into this affinoid domain. Its reduction is an isomorphism over the same graded field, hence proper. Theorem  [fnd:generalproperreductioninterior] makes yy an interior point of this lifted map. The map is still quasi-smooth of rank zero by the same base change and differential comparison.

Lemma [fnd:quasismoothrankzeroisolated] gives isolation of the fibre point. The identity test in Theorem [fnd:jacobianflatregularcriterion] gives flatness of the ordinary local map. The relative differential is coherent by Theorem [fnd:analyticdifferentialdomains]. Its rank is zero at yy, so its tensor with the residue field of the ordinary source stalk is zero, as can be checked after the field extension to ℋ(y)\mathcal H(y). It vanishes at the ordinary stalk by . The source and the affinoid target are good, so Proposition [fnd:localfiniteetalecriterion] applies at this isolated interior point and makes the lifted map étale. Its completed residue fields agree by Corollary [fnd:domainresiduefields] and the original lift’s field identity. A second application of Corollary [fnd:etalesameresiduelocalisomorphism] identifies actual ordinary neighbourhoods. An affinoid ordinary neighbourhood VV in the resulting source has image an affinoid domain of TT, by transitivity of analytic domains in Proposition [fnd:generalnetdomaincalculus]. The original finite étale T→UT\to U and VV give the factorization.
proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Choose ordinary affinoid neighbourhoods of \(x\) in \(X\) and of
\(y\) in its inverse image, keeping the given rank-zero germ.
Write \(F=\mathcal H(x)\) and \(E=\mathcal H(y)\).
Lemma~\ref{fnd:rankzeroquasismoothseparableresidue} gives a finite
separable extension \(E/F\). The essential-surjectivity assertion of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodetalegermresidueequivalence} gives a finite
\'etale morphism \(T\to U\) over an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood
\(U\) of \(x\), with its finite affinoid source and unique point \(t\)
over \(x\). It gives the specified
identification \(\mathcal H(t)=E\) over \(F\). Take an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood \(Y_U\) of \(y\) mapping
into \(U\).

In the actual finite base change \(Y_U\times_U T\to Y_U\),
the fibre at \(y\) has algebra \(E\otimes_F E\) by
Theorem~\ref{fnd:allpointaffinoidfibres} and
Proposition~\ref{fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange}. The multiplication
map to \(E\) defines a point \(y'\) over \(y,t\) and induces the
identity of \(E\) on the two completed residue fields. The projection
to \(Y_U\) is finite \'etale: the finite algebra is the ordinary
tensor product with the finite norm and finite \'etaleness is
preserved by that base change, using the finite algebra calculation
in Proposition~\ref{fnd:finiteetalequasismooth}. Apply
Corollary~\ref{fnd:etalesameresiduelocalisomorphism} at \(y'\) to
obtain a lift \(g:(Y,y)\to(T,t)\) on an ordinary neighbourhood of
\(y\). This lift is quasi-smooth of rank zero, since the map to
\(T\) before the local identification is a base change of \(f\).
Use Theorem~\ref{fnd:jacobiansmoothdomainbasechange} and the actual
differential base change in
Proposition~\ref{fnd:analyticdifferentialbasechange}.

Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodgermiffaffinereduction} makes the reductions of
these two good germs affine. The completed-residue-field map of \(g\)
is the given identity, so their structural maps place both reductions
in the same graded valuation space over \(\widetilde K^{\rm gr}\).
Functoriality in Theorem~\ref{fnd:allgradedgermreduction} identifies
the reduction morphism with inclusion of the first affine open in
the second. Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodgermdomainclassification} realizes
that open as the reduction of a subdomain germ \((W,t)\) of \((T,t)\).
It is good by the affine-to-good implication of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodgermiffaffinereduction}. Choose an ordinary
affinoid neighbourhood of \(t\) in this subdomain representative.

The actual inverse-image germ under \(g\) of this affinoid domain
has full source reduction, by
Theorem~\ref{fnd:allgradedgermreduction}. Order reflection in
Theorem~\ref{fnd:allgermdomainclassification} makes it the whole
source germ. Restricting an ordinary neighbourhood gives the lifted
map into this affinoid domain. Its reduction is an isomorphism over
the same graded field, hence proper. Theorem~
\ref{fnd:generalproperreductioninterior} makes \(y\) an interior point
of this lifted map. The map is still quasi-smooth of rank zero by
the same base change and differential comparison.

Lemma~\ref{fnd:quasismoothrankzeroisolated} gives isolation of the
fibre point. The identity test in
Theorem~\ref{fnd:jacobianflatregularcriterion} gives flatness of the
ordinary local map. The relative differential is coherent by
Theorem~\ref{fnd:analyticdifferentialdomains}. Its rank is zero
at \(y\), so its tensor with the residue field of the ordinary source
stalk is zero, as can be checked after the field extension to
\(\mathcal H(y)\). It vanishes at the ordinary stalk by
\cite[Tag 00DV(2)]{StacksAlg}. The source and the affinoid target are
good, so Proposition~\ref{fnd:localfiniteetalecriterion} applies at
this isolated interior point and makes the lifted map \'etale.
Its completed residue fields agree by
Corollary~\ref{fnd:domainresiduefields} and the original lift's field
identity. A second application of
Corollary~\ref{fnd:etalesameresiduelocalisomorphism} identifies actual
ordinary neighbourhoods. An affinoid ordinary neighbourhood \(V\)
in the resulting source has image an affinoid domain of \(T\), by
transitivity of analytic domains in
Proposition~\ref{fnd:generalnetdomaincalculus}. The original
finite \'etale \(T\to U\) and \(V\) give the factorization.

\subsection*{NAG-002072. An integral-coefficient bound at the outer annulus}
\label{errata:nag002072}
See \hyperref[fnd:curves]{Analytic curves and skeleta} and the
\hyperref[cand:boundarycoefficientorder]{historical slope lemma}.
Its disc assertion has integral coefficients. The annular assertion
uses the weaker phrase \emph{bounded double series} and reduces only
the coefficients with second exponent zero.

\paragraph{Counterexample to the bounded-series assertion.}
Take \(K=\mathbb Q_p\), \(a=p\) with the usual \(p\)-adic absolute
value, and use the finite double series
\[
 g(s)=1+s-a^{-1}s(a/s)
 \qquad (|a|<|s|<1).
\]
Its coefficients are bounded, and the analytic function is \(s\),
which is itself bounded by \(1\). The row with second exponent zero
has reduction \(1+\bar s\), of order \(0\). At every annular Gauss
point of radius \(\rho\), the norm of \(g\) is \(\rho\). The historical
formula would give \(1\). The row with second exponent zero thus
depends on the chosen bounded double-series representative.
If bounded is taken to mean that each coefficient has absolute value
at most one, it is precisely the integral hypothesis below.

\begin{lemma}[Integral coefficients and residual order]
\label{errata:nag002072:integral}
Let \(K\) be a complete non-Archimedean field with valuation ring \(O\).
If a power series \(g(z)=\sum_{j\geq0}b_jz^j\) has all \(b_j\in O\)
and its formal reduction has finite order \(d\), then its Gauss norm
at radius \(\rho<1\) is \(\rho^d\) for all \(\rho\) sufficiently close
to \(1\). The same holds at the outer end of \( |a|<|s|<1 \), where
\(0<|a|<1\), for a double series
\[
 g(s)=\sum_{i,j\geq0}c_{ij}s^i(a/s)^j
\]
with \emph{all} \(c_{ij}\in O\), if the reduction of
\(\sum_i c_{i0}s^i\) has finite order \(d\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the disc, \(|b_d|=1\) and \(|b_j|<1\) for \(j<d\). Choose
\(\rho_0<1\) so that \(|b_j|<\rho_0^{d-j}\) for all \(j<d\).
For \(\rho_0<\rho<1\) the term \(b_dz^d\) has Gauss norm \(\rho^d\).
Every earlier term has strictly smaller norm and the convergent tail
starting at \(d+1\) has norm at most \(\rho^{d+1}\).
The ultrametric inequality, applied in both directions, gives
the equality.

For the annulus the \(j=0\) part satisfies the disc calculation.
Increase \(\rho_0\) so that \(|a|<\rho_0^{d+1}\).
At a fixed \(\rho\) with \(\rho_0<\rho<1\), the norms of the double
series terms are bounded by \(\rho^i(|a|/\rho)^j\). Both factors
decay geometrically in their respective exponents. Only finitely
many of their products exceed any fixed positive bound, so the
terms converge as a sum in the complete Gauss field. The norm of
the entire \(j\geq1\) sum is at most \(|a|/\rho<\rho^d\).
Adding it leaves the norm of the \(j=0\) sum unchanged.
\end{proof}

\noindent
This proof uses the same integral scope as the valid fragments of the
\hyperref[cand:boundarycoefficientorder]{historical proof}.
The restriction applies to the coefficients of the displayed
representative.

\subsection*{NAG-002213. Generizations along nonempty faces}
\label{errata:nag002213}
See \hyperref[ch:3]{Charts, skeleta and faithful tropicalization}
and the \hyperref[cand:uniquestratumfacegenerization]{historical face lemma}.
The standing definition indexes strata by nonempty coordinate sets,
whereas the last sentence allows an arbitrary \(J'\subseteq J\).

\paragraph{Counterexample to the empty-face assertion.}
Take \(K=\mathbb Q_p\) with valuation ring \(O=\mathbb Z_p\),
and use the identity formally \'{e}tale, topologically finitely
presented map on \(O\langle X,Y\rangle/(XY-p)\). Its special fibre is
\(\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb F_p[X,Y]/(XY))\).
The nodal point \(\eta=(X,Y)\) is the generic point of the closed
stratum with \(I=\{X,Y\}\). For \(J=\{X\}\), the generic point
\(\eta_J=(X)\) of \(X=0,\ Y\ne0\) specializes to \(\eta\).
If the same defining rule is applied to \(J'=\varnothing\), it
requires \(X,Y\) both invertible. Localizing the special-fibre ring

point, so the claimed generization cannot exist.

and \(\varnothing\ne J\subseteq I\). Exactly one
\(\eta_J\in Q_J\) specializes to \(\eta\).

of \(\eta_J\) is \(\eta_{J'}\). The
\hyperref[cand:nonemptyfacegenerization]{full proof for nonempty faces}
is the existing checked proof. It applies flat going down on the
actual pullback of the affine coordinate face, and uniqueness follows
from the local normal domain at the specialization point.

Theorem [v037:globaltrop:finiteimage] gives a finite polyhedral image of dimension at most dd and a finite boundary image of dimension at most d−1d-1. Choose one finite common subdivision with the boundary image as a subcomplex. At a point in the relative interior of a dd-cell, the whole moment fibre is therefore interior, and the local image is contained in that cell’s affine dd-plane. Theorem [v037:degree:moduleweight] defines the nonnegative integer weight there. It is locally constant, by Theorem [v037:degree:modulecycle] on small convex neighbourhoods with the actual local fan presentations of Theorem [v037:analytic:interiorlocalstar]. The relative interior of the cell is convex, so the weight is constant there. For the structure module it is positive by Theorem [v036:flatgermweight].

On a common subdivision of two choices, the generic weights compute the same whole-fibre module invariant. Thus their chains agree. Additivity follows from the exact-sequence formula of Theorem [v037:degree:moduleweight]. On the complement of the boundary image the chain is the local balanced module cycle of Theorem [v037:analytic:interiorcycle]. All cells with nonzero weights are compact polytopes: the actual moment image is compact, and the complex is finite. Consequently the integral is a finite sum of the integrals constructed in Lemma [v037:integration:polyhedralcalculus]. That lemma gives subdivision independence and positivity. Restriction to the whole interior weight domain gives exactly the previously defined local integral.

First suppose that the compatibility is an identity of analytic characters: each target unit pulls back to the monomial in the source units prescribed by aa. For this finite morphism, take finite global subdivisions of the two actual images and their boundary images. Refine along the images of all source cells, using the finite linear elimination and hyperplane construction in Theorem [cand:balancedpolyhedralpushforward]. Outside a finite union of polyhedra of dimension at most d−1d-1 in each target dd-cell, the target whole fibre is interior, and every source weight above it lies in a full-rank dd-cell. The entire inverse weight set is finite, with at most one point per such source cell. Finite relative interior and composition imply absolute interior for every point of those source fibres.

Near such a target weight, Lemma [v037:analytic:finitepolyhedralpatching] retains the complete source inverse support in a finite pure presentation. Theorem [v037:degree:modulefunctoriality] then identifies the finite lattice-index sum with the target weight of MM as an AA-module. Its empty-inverse- image case gives zero on both sides. statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Global finite-module tropical chains]
\label{v037:integration:globalchain}
Let $X=\mathcal M(A)$ be pure of analytic dimension $d$ over
a complete non-Archimedean field with its specified absolute
value, and let a unit tuple $f$ define $t_f:X\to\mathbb R^n$.
For every finite $A$-module $M$ there is a canonical finite
nonnegative integral $d$-dimensional polyhedral chain
\[
                              \mathcal T_f(M).
\]
Its support is contained in $t_f(X)$. On any common finite
subdivision of the actual image and $t_f(\partial_KX)$,
the weight of a $d$-cell is the module weight
$m_{M,f}(v)$ at any point of its relative interior. Cells
of dimension less than $d$ give no $d$-chain term.
The chain is additive in short exact sequences, independent
of subdivision, and balanced off $t_f(\partial_KX)$.
For $M=A$ every occurring $d$-cell has positive weight.

For a smooth $(d,d)$-superform $\alpha$ on an open
neighbourhood of the actual compact image, define
\[
                   \mathcal I_{M,f}(\alpha)
                              =\sum_\sigma m_\sigma\int_\sigma\alpha.
\]
This is independent of subdivision and is nonnegative when
the tangential top coefficients of $\alpha$ are nonnegative.
It agrees with $I_{M,f}$ of
Theorem~\ref{v037:integration:momenttests} for tests supported
in the whole interior weight domain.

Let $p:\mathcal M(B)\to\mathcal M(A)$ be finite, with both
spaces pure of analytic dimension $d$, and suppose moment
tuples satisfy $t_{f_A}\circ p=a\circ t_{f_B}$ for an
integral map $a$. For every finite $B$-module $M$,
\[
                  a_*\mathcal T_{f_B}(M)=\mathcal T_{f_A}(M),
                  \qquad
                  \mathcal I_{M,f_B}(a^*\alpha)
                               =\mathcal I_{M,f_A}(\alpha).
\]
On the right $M$ is its finite $A$-module. In particular,
adjoining analytic unit coordinates preserves these chains
under projection and preserves the corresponding integrals.
\end{theorem}

NAG-002405.title: Global finite-module tropical chains

statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Proper moment pushforward with generic lengths]
\label{v038:degree:propercycle}
Let $p:X\to Y$ be proper, where $X$ and $Y$ are good Hausdorff
and pure of the same analytic dimension $d$. Let $\mathcal F$
be coherent on $X_G$. For an affinoid domain $V\subseteq Y$
and a unit tuple $f$ on $V$, put $Z=p^{-1}(V)$ and
\[
              \mathcal P_{p,\mathcal F,f}
                       =\mathcal T_{Z,p^*f}(\mathcal F|_Z).
\]
This is a finite nonnegative integral $d$-chain. There is a
compact finite polyhedral set $E$ of dimension at most $d-1$
such that at every generic $d$-cell point $w\notin E$ it has
the following description. There is an actual finite
restriction
\[
 p_P:X_P=p^{-1}(V_P)\longrightarrow V_P=t_f^{-1}(P),
 \qquad w\in\operatorname{int}(P),
\]
with affinoid algebras $A_P,B_P$. For the finite $B_P$-module
$M_P=\Gamma(X_P,\mathcal F)$ its coefficient is
\begin{align*}
 m_{\mathcal P}(w)
   &=\sum_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Min}(A_P)}
       \operatorname{length}_{(A_P)_{\mathfrak p}}
                     ((M_P)_{\mathfrak p})
                  m_{\mathcal M(A_P/\mathfrak p),f}(w),\\
 \operatorname{length}_{(A_P)_{\mathfrak p}}
                     ((M_P)_{\mathfrak p})
   &=\sum_{\substack{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Min}(B_P)\\
                      \mathfrak q\cap A_P=\mathfrak p}}
       \operatorname{length}_{(B_P)_{\mathfrak q}}
                       ((M_P)_{\mathfrak q})
                    [\kappa(\mathfrak q):\kappa(\mathfrak p)].
\end{align*}
An empty component fibre contributes zero. Residue-field
degrees in this expression are full degrees, including their
inseparable factors. The coefficient and the chain do not
depend on the finite collar or the affinoid cover of $Z$.

If a global unit tuple $g$ on $Z$ and an integral map $a$
satisfy $t_f\circ p=a\circ t_g$, then
\[
                a_*\mathcal T_{Z,g}(\mathcal F|_Z)
                                          =\mathcal P_{p,\mathcal F,f}.
\]
In particular its generic coefficient is the full lattice-index
sum over all full-rank source cells above that target cell;
contracted cells contribute zero. For every smooth
$(d,d)$-superform $\alpha$ defined near $t_f(V)$,
\[
          \mathcal I_{Z,\mathcal F}(p^*t_f^*\alpha)
                             =\int_{\mathcal P_{p,\mathcal F,f}}\alpha.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Proper projection from generic coefficient agreement]
\label{v038:degree:propergenericprojection}
Let $p:X\to Y$ be proper between good Hausdorff analytic spaces
pure of the same dimension $d$. Let $\mathcal F$ and
$\mathcal G$ be coherent on $X_G$ and $Y_G$, respectively,
and fix $\Delta\in\mathbb Q_{\geq0}$. Let $D\subseteq Y$
be a closed analytic subspace whose defining ideal, on every
affinoid domain of $Y$, is contained in no minimal prime.
The empty subspace is permitted.

Suppose that whenever $W=\mathcal M(A)$ is an affinoid domain
of $Y\setminus D$ for which $p^{-1}(W)=\mathcal M(B)\to W$
is finite, the modules
\[
          M=\Gamma(p^{-1}(W),\mathcal F),\qquad
          L=\Gamma(W,\mathcal G)
\]
satisfy, for every $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Min}(A)$,
\begin{equation}
\label{v038:degree:genericcoefficientcondition}
  \operatorname{length}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{\mathfrak p})
          =\Delta\operatorname{length}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}
                                             (L_{\mathfrak p}).
\end{equation}
Then for every affinoid domain $V\subseteq Y$ and unit tuple
$f$ on $V$,
\[
        \mathcal P_{p,\mathcal F,f}
               =\Delta\mathcal T_f\bigl(\Gamma(V,\mathcal G)\bigr).
\]
For every ordinary smooth moment form
$\alpha\in\mathcal A^{d,d}_{Y,c}(Y)$, the pullback has compact
support and
\[
               \int_{X,\mathcal F}p^*\alpha
                                  =\Delta\int_{Y,\mathcal G}\alpha.
\]
These scalar formulas multiply under composition when the
corresponding coefficient conditions hold for the two maps.

For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and
$\mathcal G=\mathcal O_Y$, condition
\eqref{v038:degree:genericcoefficientcondition} uses the ratio
of the full generic local lengths. If $A$ is reduced, its
denominator is one, so a nonzero such ratio is a positive

full inseparable degree retained.

In the isomorphism case the two finite modules on every
affinoid restriction disjoint from $D$ are identified.
Their generic local lengths are equal, so
Theorem~\ref{v038:degree:propergenericprojection} applies
with $\Delta=1$.

For the rank assertion, fix an actual affinoid \(V\) and
a unit tuple \(f\) on it. By
Theorem~\ref{v037:degree:exceptionalimage}, the image of the
actual closed quotient \(D\cap V\) has dimension at most \(d-1\).
Away from this image and the finite-collar exceptional set of
Theorem~\ref{v038:degree:propercycle}, take a generic point
\(w\) of a \(d\)-cell of the common subdivision of the actual
chain supports and excluded images given by
Lemma~\ref{cand:polyhedralrefinementproduct}, and choose the
whole actual collar \(p_P:X_P\to V_P\) with \(w\in\operatorname{int}P\)
and \(V_P\cap D=\varnothing\), using
Corollary~\ref{v038:degree:properfinitecollar}. The nonempty
domains \(X_P,V_P\) are pure of dimension \(d\) by
Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:puritylocality}.
The finite analytic direct image on \(V_P\) is locally free of
the given rank \(r\) by restriction of the direct image over
\(Y\setminus D\) and the finite coherent direct-image comparison
of Proposition~\ref{fnd:finitecoherentdirectimagebasechange}.
If \(X_P\) is empty and \(V_P\) is nonempty, this direct image
is zero, so \(r=0\) on that collar.

Apply the rank assertion of
Theorem~\ref{v037:integration:compactfinitepushforward} to this
finite map, with \(Q=V_P\) and the literal pullback of the
target tuple. On its finite affinoid trivializing cover and
all actual intersections the direct-image modules are free
of rank \(r\); every localized module length is \(r\)
times the corresponding structure-ring length. The finite
chart comparison and inclusion--exclusion give the factor
\(r\) for the compact integral on the collar.

By Theorem~\ref{v038:degree:compactchain}, these are integrals
of the two collar chains. Take ambient top forms supported in
a small open neighbourhood of \(w\) inside \(\operatorname{int}P\),
meeting the refined top-dimensional support only in the given
\(d\)-cell. A smooth bump with nonzero integral on this cell
detects its coefficient, hence the source coefficient is \(r\)
times the target coefficient, including zero coefficients. The same theorem
identifies the source collar chain with the restriction of the
compact chain on \(p^{-1}(V)\). For the target it identifies the
collar structure chain with the corresponding restriction on
\(V\). Thus the equality holds at all generic \(d\)-cells.

statement.tex:
\begin{corollary}[Proper modifications and generic finite free degree]
\label{v038:degree:propermodification}
Keep $p:X\to Y$ and $D\subseteq Y$ as in
Theorem~\ref{v038:degree:propergenericprojection}.
If $p$ is an isomorphism over $Y\setminus D$ and coherent
modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are identified there by
$\mathcal F\simeq p^*\mathcal G$, then
\[
                    \int_{X,\mathcal F}p^*\alpha
                                         =\int_{Y,\mathcal G}\alpha
\]
for every compactly supported ordinary smooth top form.
In particular a proper modification which is an isomorphism
away from such a closed subspace preserves the structure-module
integral. Additional source components mapped into $D$ are
allowed, provided $X$ remains pure of dimension $d$.

More generally, suppose that over $Y\setminus D$ the map is
finite and its coherent direct image of $\mathcal F$ is
locally free of constant rank $r$ on the analytic G-site.
Then
\[
                    \int_{X,\mathcal F}p^*\alpha
                                      =r\int_{Y,\mathcal O_Y}\alpha.
\]
The rank may be the full degree of a finite inseparable map;
separability is not required.
\end{corollary}

proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Represent \(\alpha\in\ker r_{\partial,w}\) on a real neighbourhood
\(O_0\) of \(w\). The zero-germ locus of its ordinary pullback is
an open \(N\) in \(t_f^{-1}(O_0)\) by
Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:germsheaf}, and contains every point of
\(\partial_K V\cap t_f^{-1}(w)\). The absolute analytic boundary
is closed in the compact \(V\), by openness of the affinoid
interior in Proposition~\ref{fnd:affinoidinteriorcalculus}.
Hence \(t_f(\partial_K V\setminus N)\) is compact and misses \(w\).
Choose a smaller real neighbourhood \(O\subset O_0\) avoiding
that image. For \(\rho\in C_c^\infty(O)\), extend \(\rho\alpha\)
by zero. Its pullback is zero on an ordinary neighbourhood of
every boundary point: over \(O\) such points lie in \(N\), and
outside \(O\) they have neighbourhoods avoiding the pullback
of \(\operatorname{supp}\rho\). The union of these neighbourhoods
is an ordinary neighbourhood of \(\partial_K V\).
Theorem~\ref{f7v38:annihilation} applies to this one global
representative, with the original \(V,M,f\), and gives
\(\B_C(\rho\alpha)=0\) by \eqref{f7v38:polyhedralboundary}.

Shrink \(O\) so that it meets no geometric facet except \(\tau\).
This is possible for the finite complex at \(w\in\relint\tau\).
The boundary formula gives
\[
  \int_\tau \rho\,\lambda_{\tau,\cdot}(\alpha)\,d\mu_\tau=0
                         \qquad(\rho\in C_c^\infty(O)).
\]
The density is continuous on the relative interior of this
fixed facet. A nonzero value at \(w\) would have strict constant
sign on a smaller neighbourhood and give a nonzero integral
against a nonnegative bump positive at \(w\). For \(d=1\) the
facet is a point with mass one, and the same identity is
evaluation. Thus \(\lambda_{\tau,w}(\alpha)=0\) and the functional
descends to the image of \(r_{\partial,w}\).

For the integrated assertion, two representatives of an ordinary
section give the same numerical value by
\eqref{f7v38:polyhedralboundary},
Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:germsheaf} and the single-chart comparison
of Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:compactintegral}. In fact the value
is the ordinary integral of the derivative. If a section
represented by \(f\) has all boundary stalks zero, its zero-germ
locus is an ordinary neighbourhood of \(\partial_K V\).
Theorem~\ref{f7v38:annihilation} therefore kills the kernel of
this restriction, giving the asserted algebraic factorization.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The pending facet-normal kernel inclusion]
\label{f7v38:kernel}
In the exact scope of Theorem~\ref{f7v38:annihilation},
\[
                   \ker r_{\partial,w}\subseteq\ker\lambda_{\tau,w}

the image of these source-local boundary germs.

also factors through restriction to the boundary stalks.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proposition}[Cancellation for compatible artificial cuts]

 \B_{\T_F(M_W)}(\eta)

statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Analytic uniform logarithmic excision; F8LA-A1R]
\label{fnd:nag002565:analytic-excision}
Assume \hyperref[f8la:supplied-graph]{the supplied finite graph hypothesis}. Let \(\alpha\) be a smooth ambient
\((n,n)\)-form near \(B\), and suppose its ordinary pullback to \(V\)
extends by zero to a compactly supported section \(\alpha_X\) on \(X\),
with support in \(\Int_{\rm top}(V,X)\).

Choose any smooth \(\theta\) as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:weak}, and let
\[
 u_R(x)=
 \begin{cases}
   \log|f(x)|\,\theta(t_f(x)-R),&x\in V\setminus Z,\\
   0,&x\in Z.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{4.3}
\]
Then \(u_R\) is an ordinary smooth function on \(V\), and
\[
 L_R(\alpha_X):=\int_X\operatorname{ext}_0(u_R\alpha_X|_V)
      =I_C\bigl((-t)\theta(t-R)\pi^*\alpha\bigr).
 \tag{4.4}
\]
For all \(R\geq H\) these numbers equal the single finite value
\[
 L_f(\alpha_X)=I_C((-t)\pi^*\alpha),
 \tag{4.5}
\]
and
\[
 |L_f(\alpha_X)|
 \leq A_C\max\{|a|,|H|\}\,
           \max_{I,J}\sup_B|\alpha_{I,J}|.
 \tag{4.6}
\]
The threshold and constant are independent of the variable coefficients
of \(\alpha\). No boundary-separation or balancing condition is required
for this estimate.
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}[Conditional local weak Poincar\'e--Lelong; F8LA-A2R]
\label{thm:analyticpl}
Under \hyperref[f8la:supplied-graph]{the graph hypothesis} and \hyperref[f8la:supplied-flux]{the support and divisor calibration},
\[
 L_f(\dd\eta_X)=\int_D (t_g|_D)^*\eta.
 \tag{4.11}
\]
Here \(L_f\) is the stabilized logarithmic excision from
Proposition~\ref{fnd:nag002565:analytic-excision}. The sign is positive for \(\log|f|\)
and negative for \(-\log|f|\).

\[

       =\int_D(t_g|_D)^*\eta .
 \tag{4.12}
\]

\(R<t_f<R+1\) and the fixed support of \(\eta_X\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The map $p$ is surjective by

The actual finite base-change theorem
\Dep{fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange} gives its algebra $D_s$ and

For $s\in\operatorname{int}(P)$, multiplying target coordinates by
the actual constants $c^{q_j}$ gives isometric identifications with

The monomial Gauss-field theorem \Dep{v036:gaussisogeny} gives
\[
 R_s\widehat\otimes_{R_{Q,v}}H_{Q,v}=H_s,
       \qquad [H_s:H_{Q,v}]=|\det(QA)|,
\]
and makes $R_s$ finite free of that rank over $R_{Q,v}$.

$\dim_{H_s}(M\otimes_{R_P}H_s)=D_M$.
The index chain $QA\mathbb Z^d\subset QN\subset\mathbb Z^d$ gives
\[
 |\det(QA)|=[\mathbb Z^d:QN][QN:QA\mathbb Z^d]=e_Qj_A,
\]
which proves \eqref{mpw:eqcalibration}. The lattice factor is
$j_A$, not its reciprocal.

Apply Proposition~\ref{mpw:finiteoverlap} to the ordinary interior
of $U$ in $Y$. For $s$ near $s_0$ outside finitely many walls,
$U$ contains the whole fibre in its ordinary interior.
All points above such $s$ are absolute interior in $Y$: the

small box in $b+A\mathbb R^d$. Off the walls every entire fibre

statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Pointed projection independence in finite Gauss charts]
\label{mpw:pointedweight}
In Definition~\ref{mpw:chartclass}, ordinary affinoid neighbourhoods
$U$ of $x$ in $Y$ have the same germ at $w_0$ of their existing
top-dimensional module chains. This germ is the affine $d$-plane
$w_0+N_{\mathbb R}$ with coefficient
\[
                               \mu_x(M,f)=j_A D_M.
\]
For $M=B$ the coefficient is positive; a zero module coefficient
denotes the zero chain.

For each $U$, outside finitely many proper hyperplanes in a
neighbourhood of $s_0$, its entire moment fibre at $v=b+As$ has
the actual algebra $D_s=B\widehat\otimes_{R_P}R_s$.
For every admissible $Q$, that same algebra is norm-admissible
finite over $R_{Q,v}$ and
\begin{equation}
\label{mpw:eqcalibration}
 \frac{\dim_{H_{Q,v}}
     \bigl(M\otimes_B(D_s\widehat\otimes_{R_{Q,v}}H_{Q,v})\bigr)}
      {e_Q}=j_A D_M.
\end{equation}
The entire fibre and module, including their scheme structure,
occur in this formula. Its value is independent of the projection
and of the ordinary affinoid neighbourhood.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write \(d=n-1\) and let \(S=\{e^{-b}\leq |f|\leq e^{-a}\}\).
On an affinoid chart of \(V\), the constraints \(t_g\in C\),
the slab constraints, and the equalities specifying individual
moment levels are the \hyperref[fnd:generalizedrationaluniversal]
{actual Laurent-domain conditions}. An integral-affine inequality
is a bound on the absolute value of a monomial. The
\hyperref[fnd:generalnetdomaincalculus]{analytic-domain calculus}
allows these restrictions on the chart net of \(V\).

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The two finite-flat fibres.}
Let \(w\) be in the relative interior of \(C\), and let
\(\tau\in(a,b)\), with the relevant section points covered by (2.3).
Let \(\xi_0\) be the Gauss point of radii \(\exp(-Pw)\) over the
rigid origin. Let \(\xi_\tau\) be the relative Gauss point of
those horizontal radii over the parameter Gauss point of radius
\(e^{-\tau}\). On a Laurent polynomial the successive Gauss
maxima are the maximum over all pairs of horizontal and parameter
exponents, with monomial weight
\(\exp(-\langle I,Pw\rangle-j\tau)\) for exponents \(I,j\).
The \hyperref[fnd:gaussnorm]{multiplicative Gauss norm} and the
\hyperref[fnd:multilaurentactualpresentation]{actual Laurent
presentation} identify \(\mathcal H(\xi_\tau)\) with the field
of the joint polytorus Gauss point. The central field is
\(H_C=\mathcal H(\xi_0)\).

At either point \(\xi\), restrict the given finite map to an
affinoid target neighbourhood in the supplied neighbourhood.
Let \(R\) and \(B\) be its target algebra and the algebra of the
entire inverse image. The \hyperref[fnd:allpointaffinoidfibres]
{actual point fibre} and \hyperref[fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange]
{finite base change} give
\[
 E_\xi=B\widehat\otimes_R\mathcal H(\xi)
       =B\otimes_R\mathcal H(\xi).
\]
The supplied rank gives \(\dim_{\mathcal H(\xi)}E_\xi=\delta_C\).
At the rigid origin the parameter maps to zero, so the central
tensor factors through the full quotient \(B/fB\) and then through
the horizontal Gauss base change. The punctured calculation uses
its own field \(\mathcal H(\xi_\tau)\).

The horizontal weight of every point of the analytic fibre projects to
\(Pw\). Since the point lies over \(W_C\), injectivity of \(P\)
on \(C\) forces its horizontal weight to be \(w\). At \(\xi_0\)
the map factors through \(D\) as an analytic subspace, by the
equation \(f=0\) in the fibre algebra. At \(\xi_\tau\) the point
lies in \(S\) and has joint weight \((w,\tau)\).
Conversely, on the full central level at \(w\) and the full
slab level at \((w,\tau)\), the corresponding projected Gauss
fibres already satisfy the \(C\) constraints and have projected
target \(\xi_0\) and \(\xi_\tau\), respectively. Their targets
therefore lie in the actual chosen neighbourhoods. These
identifications apply to every affinoid test over the respective
completed residue field. The same inequalities and structural
maps give both factorizations by the
\hyperref[fnd:generalnetmorphismgluing]{analytic-domain universal property},
the \hyperref[fnd:generalizedrationaluniversal]{Laurent-domain
universal property}, and \hyperref[fnd:generalizeddomainbasechange]
{actual affinoid-domain base change}. The maps are mutually inverse.
This identifies \(E_C^D=E_{\xi_0}\) and proves the first equality.
It also identifies the full joint punctured Gauss fibre with
\(E_{\xi_\tau}\), with the full analytic structure on both sides.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Interior and flatness on the integrating charts.}
Choose a finite affinoid cover of the compact good \(V\), or a
common finite refinement of the given presenting cover. Its
\hyperref[v037:integration:separatedintersections]{actual finite
intersections} \(V_I\) are \hyperref[v037:integration:puritylocality]
{pure of dimension \(n\)} when nonempty. On the central side,
the \hyperref[f8:zero-purity-restriction]{actual principal-zero
purity theorem} gives the full quotient \(D_I=V_I\cap D\),
empty or pure of dimension \(d\). On the punctured side
\(S_I=V_I\cap S\) is an actual Laurent domain of \(V_I\), pure
of dimension \(n\) when nonempty.

Use \hyperref[v037:globaltrop:finiteimage]{finite polyhedrality
and the boundary-image dimension bound} on each chart in these
two finite lists. Refine their images and boundary images jointly
with the indicated cells by the
\hyperref[cand:polyhedralrefinementproduct]{common finite
subdivision}. On the central side omit the intersections of
\(C\) with the boundary images, the chart cells of dimension
less than \(d\), and the \(d\)-cells whose affine spans differ
from that of \(C\). Each omitted intersection has dimension less
than \(d\). At the remaining relative-interior points \(w\),
the entire \(g\)-level of every nonempty \(D_I\) at \(w\) avoids
its absolute boundary, and its local image is contained in
\(w+(N_C)_{\mathbf R}\). Indeed the finitely many image
cells through \(w\) all have this span, and a small neighbourhood
misses the other closed cells. When \(d=0\) the boundary images
are empty and the finite chart images have isolated points.

On the punctured side use \(C\times[a,b]\) in dimension \(n\)
and omit the corresponding intersections of dimension less than
\(n\). To make both calculations at the same horizontal weight,
also omit the product of the central exceptional set with
\([a,b]\). At each remaining generic \((w,\tau)\), the entire
joint level in every chart \(S_I\) meeting it is absolutely
interior, and the local image lies in
\((w,\tau)+(N_C\oplus\mathbb Z)_{\mathbf R}\).
Positivity of the supplied rank shows the levels under
consideration occur in the actual image. These arguments use the
generic points of the indicated cells and their finer
subdivision, with no calibrated product hypothesis for the
surrounding image.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The two weight calculations.}
Apply \hyperref[v037:degree:moduleweight]{the full module weight
formula} to the structure module on each \(D_I\) with a
nonempty level at such a \(w\), using \(P\) on \(N_C\).
Its numerator is the dimension over \(H_C\) of its actual
projected Gauss algebra. Apply the same formula separately
on each \(S_I\) with a nonempty joint level at \((w,\tau)\),
using \(P\oplus 1\) on \(N_C\oplus\mathbb Z\) and the joint
Gauss field. In both applications the chart fibre is the
restriction of the just-identified full actual fibre to the
indicated chart, by the same domain universal properties.
An empty level has zero contribution. The index on the
punctured side is \(e_C\), since
\[
 \mathbb Z^{d+1}/(P\oplus 1)(N_C\oplus\mathbb Z)
       \simeq \mathbb Z^d/P(N_C).
\]
When \(d=0\), the central tuple is empty, the horizontal field
is \(K\), and the lattice index is one.

For clarity, if there are several integrating charts, the two
full numerators each assemble by finite inclusion--exclusion.
At a fixed parameter point use
\(\mathcal M_{\mathcal H(\xi)}(E_\xi)\).
The finite algebra \(E_\xi\) is the product of its local
Artinian factors by \cite[Tag 00JB]{StacksAlg}. Each factor
has one analytic point, since its seminorms kill nilpotents and
\hyperref[fnd:finiteextensionnorms]{a finite residue-field extension}
has a unique extending norm. The pullback of a presenting domain
to a singleton factor is empty or is the original whole factor
by the domain universal property. The chart intersections
therefore contain exactly the common factors, with their full
algebras. The cover includes every factor, and a factor in
\(r\geq 1\) charts occurs with signed multiplicity
\[
              \sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{j+1}\binom rj=1.
\]
Thus the signed sum of the chart-intersection Gauss dimensions is
\(\delta_C\) on each side. It counts every full local length
times its residue-field degree. This is the same signed sum
as in the \hyperref[v037:integration:compactintegral]
{compact integral formula} for the actual central space and
for the compact annular domain with its finite presenting
affinoids. The tuples agree on the overlaps because they are
restrictions of the given global tuples. For a single chart
the sum is just its weight calculation.

The \hyperref[fnd:nag002405:global-finite-module-chain-weights]
{finite-chain weight and subdivision rule} now gives the
coefficient \(\delta_C/e_C\) on the indicated central cell
and on the indicated top product cell. All their finer
top-dimensional pieces under the supplied section rank have
this value. Lower-dimensional faces have no contribution to
the top chains. This proves the two weight equalities in
(2.4).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
The forms \(u\,d''\eta\) and \(d'u\wedge\eta\) are ordinary smooth,
with compact support contained in \(K_0\). Thus \hyperref[f7gg:global]{(1.1)} applies to them.
The frozen exterior algebra uses total-degree signs and
\(d''d'=-d'd''\). Therefore
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 0&=I_{\mathcal F}\bigl(d'(u\,d''\eta)\bigr)
   =I_{\mathcal F}(d'u\wedge d''\eta)
      +I_{\mathcal F}(u\,\dd\eta),\\
 0&=I_{\mathcal F}\bigl(d''(d'u\wedge\eta)\bigr)
   =-I_{\mathcal F}(\dd u\wedge\eta)
      -I_{\mathcal F}(d'u\wedge d''\eta).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Eliminating the common term proves (1.2). The zero extensions are smooth
because their supports are closed compact subsets of the neighbourhood
where the products are defined. No \(J\)-symmetry condition is needed.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Local compatible collars and their intrinsic common Gauss set]
\label{gci:localcollars}
Let \(X=\mathcal M(B)\) be nonempty and pure of analytic
dimension \(d\geq1\), with actual units
\(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)\) and moment map \(t=t_f\).
Assume
\[
             w\in t(X),\qquad F=t^{-1}(w)
                          \subset\operatorname{Int}(X/K).
 \tag{8}\label{gci:wholeinner}
\]
This hypothesis concerns the entire original moment fibre.

There are a finite pure \(d\)-dimensional rational fan
\(\Sigma\) and a real neighbourhood \(O\) of \(w\) such that
\[
                         t(X)\cap O=(w+|\Sigma|)\cap O.
 \tag{9}\label{gci:star}
\]
Choose a closed rectangular box \(W\subset O\) with
\(w\in\operatorname{int}(W)\), and set
\[
                              Z=t^{-1}(W)\subset X.
 \tag{10}\label{gci:localizedsource}
\]
Call an integral \(Q:\mathbb Z^n\to\mathbb Z^d\)
admissible here when it is injective on the span of every
top cone of \(\Sigma\). Such maps exist.
For any finite family of admissible maps \(Q_i\), including
any two distinct ones, there are boxes \(P_i\) about \(Q_iw\),
with \(Q_iw\in\operatorname{int}(P_i)\), for which
\[
 C_i=(Q_it|_Z)^{-1}(P_i),\qquad
 \psi_i=f^{Q_i}:C_i\longrightarrow\mathbb T_{P_i}
                  \quad\hbox{is norm-admissible finite}.
 \tag{11}\label{gci:constructedcollars}
\]
The boxes may be chosen inside any prescribed real
neighbourhoods of their centres.

Every projection has the same \emph{entire} central analytic
Gauss set, namely
\[
 \psi_i^{-1}(\eta_{Q_iw})
       = S:=\{x\in F:r_f(x)=d\},\qquad 1\leq |S|<\infty .
 \tag{12}\label{gci:intrinsicset}
\]
All points of \(S\) are absolutely interior in \(Z\).
The full pointed fans at these points admit a common
subdivision on whose top-cone spans every \(Q_i\) is injective.
Thus any pair of these collars satisfies the exact hypotheses
of the independently reviewed \Dep{mso:setup}.
For any finite \(\mathcal O(Z)\)-module the reviewed
\Dep{mso:unionoverlap} and \Dep{mso:sectorcomparison} apply.

The saturation in (11) is in \(Z\).
It is also saturation in the original \(X\), after shrinking
the \(P_i\) if needed, \emph{if and only if}
\[
        Q_iw\notin
          \overline{\,Q_it(X\setminus Z)\,}
                              \quad\hbox{for every }i.
 \tag{13}\label{gci:originalcompletion}
\]
Without (13), no completeness assertion over \(X\) is made
for the projected collars.
Nevertheless the original moment fibre \(F\), and every
original moment fibre with value in \(W\), is retained in
its entirety by (10).
\end{theorem}

On each interval of a finite affine subdivision the slope is constant.
Continuity of the derivative makes adjacent slopes equal. Hence a
\(C^1\) piecewise-affine function on such a subdivision is affine, and
cannot have distinct tail slopes \(-m\) and \(0\) when \(m>0\).

\(U_i=T_i\) and the standard generic identification. In the finite

\(\max(1,|T_i|)^{-m_i}\): it is one on \(|T_i|\le1\), and on the
reciprocal unit chart the frame \(T_i^{m_i}\) has norm one. Thus the
profile is \(m_i\max(0,-t_i)\). The mixed model measure is
\(D\delta_{\zeta_0}\), with \(\bar t(\zeta_0)=0\). Its evaluation

Consequently, for m>0m>0 it cannot also have the two different tail slopes −m-m and 00 in [eq:tails]. Thus the positive-degree finite piecewise-affine toric model profiles do not lie in the smooth fixed-torus-profile class above.

\begin{proposition}[Why a model profile cannot be treated piecewise]
\label{f9tm:modelobstruction}
A continuous function on $\mathbf R$ which is affine on a finite
polyhedral subdivision and is $C^1$ is affine. Consequently, for
$m>0$ it cannot also have the two different tail slopes $-m$ and $0$
in \eqref{eq:tails}. Thus the positive-degree finite piecewise-affine
toric model profiles do not lie in the smooth fixed-torus-profile
class above.

For the product model $(\mathbf P^1_{K^\circ})^d$ with the standard
model metrics on $L_i$, the profiles are
$\phi_i^{\rm mod}(t)=m_i\max(0,-t)$. The Chambert--Loir model-measure
formula in this explicit reduced model gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:modelmeasure}
 \mu_{\rm CL}^{\rm mod}=D\,\delta_{\zeta_0},\qquad
 \int u_F\,d\mu_{\rm CL}^{\rm mod}=D F(0)
 \quad\bigl(F\in C(\overline{\mathbf R}^{,d})\bigr),
\end{equation}
where $\zeta_0$ is the unit-radius Gauss point of $T^\an$.
In contrast, discarding the corners and using the ordinary Hessians
on the affine pieces gives the zero density. It fails to reproduce
\eqref{eq:modelmeasure}, even for a compactly supported smooth radial
test equal to one near the origin.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Take the two copies of the same \(R\)-product model, first with the
standard coordinates \(U_i=T_i\), and second with coordinates
\(U_i=S_i\) and specified identification \(T_i=1+\pi S_i\), where
\(0<|\pi|=r<1\). This generic isomorphism is defined over \(K\),
extends to the coordinate projective lines, and preserves \(\infty\).
In particular the two model lines extend the same generic line
\(L_i\) in each factor. Lemma~\ref{f9-batch-b:reduced-product-model-mass}
on the first model gives \(\mu_0=D\delta_\zeta\) for the \(T\)-Gauss
point \(\zeta\). On the second actual model it gives
\(\mu_1=D\delta_\xi\) for the transported \(S\)-Gauss point \(\xi\).
The relative nefness argument of that lemma applies on each of these
models and gives both collections of semipositive metrics.

By the finite polynomial Gauss calculation,
\[
 |T_i(\zeta)|=|T_i(\xi)|=1,\qquad
 |(T_i-1)(\zeta)|=1,\qquad |(T_i-1)(\xi)|=r .
\]
Thus their radial vectors are both \(0\), both mixed measures have
mass \(D\), and the measures are distinct. More explicitly the
function
\begin{equation}\label{eq:separator}
  g=\frac{|T_1-1|}{\max(1,|T_1|)}
\end{equation}
extends continuously to the projective product by \(1\) on the first
infinity divisor. It is already \(1\) when \(|T_1|>1\). Its two integrals differ by
\(D(1-r)>0\). The standard metric is toric. For the translated
model the finite frame weight in the \(T_i\)-coordinate is
\(m_i\log\max(1,|(T_i-1)/\pi|)\), because \(S_i=(T_i-1)/\pi\)
and the frame is unchanged under this generic identification.
Its values at the two points of the same tropical fibre differ,
so it is not toric for the fixed \(T\)-coordinates.

Finally \(\eta=\delta_\xi-\delta_\zeta\) is a nonzero signed Radon
measure with zero radial pushforward. The existing smooth measure
\(\mu_\Gamma\) is the pushforward of \(W\,dt\) under the Gauss section
as in Theorem~\ref{f9fm:alltests}, and consequently gives zero mass
to \(\{\zeta\}\): the inverse image of that singleton under the
Gauss section is \(\{0\}\). Hence \(\mu_\Gamma+\eta\) has the same
smooth radial pushforward, has mass \(-1\) at \(\zeta\), and has a
different value on the bounded continuous separating function.
\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Same radial data, different model measures]
\label{f9fm:modelambiguity}
In every dimension $d\geq2$ and for the same $L_i$ as above, there are
two collections of semipositive algebraic model metrics whose mixed
Chambert--Loir measures $\mu_0,\mu_1$ satisfy
\[
 \bar t_*\mu_0=\bar t_*\mu_1=D\delta_0,\qquad
 \mu_0(X^\an)=\mu_1(X^\an)=D,\qquad\mu_0\ne\mu_1.
\]
The first collection is toric for the specified $T$-coordinates; the
second is a translated product model and is not toric for those
coordinates. Thus this is not a counterexample within the fixed toric
metric class or within the positive smooth-density hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{f9fm:radondetermination}.

Moreover, if positivity is dropped, even the smooth radial data $Wdt$
does not determine a signed Radon measure: one may add a nonzero signed
measure of zero tropical pushforward to $\mu_\Gamma$.
\end{proposition}

Use Theorem [v036:flatgermweight] now in dimension nn for the actual pure slab and its joint unit tuple, with projection Q⊕1Q\oplus1. The whole-level fibre after tensoring with its Gauss field is the same actual affine fibre of FCF_C at su,Qws_{u,Qw}: all its points satisfy the CC and slab inequalities, and both affinoid rebindings follow from the rational domain universal property and affine fibre base change. The rank is δC\delta_C, with no identification of the punctured Gauss field with the central one. Since the product tangent lattice is NC⊕ℤN_C\oplus\mathbb Z, its transverse index is eCe_C. The punctured weight is therefore mCm_C.

For any H<a<bH<a<b the actual slab image is in P0×[a,b]P_0\times[a,b]. All its top coefficients over relintC×(a,b)\operatorname{relint}C\times(a,b) are the ones just computed, and the missing boundaries of these cells belong to lower-dimensional strata. If P0P_0 has dimension less than dd, the tube inclusion puts the entire slab image in dimension less than nn, and both top chains vanish. proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Put \(d=n-1\). Apply both conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:tube}
to the actual quotient \(D=\mathcal M(A/(f))\) of H1, of
dimension \(d\), and to the actual units of H3. Fix the common
\(\rho>0\) and set \(H=-\log\rho\). The
\eqref{fnd:nag002795:whole-ordinary-tube} image inclusion and
\eqref{eq:boundarytube} absolute-boundary inclusion concern the
same strict tube. Use a finite common subdivision of \(P_0=t_g(D)\)
containing \(\Delta\) as a subcomplex by
Lemma~\ref{cand:polyhedralrefinementproduct}. Fix a \(d\)-cell
\(C\) and its saturated tangent lattice \(N_C\); its relative
interior misses \(\Delta\). Choose an integral projection
\(Q:\mathbb Z^N\to\mathbb Z^d\) injective on \(N_C\), and set
\(e_C=[\mathbb Z^d:Q(N_C)]\).

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{Finiteness on the whole projected fibre.}
The inverse image \(W_C=t_g^{-1}(C)\) is the actual affinoid
domain given by the finitely many monomial inequalities on
units defining \(C\), using the rational domain property in
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedrationaluniversal}. It is pure of
dimension \(n\) by Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:puritylocality}.
The map \(F_C=(g^Q,f)\) takes it to a compact polyannulus times
closed disc \(Z_0\) in the torus times the parameter line,
chosen with bounds strictly larger than needed for the image.
The disc radius is also strictly larger than \(\rho\), and
the torus bounds strictly enclose \(Q(C)\).
For \(w\in\operatorname{relint}C\) and \(u\) with
\(|T(u)|<\rho\) in the parameter line, let \(s=s_{u,Qw}\)
be the relative Gauss point above \(u\) with torus radii
\(e^{-(Qw)_i}\). The whole inverse image of \(s\) in \(W_C\)
is at \(g\)-weight \(w\), since \(Q\) is injective on the
affine span of \(C\). Its points have \(|f|<\rho\).
By \eqref{eq:boundarytube} every one lies in
\(\operatorname{Int}(V/K)\). A neighbourhood of \(w\) meets
\(P_0\) only in \(C\), since \(w\) is in the relative interior
of a top-dimensional cell of the finite complex.
By \eqref{fnd:nag002795:whole-ordinary-tube}, pulling back this
neighbourhood and intersecting with \(\{|f|<\rho\}\) gives an
ordinary neighbourhood of the entire fibre in \(V\) contained
in \(W_C\).
The domain-interior comparison of
Proposition~\ref{fnd:generaldomainordinaryinterior} and the
affinoid composition formula
Theorem~\ref{fnd:affinoidinteriorcompositionequality} put the
entire fibre in \(\operatorname{Int}(W_C/K)\), hence in
\(\operatorname{Int}(W_C/Z_0)\) for the actual map.

The compact relative boundary of \(W_C\to Z_0\) has image
missing \(s\), by openness of affinoid interior in
Proposition~\ref{fnd:affinoidinteriorcalculus}.
Choose an affinoid ordinary neighbourhood \(N_s\) of \(s\)
in \(Z_0\) disjoint from that image. Its entire inverse image
\(Y_s\) is an actual affinoid domain of \(W_C\) by
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizeddomainbasechange}. If the fibre is empty, one may take
\(N_s\) disjoint from the compact image of \(W_C\).
For a nonempty inverse image, the forward base-change limb
of Proposition~\ref{fnd:affinoidinteriorcalculus} makes
\(Y_s\to N_s\) boundaryless. Theorem~
\ref{fnd:affinoidboundarylessfinite} therefore makes this
actual whole inverse image finite with its canonical
finite-module topology.

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{A single rank through the rigid zero.}
The target \(N_s\) is a nonempty affinoid domain of
\(\mathbb A_K^{n,\mathrm{an}}\) and is pure and ordinary regular
by Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:puritylocality} and
Theorem~\ref{fnd:affinespacedomainregular}. The source \(Y_s\),
when nonempty, is pure of dimension \(n\); each of its
nonempty affinoid domains is an affinoid domain of \(V\) by
Proposition~\ref{fnd:generalnetdomaincalculus}, so H2 applies
to its actual algebra. The Gauss dimension calculation
Lemma~\ref{fnd:gaussvaluedfielddimension} and the tower formula
Lemma~\ref{fnd:valuedfielddimensioncalculus} give
\(d_K(s)=d+d_K(u)\ge n-1\).
Use Lemma~\ref{lem:finiteflat} on \(Y_s\to N_s\) to get a
locally free pushforward on an ordinary neighbourhood of
\(s\). In the empty case the rank is zero. The finite
base-change formula in Proposition~
\ref{fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange} identifies the rank
with the dimension of the entire \(\mathcal H(s)\)-fibre
algebra; hence the ranks agree wherever their computations
overlap.

The map \((u,w)\mapsto s_{u,Qw}\) on the product of the open
disc \(\{|T|<\rho\}\) with \(\operatorname{relint}C\) is continuous.
On Laurent polynomials its norm is the finite maximum
\(\max_I |a_I(u)|e^{-\langle I,Qw\rangle}\).
On a compact disc times a compact torus annulus containing
the evaluating points, Laurent polynomials are uniformly dense
in the indicated affinoid algebra, so the same continuity
holds on all analytic functions. The open disc is the increasing
union of closed discs containing zero. Each is connected:
its power-series algebra is integral, and an ordinary clopen
separation would give a nontrivial idempotent by the analytic
sheaf property. This works also for the trivial valuation.
The other factor is convex. Thus the rank on this section is a
single integer \(\delta_C\), including at \(u=0\).

\smallskip
\noindent\emph{The two full Gauss calculations.}
At the rigid parameter zero, base change first cuts out the
actual quotient by \(f\); then the Gauss fibre over the
horizontal point at \(Qw\) gives the rank \(\delta_C\).
The whole \(g\)-level in \(D\) at \(w\) lies in \(W_C\).
It is absolutely interior in \(D\): by the boundary-tube
bound every such point is interior in \(V\) and the closed
immersion \(D\to V\) is relatively interior by the finite quotient
case of Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedfinitealgebras}. Apply the
forward composition formula of
Proposition~\ref{fnd:affinoidinteriorcalculus}.
Near \(w\) the moment image of \(D\) lies in the affine span
of \(C\). Apply Theorem~\ref{v036:flatgermweight} in dimension
\(d\) to the actual pure \(D\) and the tuple \(g|_D\).
Its whole-level Gauss algebra is the same fibre: the
horizontal \(Qw\)-level inside \(W_C\) forces \(w\), and
the equality constraints are actual affinoid constraints
preserved under base change. The ordinary quotient by \(f\)
and the tensor with the Gauss field are the actual affine
fibre and finite tensor comparisons
of Theorem~\ref{fnd:allpointaffinoidfibres} and Proposition~
\ref{fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange}. In particular
\[
                     \delta_C=e_C\,m_C>0 .
\]
Here \(m_C\) is the structure weight of the full quotient
\(D\) on \(C\).

For \(\tau>H\) let \(u\) be the radius-\(e^{-\tau}\) Gauss
point on the parameter line. The iterated maximum formula
for Gauss norms is the joint Gauss norm of \((g^Q,f)\), over
its own completed residue field. Its whole fibre has
dimension \(\delta_C>0\); consequently \((w,\tau)\) occurs
in the actual moment image.
On any slab with both endpoints above \(H\) and \(\tau\)
strictly between them, the strict radial inequalities put each
point of the entire level in the ordinary interior of the slab in
\(V\). The boundary-tube bound also puts those points in
\(\operatorname{Int}(V/K)\), so domain interior and composition
give absolute interior in the slab. Near \((w,\tau)\)
the actual image lies in the affine span of \(C\times\mathbb R\)
by the ordinary tube inclusion. Use
Theorem~\ref{v036:flatgermweight} now in dimension \(n\) for
the actual pure slab and its joint unit tuple, with projection
\(Q\oplus1\). The whole-level fibre after tensoring with its
Gauss field is the same actual affine fibre of \(F_C\) at
\(s_{u,Qw}\): all its points satisfy the \(C\) and slab
inequalities, and both affinoid rebindings follow from the
rational domain universal property and affine fibre base
change. The rank is \(\delta_C\), with no identification of
the punctured Gauss field with the central one. Since the
product tangent lattice is \(N_C\oplus\mathbb Z\), its
transverse index is \(e_C\). The punctured weight is
therefore \(m_C\).

For any \(H<a<b\) the actual slab image is in
\(P_0\times[a,b]\). All its top coefficients over
\(\operatorname{relint}C\times(a,b)\) are the ones just
computed, and the missing boundaries of these cells belong
to lower-dimensional strata. The
\hyperref[fnd:nag002405:global-finite-module-chain-weights]{finite-chain
and weights clause} gives the required equality of
\(n\)-chains, including the closures of the top cells.
If \(P_0\) has dimension less than \(d\), the tube inclusion
puts the entire slab image in dimension less than \(n\),
and both top chains vanish. The construction of \(\rho\)
and the central subdivision preceded the choice of slab.
\end{proof}

statement.html: Under H1–H3, there is $H\in\RR$ such that, for every pair of real numbers H<a<bH<a<b, the actual annular domain V[a,b]={e−b≤|f|≤e−a}⊂VV_{[a,b]}=\{e^{-b}\leq|f|\leq e^{-a}\}\subset V has the following equality of integral nn-dimensional moment chains: $$\TT_{(g,f)}(\cO_{V_{[a,b]}}) =\TT_g(\cO_D)\times[a,b].$$ On the left the final coordinate is −log|f|-\log|f|; on the right the interval has the standard lattice $\ZZ$ and weight one. All weights of $\TT_g(\cO_D)$ are the full actual quotient weights. The same finite central complex works for every a,ba,b in this range. Equality is equality of top-dimensional calibrated chains; no assertion is made about persistence of every lower-dimensional stratum or about convergence in a test-space topology.
statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Uniform rigid-zero calibration; F8RC-P]
\label{thm:product}
Under H1--H3, there is \(H\in\RR\) such that, for every pair of real
numbers \(H<a<b\), the actual annular domain
\[
 V_{[a,b]}=\{e^{-b}\leq|f|\leq e^{-a}\}\subset V
\]
has the following equality of integral \(n\)-dimensional moment
chains:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:product}
 \TT_{(g,f)}(\cO_{V_{[a,b]}})
       =\TT_g(\cO_D)\times[a,b].
\end{equation}
On the left the final coordinate is \(-\log|f|\); on the right the
interval has the standard lattice \(\ZZ\) and weight one. All
weights of \(\TT_g(\cO_D)\) are the full actual quotient weights.
The same finite central complex works for every \(a,b\) in this
range. Equality is equality of top-dimensional calibrated chains;
no assertion is made about persistence of every lower-dimensional
stratum or about convergence in a test-space topology.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fixed-test support avoidance makes the left pairing the integral over
\(A_{\sigma,\tau}\). In \eqref{eq:green}, \(\dd u=0\). The first
boundary term is zero on both radial faces: \(d''\eta_1\) is zero

integral in \eqref{eq:sign}. Its minus sign in Green and its lower-face

and denominator, then subtract. Actual Cartier coefficients and
coherent-cycle integration are precisely the pending \tagg{F8ST-C}
and \tagg{F8ST-I} interfaces; they have not been replaced by point

\begin{proposition}[Conditional scalar reduction; F8RC-R]
\label{prop:conditional}
Under H1--H3, for an ordinary compact analytic-interior test satisfying
the representation and Green-symmetry scope above, R-GREEN implies
\[
       L_f(\dd\eta_1)=\int_D\eta.
\]
If smooth double integration by parts is available for the complementary
ordinary test \(\eta_2=\eta-\eta_1\), then
\(L_f(\dd\eta)=\int_D\eta\). Identification with the project Cartier
current, global finite-chart gluing, and extension to the full test class
require their own stated comparison interfaces.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The support of each differentiated form is contained in the support
of the original form. All products displayed therefore have compact
support. Leibniz gives
\[
 d'\Gamma=\alpha\wedge\dd\eta-\dd\alpha\wedge\eta
               +d'\alpha\wedge d''\eta+d''\alpha\wedge d'\eta.
\]
Let \(A=d'\alpha\wedge d''\eta\). Commutation with the exchange
involution gives
\(JA=(-1)^{p+q}d''\alpha\wedge d'\eta\).
On every \(n\)-dimensional tangential face, a top \((n,n)\)-form
satisfies \(JA=(-1)^nA\). On a lower-dimensional face it is zero.
Since \(p+q=n-1\), the two cross terms cancel as ordinary top forms.
Thus \(d'\Gamma\) is exactly the bulk integrand. Apply the proved
facet identity \eqref{eq:fullstokes}, not a zero-boundary version of
Stokes. The trace factorization in Theorem~\ref{thm:trace} identifies
its right side with the indicated ordinary boundary germs.
\end{proof}

Then $$\int_{X,\mathcal F}\bigl(\alpha\wedge\dd\eta-\dd\alpha\wedge\eta\bigr) =\BB_{X,\mathcal F}\bigl(\Gamma(\alpha,\eta)\bigr).$$ In particular, for an ordinary smooth scalar uu and symmetric (n−1,n−1)(n-1,n-1)-test η\eta of compact support, $$\int_{X,\mathcal F}u\,\dd\eta-\dd u\wedge\eta =\BB_{X,\mathcal F}(u\,d''\eta-d''u\wedge\eta).$$ The right side is evaluated on the full boundary trace r∂XΓr_{\partial X}\Gamma. statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Full Green identity; F8AG-G]
\label{fnd:nag002880:green}
Let \(\alpha\) and \(\eta\) be ordinary smooth forms of bidegrees
\((p,p)\) and \((q,q)\), with \(p+q=n-1\), satisfying
\(J\alpha=(-1)^p\alpha\), \(J\eta=(-1)^q\eta\). Suppose
\(\Supp\alpha\cap\Supp\eta\) is compact. Define the flux form
\[
        \Gamma(\alpha,\eta)=\alpha\wedge d''\eta-d''\alpha\wedge\eta.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}\label{fnd:nag002880:green-equation}
 \int_{X,\mathcal F}\bigl(\alpha\wedge\dd\eta-\dd\alpha\wedge\eta\bigr)
                     =\BB_{X,\mathcal F}\bigl(\Gamma(\alpha,\eta)\bigr).
\end{equation}
In particular, for an ordinary smooth scalar \(u\) and symmetric
\((n-1,n-1)\)-test \(\eta\) of compact support,
\begin{equation}\label{fnd:nag002880:scalar-green}
 \int_{X,\mathcal F}u\,\dd\eta-\dd u\wedge\eta
               =\BB_{X,\mathcal F}(u\,d''\eta-d''u\wedge\eta).
\end{equation}
The right side is evaluated on the full boundary trace
\(r_{\partial X}\Gamma\). It need not vanish when the test reaches
\(\partial_KX\).
\end{theorem}

statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Inherited boundary and radial trace functionals; F8AG-A]
\label{fnd:nag002887:radial-traces}
One has
\begin{equation}\label{fnd:nag002887:boundary-containment}
 \partial_KA\subset (A\cap\partial_KV)\cup E_a\cup E_b.
\end{equation}
Equality is not asserted: a level set can contain points where the
inequality is locally redundant. If an ordinary
\(\beta\in\cA^{n-1,n}(A)\) vanishes near \(A\cap\partial_KV\),
choose smooth real functions \(\psi_a,\psi_b\) equal to one near
the respective endpoint and zero near the other, with disjoint small
endpoint collars. Then
\[
 T_a(\beta)=\BB_A(\psi_a(x)\beta),\qquad
 T_b(\beta)=\BB_A(\psi_b(x)\beta)
\]
are independent of these choices, and
\begin{equation}\label{fnd:nag002887:two-traces}
                         \BB_A(\beta)=T_a(\beta)+T_b(\beta).
\end{equation}
They depend only on the actual germs at the indicated end, within
this inherited-boundary-vanishing class. Without that vanishing
hypothesis, only the full trace is being declared intrinsic here;
one must retain the other boundary contribution for a chosen splitting.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Apply the \hyperref[fnd:nag002893:product-chart]{weighted product formula}
to the actual \(A,\mathcal F,h\) and the stated representative. It gives
the full expression \eqref{eq:productboundary}, with all the given
weights and saturated normal indices. The same result gives zero
lateral term when \(\beta\) vanishes near the inherited boundary.

Assume this vanishing and use the two selectors of
Proposition~\ref{fnd:nag002887:radial-traces} on this same annulus.

\((1-\psi_a(x)-\psi_b(x))\beta\) has the same vanishing.
By \eqref{fnd:nag002887:boundary-containment}, all three sections
have support disjoint from the actual absolute boundary
\(\partial_K A\). Each support is closed in the compact \(A\), hence
compact in \(\operatorname{Int}(A/K)\). They are ordinary
\((n-1,n)\)-forms with the same coefficient sheaf \(\mathcal F\).

\hyperref[f7gg:global]{true-interior Stokes} to each of these
\(d'\)-tests. The two differences give zero trace, proving
independence of the two selectors, and the complement gives
\(\BB_A(\beta)=T_a(\beta)+T_b(\beta)\). Dependence only on the actual
ordinary germs at the respective ends is the
\hyperref[fnd:nag002887:radial-traces]{germ assertion} on this same
inherited-boundary-vanishing class.

For the lower end, the form \(\psi_a(x)\beta\) is represented on
the same joint chart by \(\psi_a(x)\widetilde\beta\). Apply the
\hyperref[fnd:nag002893:product-chart]{product formula at the lower end}
to this section. Its lateral term is zero, since its inherited
boundary germ is still zero. The scalar in the radial contraction
at \(c'\) is \(\psi_a(c')\), so the upper term is zero and
\(T_a(\beta)=-\int_P R_a\widetilde\beta\).
Apply the \hyperref[fnd:nag002893:product-chart]{product formula at the upper end}
to \(\psi_b(x)\beta\) with representative \(\psi_b(x)\widetilde\beta\).
Again the lateral term is zero. The lower scalar is now zero and the
upper one is one, giving \(T_b(\beta)=+\int_P R_b\widetilde\beta\).

they are the full ordinary trace of the selected forms and depend
only on the respective end germs. This also gives the same values for
any representatives of those ordinary germs to which the stated
product formula applies.
\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Horizontal profile with both ends; F8AG-H]
\label{prop:profile}
Under CP, suppose
\(\eta=\chi(x)t_g^*\alpha\), where \(\alpha\) is a symmetric smooth
\((n-1,n-1)\)-form on the horizontal image and \(\chi\) is smooth
near \([a,b]\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:profile}
 \int_{A,\mathcal F}x\,\dd\eta
  =\left[(x\chi'(x)-\chi(x))\right]_{a}^{b}\int_P\alpha.
\end{equation}
This is the full Green identity for this profile. No inherited-boundary
vanishing is needed: its lateral flux is zero by tangential degree.
In particular, if \(\chi=1\) near \(a\) and \(\chi=0\) near \(b\),
the right side is \(+\int_P\alpha\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write \(K_0\) for the compact carrier in the statement. First
suppose \(J\eta=(-1)^{n-1}\eta\). By the ordinary moment-sheaf
Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:germsheaf}, choose a finite cover of
\(K_0\) by ordinary interiors of affinoid domains \(V_i\) in
the open region of regularity of \(f\) and purity of \(D\).
Write \(\eta=t_{g_i}^*\alpha_i\) on \(V_i\), and symmetrize
the ambient representatives using \(J\). Their ordinary sections
are unchanged. Put \(Q=\bigcup_i V_i\) and
\(V_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}V_i\) for nonempty index sets \(I\).
The intersections are actual affinoid domains by
Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:separatedintersections}; the nonempty ones
are pure of dimension \(n\) by Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:puritylocality}.
The corresponding zero subspace is
\[
    D_I=\mathcal M\bigl(\mathcal O(V_I)/(f|_{V_I})\bigr).
\]
Indeed the actual quotient of Corollary~
\ref{fnd:generalizedaffinoidquotients} base changes to this quotient
by Proposition~\ref{fnd:generalizedfinitebasechange}. By the actual
domain base-change property
Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizeddomainbasechange}, it is an
affinoid domain of \(D\); it is pure of dimension \(n-1\) when
nonempty. No reduction replaces this closed subspace. Choose one
of the presenting tuples on each intersection and restrict it and
its representative there.

Apply the actual products supplied by hypothesis (ii) for
these \(V_I,D_I\) and the chosen tuples. With
Theorem~\ref{thm:product}, this input is available for each
nonempty \(D_I\) when that intersection satisfies H1--H3.
If the product is supplied directly, use precisely that hypothesis.
Choose a single positive small-tube bound \(\rho\) over the
finitely many chosen products. When \(D_I\) is empty, compactness
gives a positive minimum of \(|f|\) on \(V_I\); take \(\rho\)
small enough to make its tube empty. The frozen estimate with
coordinate \(-\log|f|\) transfers to \(x=\log|f|\) on each actual
annular piece by reflection of the interval and by the unit tuple
using \(f^{-1}\). The lattice reflection is unimodular. At generic top weights
outside the boundary image, the
whole fibre is interior by Theorem~\ref{v037:globaltrop:finiteimage}.
In Theorem~\ref{v036:flatgermweight} choose the transverse
projection for the reflected coordinates by composing the
original one with the reflection. This gives the same projected
unit functions, the same actual Gauss algebra and the same
index. The interval retains weight one.

Choose \(b<\log\rho\), so the reflected slab \([-b,-a]\)
will be in the calibrated range. Let \(\chi\) be smooth, equal to one on
a sufficiently far left ray, and zero on \(x\ge b_0\), where
\(b_0<b\). The function \(\chi(\log|f|)\) extends by one near
\(D\), since it is already locally constant there. Set
\(\eta_1=\chi(\log|f|)\eta\), \(\eta_2=\eta-\eta_1\).
The fixed-test result Proposition~\ref{prop:log} applies to
\(d''\eta_1\) and \(\dd\eta_1\) of bidegrees \((n-1,n)\) and
\((n,n)\). Each has compact support disjoint from \(D\).
Thus we may choose a single \(a<b_0\) so low that \(\chi=1\)
near \(a\) and the derivatives have support disjoint from
\(\{x\le a\}\) and a neighbourhood of \(D\).
The terms are also zero near \(x\ge b\) by the upper cutoff.

On the actual affinoid intersections
\(A_I=V_I\cap\{e^a\le |f|\le e^b\}\), the chosen unit chart
has the supplied product with horizontal chain
\(\mathcal T_{g_i}(\mathcal O_{D_I})\).
The fixed-profile identity in Proposition~\ref{prop:profile}
applies with the structure sheaf and the restricted \(\alpha_i\).
The upper end expression is zero; the lower end expression
\(a\chi'(a)-\chi(a)\) is \(-1\). The lateral term vanishes by
the horizontal primed degree of this particular profile.
Consequently
\[
                 \int_{A_I}x\,\dd\eta_1=\int_{D_I}\eta.
\]
Both sides are zero in the empty case. On the right the
single-chart integral uses the actual quotient structure sheaf.
On the left the profile has used the full facet value, including
both radial ends.

Use the finite-cover signs \((-1)^{|I|+1}\).
The annular domains \(A_i\) intersect in the indicated \(A_I\),
so the compact finite-chart formula of
Theorem~\ref{v037:integration:compactintegral} identifies the
left sum with the integral on their union. The support lies in
the ordinary interior of this union: the carriers contained an
ordinary neighbourhood of \(K_0\) and the radial bounds are
strict on the support of the derivative. The comparison of
Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:compactintegral} and the definition
in Proposition~\ref{prop:log} give \(L_f(\dd\eta_1)\).
On \(D\), the domains \(D_i\) contain an ordinary neighbourhood
of the restricted support in their union. The same compact
formula with the structure module and all the actual quotient
intersections gives \(\int_D\eta\).

For the complementary term, the support of \(\eta_2\) lies
in \(K_0\subset\operatorname{Int}(X/K)\) and is disjoint
from \(D\): \(1-\chi\) vanishes on a strict small tube.

smooth forms on the unit locus, with compact support in the
same true interior, and extend by zero across open regions
disjoint from their supports. The two assertions of
Theorem~\ref{f7gg:global} apply respectively in bidegrees
\((n-1,n)\) and \((n,n-1)\). Their Leibniz expansions give
\[
 \int d'x\wedge d''\eta_2+\int x\,\dd\eta_2=0,\qquad
 -\int \dd x\wedge\eta_2-\int d'x\wedge d''\eta_2=0.

\((-1)^n\) by Definition~\ref{v037:integration:conventions}
and vanishes on smaller faces. The ordinary top derivative
of the opposite part is therefore zero. Both pairings vanish

\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Conditional finite-cover scalar identity; F8AG-P]
\label{thm:application}
Let \(X\) be good, Hausdorff, and pure of dimension \(n\), let \(f\)
be regular analytic near a compact set \(K\subset\Int(X/K)\), and
let \(\eta\) be an ordinary \((n-1,n-1)\)-test supported in \(K\).
Suppose the actual zero space \(D\) is empty or pure of dimension
\(n-1\) near \(K\). Assume the following separately identified inputs:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item fixed-test support avoidance and the scalar logarithmic pairing
of the unchanged \tagg{F8RC-L} candidate;
\item on the finite affinoid intersections used below, the actual
calibrated product assertion \tagg{F8RC-P}, with \(P_I=\TT_{g_i}(\cO_{D_I})\);
\item R-F7 for the complementary test away from \(D\).
\end{enumerate}
Then the proposed primary identity is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:PL}
               L_f(\dd\eta)=\int_D\eta,
\end{equation}
with the full actual quotient integration. The annular Green and
finite-cover cancellation used in this implication are proved above;
they are no longer additional black-box premises of the implication.
Inputs (i)--(ii) remain under independent audit, and this theorem does
not mark them, or general PL, as admitted. To invoke (ii) by the
submitted rigid-zero theorem, its affinoid-domain \(S_1\) hypothesis
must also hold; the separately reviewed \tagg{F8ST-A} supplies it
from intrinsic analytic \(S_1\) in the exact good-space scope. A
regular nonunit is not used to infer \(S_1\).
\end{theorem}
