\begin{proof}
We first establish the finiteness used to isolate a point. For an analytic
map $\psi:X\to(\mathbf G_{m,K}^d)^{\rm an}$ and its target Gauss point
$\eta_s$, the analytic fibre is an affinoid over
$H_s=\mathcal H(\eta_s)$, after choosing a compact target polyannulus.
The actual fibre theorem \Dep{fnd:allpointaffinoidfibres}, the Gauss
residual dimension \Dep{fnd:gaussvaluedfielddimension}, the tower formula
\Dep{fnd:valuedfielddimensioncalculus}, and the Abhyankar maximum
\Dep{fnd:affinoidabhyankarmaximum} give, for every point $y$ of that fibre,
\[
 0\leq d_{H_s}(y)=d_K(y)-d_K(\eta_s)\leq d-d=0.
\]
The fibre has analytic dimension zero. Such an affinoid has finitely many
points: simultaneously strictify, preserve dimension, use strict finite
normalization in dimension zero, and project the finite spectrum
surjectively back. The exact inputs are
\Dep{fnd:simultaneousstrictification},
\Dep{fnd:analyticdimensionindependence},
\Dep{fnd:strictfinitenormalization}, \Dep{fnd:stricttatedimension},
\Dep{fnd:strictfinitealgebras}, \Dep{fnd:finiteanalyticbranchseparation},
and \Dep{fnd:scalarextensionspectralsurjective}.
This proves finiteness of the Gauss fibre as a set; it does not assert
finiteness over an ordinary target neighbourhood.

For $x\in S_w$, a $d$-element subset of the initial forms of the $f_i(x)$
is algebraically independent over $\widetilde K^{\rm gr}$.
For the corresponding $d$-coordinate projection, every Laurent polynomial
has its Gauss value at $x$: cancellation of its terms of maximal size
would be a nonzero homogeneous relation on those initial forms.
Density gives the same assertion for the exact-radius Laurent algebra.
Consequently $x$ maps to its Gauss point. There are finitely many
$d$-coordinate subsets and finitely many points in each such fibre.
This proves that $S_w$ is finite.

If $r_f(x)<d$, the pointed upper bound
\Dep{v038:pointed:pointedupper} gives an ordinary affinoid $Y_0$ whose
moment-image germ has dimension less than $d$. All smaller domains have
zero $d$-chain germ. Suppose now $r_f(x)=d$ and choose $Y_0$ excluding the
other members of $S_w$. Fix one $U\subset Y_0$ as in the statement. The set
\[
 C=F_w(Y_0)\setminus\operatorname{Int}_{\rm top}(U,Y_0)
\]
is compact and contains no point of graded rank $d$. For each $y\in C$
the same pointed upper bound supplies an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood
$V_y\subset Y_0$ whose moment-image germ at $w$ is contained in a finite
rational fan of dimension $r_f(y)<d$. Finitely many ordinary interiors of
these $V_y$ cover $C$. The compact set
\[
 Y_0\setminus\bigl(\operatorname{Int}_{\rm top}(U,Y_0)
            \cup\textstyle\bigcup_y\operatorname{Int}_{\rm top}(V_y,Y_0)\bigr)
\]
has moment image avoiding $w$. Shrinking a real ball about $w$ therefore
shows that every fibre outside the finite union of the lower-dimensional
fans is wholly contained in $\operatorname{Int}_{\rm top}(U,Y_0)$.

Here is the step that permits a central boundary point. The actual boundary
images $t(\partial_KY_0)$ and $t(\partial_KU)$ are finite polyhedral sets
of dimension at most $d-1$, by \Dep{v037:globaltrop:finiteimage}.
Their germs at $w$ are finite rational fans, or are empty. Add these germs
to the exceptional union and shrink the ball. All remaining whole fibres
are analytically interior in both sources. For finitely many $U_i$ take
the union of their exceptional fans and the minimum radius. This proves
\eqref{bdg:eqfibres}. The radius and exceptional fan may depend on this
finite list; no uniform assertion over all neighbourhoods is needed.

Take a common finite subdivision of the actual moment images, the
boundary images, and the exceptional fans. In the relative interior of
each relevant $d$-cell the image germ is contained in one affine
$d$-plane. The entire fibres in $Y_0$ and $U$ are the same and are interior.
The restriction clause of \Dep{v037:degree:moduleweight} identifies their
weights, using the same full fibre algebra and the same saturated lattice.
Weights on this dense set determine the $d$-chain germ. Thus
\eqref{bdg:eqgerm} is independent of $U$, and of a different initial
$Y_0$ by taking a common ordinary affinoid neighbourhood. The additivity
and integrality follow from the frozen chain and module-weight theorem.

For \eqref{bdg:eqsum}, choose pairwise disjoint ordinary affinoid
neighbourhoods $U_x$ for all $x\in S_w$, small enough to compute their
cofinal germs. The compact remainder of $F_w(X)$ has rank less than $d$.
Apply exactly the finite-cover argument just given, and also exclude the
images of $\partial_KX$ and all $\partial_KU_x$. Outside a finite
$(d-1)$-dimensional exceptional germ, the \emph{whole original} fibre
$F_v(X)$ is the disjoint union of the $F_v(U_x)$ and all are interior.
The sheaf comparison identifies its actual algebra with the product of
their actual algebras. On generic $d$-cells choose a common admissible
projection. Finite Gauss dimensions add over this product, including
all module factors; division by the common lattice index gives
\eqref{bdg:eqsum}. If $S_w$ is empty the same argument gives zero.

For \eqref{bdg:eqpush}, work on one ordinary affinoid neighbourhood
\(U\) small enough to compute both cofinal germs. It is pure of
dimension \(d\), its two restricted tuples consist of units, and both
chains use \(M_U\). Let \(a\) and \(c\) denote projection from the
joint coordinates \((f,g)\) to the first and second blocks,
respectively. By \mbox{\hyperref[fnd:nag002405:same-affinoid-coordinate-augmentation]{same-affinoid augmentation}},
\(a_*\mathcal T_{(f,g)|U}(M_U)=\mathcal T_{f|U}(M_U)\).
Apply \mbox{\hyperref[fnd:nag002405:same-affinoid-coordinate-augmentation]{the same augmentation}}
with \(g\) as the original tuple and \(f\) as the adjoined tuple.
Swapping the coordinate blocks just relabels the full fibres. At a
generic \(d\)-cell, composing a transverse integral projection with the
inverse block swap preserves the projected monomials and the index of
the saturated tangent lattice. The
\mbox{\hyperref[v037:degree:moduleweight]{generic module weights}}
are therefore unchanged, giving
\(c_*\mathcal T_{(f,g)|U}(M_U)=\mathcal T_{g|U}(M_U)\).

The joint image is the graph of \(v\mapsto b+Lv\) over the
\(f\)-image. If \(V_\sigma\) is the tangent space of a \(d\)-cell
of the \(f\)-image and \(N_\sigma=V_\sigma\cap\mathbf Z^n\),
the saturated lattice on its graph is
\(\{(u,Lu):u\in N_\sigma\}\), because \(L\) is integral.
Thus \(a\) identifies the graph lattice with \(N_\sigma\) with
index one. On this graph \(c=b+L\circ a\). On cells where \(L\)
has rank \(d\), projection by \(c\) has the usual index
\([N_\tau:L(N_\sigma)]\). Cells where the rank drops give no
\(d\)-dimensional term. The two applications give the global identity
\((b+L)_*\mathcal T_{f|U}(M_U)=\mathcal T_{g|U}(M_U)\). We justify passage to germs, since arbitrary global
pushforward does not automatically commute with taking a germ.
Choose an initial such neighbourhood $Y$ and a small real ball about
$w$ on which its finite moment image is its conical germ. Shrink ordinarily
to $U\subset Y$ with $t(U)$ in that ball. Every $d$-cell of $t(U)$ lies
in one of finitely many affine $d$-planes $w+V_\sigma$ of this germ.
For the planes on which $L$ has rank $d$, there is $c>0$, common to this
finite list, such that
\[
 \|L(v-w)\|\geq c\|v-w\|\qquad(v-w\in V_\sigma).
\]
Thus any non-collapsed source cell contributing at target weights tending
to $b+Lw$ has its source weights tending to $w$. Rank-dropping cells
have no $d$-pushforward term. In a sufficiently small target ball the
global chain identity on $U$ consequently computes exactly the
pushforward of the source germ. This proves \eqref{bdg:eqpush}, with
multiplicity $[N_\tau:L(N_\sigma)]$ on each non-collapsed cone over
$\tau$. No finite analytic map at the central point was used.
\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Whole-fibre overlap away from boundary walls]
\label{bdg:cofinalboundary}
For every $x\in X$, with $w=t(x)$, there is an ordinary affinoid
neighbourhood $Y_0$ of $x$ such that the germs
\[
 C_{x,f}(M):=[\mathcal T_{f|U}(M_U)]_w
 \tag{B1}\label{bdg:eqgerm}
\]
are independent of the ordinary affinoid neighbourhood $U\subset Y_0$.
They are nonnegative integral $d$-fan germs and are additive in $M$.
They vanish if $r_f(x)<d$; they may also vanish when $r_f(x)=d$.
No interior assumption on $x$ is made.

More precisely, if $r_f(x)=d$, one can choose $Y_0$ with
$S_w\cap Y_0=\{x\}$. For every finite list $U_1,\ldots,U_a\subset Y_0$
of ordinary affinoid neighbourhoods of $x$, there are $\epsilon>0$ and a
finite rational fan germ $E$ at $w$, of dimension at most $d-1$, such that
for $v\in B_\epsilon(w)\setminus E$,
\[
 F_v(Y_0)=F_v(U_i)\subset
 \operatorname{Int}_{\rm top}(U_i,Y_0)\cap\operatorname{Int}(Y_0/K)
                         \cap\operatorname{Int}(U_i/K)\quad(1\leq i\leq a).
 \tag{B2}\label{bdg:eqfibres}
\]
Empty fibres are allowed. These are entire fibres in the indicated source.

For every $w$ the set $S_w$ is finite and the original source chain satisfies
\[
 [\mathcal T_f(M)]_w=\sum_{x\in S_w}C_{x,f}(M).
 \tag{B3}\label{bdg:eqsum}
\]
Finally let $L:\mathbf Z^n\to\mathbf Z^m$ be integral and let
$g_j=c_j\prod_i f_i^{L_{ji}}$, where $c_j\in K^\times$.
Writing $b_j=-\log|c_j|$, one has, for \emph{every} $x\in X$,
\[
 (b+L)_*C_{x,f}(M)=C_{x,g}(M).
 \tag{B4}\label{bdg:eqpush}
\]
Thus the directional weights are intrinsic under admissible projections,
with the usual saturated-lattice pushforward indices, including at boundary
points. This statement is about weighted fans, not finite maps through $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Simultaneous directional collars and full Gauss degrees]
\label{bdg:directionalcollars}
Let $x$ have $r_f(x)=d$, choose $Y_0,U_1,\ldots,U_a$ as in
Theorem~\ref{bdg:cofinalboundary}, and let $\sigma$ be a $d$-cone of
$C_{x,f}(A)$ in a common refinement with $C_{x,f}(M)$, with lattice
$N=N_\sigma$. Suppose
$Q_1,\ldots,Q_b:\mathbf Z^n\to\mathbf Z^d$ are integral and injective
on $N$. Refine $\sigma-w$ by a finite rational fan. In every resulting
full-dimensional open sector $\Omega\subset N_{\mathbf R}$ avoiding the exceptional walls,
and at every sufficiently small noncentral $v\in w+\Omega$, the
following assertions hold.

The fibres $F_v(Y_0)=F_v(U_i)$ are entire and interior, and their common
image germ is an affine $d$-plane. Let $D_v$ be their actual algebra,
$R_{j,v}$ the exact-radius polytorus algebra at $Q_jv$, and $H_{j,v}$
its Gauss field. Then $R_{j,v}\to D_v$ is norm-admissible finite. Set
\[
 E_{j,v}=D_v\widehat\otimes_{R_{j,v}}H_{j,v},\quad
 e_j=[\mathbf Z^d:Q_j(N)],\quad P_{j,v}=M_{Y_0}\otimes_{A_{Y_0}}E_{j,v}.
\]
The weight of $M$ in this sector is
\begin{align}
 m_\sigma(M)&=\frac{\dim_{H_{j,v}}P_{j,v}}{e_j}
 =\frac{1}{e_j}\sum_{z\in\mathcal M(E_{j,v})}
 \operatorname{length}_{E_{j,v,z}}P_{j,v,z}\,
             [\mathcal H(z):H_{j,v}]\label{bdg:eqdegree}\\
 &=\frac1{e_j}\sum_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Min}(A_{Y_0})}
 \operatorname{length}_{(A_{Y_0})_{\mathfrak p}}(M_{Y_0})_{\mathfrak p}
             \dim_{H_{j,v}}(E_{j,v}/\mathfrak pE_{j,v}).\nonumber
\end{align}
It is independent of $j$, $v$ in the sector, and the listed source
neighbourhoods. Full field degrees, including inseparable degrees, and
all Artinian and generic lengths occur in this formula.

There also exists a full-dimensional closed rational parallelotope $W$
in the affine plane of the sector, with $v\in\operatorname{relint}(W)$
and $W\subset w+\Omega$, such that the \emph{same actual domain}
\[
 Z=t^{-1}(W)\cap Y_0=t^{-1}(W)\cap U_i
\]
is finite, with canonical norms, over the toric affinoid
$\mathbb T_{Q_jW}$ under $f^{Q_j}$ for every $j$.
These are full inverse images under $t$ in $Y_0$ at all weights of $W$.
They need not be full inverse images under $Q_jt$ in $Y_0$: other original
weights may have the same projected weight.
Such collars approach $w$ through the retained sectors; no extension
of a collar or its factor idempotents to $w$ is asserted.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proposition}[Graded rank and central Gauss degree do not supply directions]
\label{bdg:rankobstruction}
The following two examples show why a boundary fan formula must be
separated from a central finite-neighbourhood assertion.

First, over a trivially valued complete $K$, choose a $K$-free polyradius
$r=(r_1,\ldots,r_d)$ and let
\[
 X_0=\mathcal M(K\{r^{-1}T,rT^{-1}\})=\mathcal M(K_r),\quad
 f=(T_1,\ldots,T_d),\quad w=-\log r.
\]
Then $X_0=\{x\}$, it is pure of analytic dimension $d$, and
$r_f(x)=d$, but $x\in\partial_KX_0$ and $C_{x,f}(K_r)=0$.
For every nonsingular integral $Q$ the actual projected Gauss algebra is
$K_r$ of degree $|\det Q|$ over its target Gauss field. Its quotient by
$[\mathbf Z^d:Q\mathbf Z^d]$ is $1$, although the weighted $d$-fan is zero.
With the redundant tuple $(T_1,\ldots,T_d,1)$, injectivity on every actual
$d$-face is vacuous: both the projection selecting the first $d$
coordinates and that selecting $(T_1,\ldots,T_{d-1},1)$ have matrix
rank $d$, but their projected graded ranks are $d$ and $d-1$.

Second, over a nontrivially valued $K$, choose $0<\rho<1$ in $|K^\times|$.
Let $X=\{\rho\leq|T|\leq1\}$, $X'=\{|T|=1\}$, and $f=T$.
At the unit Gauss point $\eta$, both sources have graded rank $1$ and the
same completed residue field. For $T\mapsto T^q$, $q\ne0$, their actual
Gauss local degree is $|q|$. Nevertheless
\[
 C_{\eta,f}(\mathcal O_X)=[\mathbf R_{\geq0}]\ \text{with weight }1,
 \qquad C_{\eta,f}(\mathcal O_{X'})=0.
 \tag{B5}\label{bdg:eqcut}
\]
The inclusion $X'\hookrightarrow X$ is an analytic-domain cut, not an
ordinary neighbourhood at $\eta$. Its map to the ambient torus is not
finite at $\eta$ in the sense of finite maps between ordinary analytic
neighbourhoods. Thus a finite analytic Gauss fibre and maximal graded
rank do not imply a central finite collar.
\end{proposition}

\(J\eta=(-1)^{n-1}\eta\). Use Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}. Replace each

\[

\(\log\min_{V_I}|f|\), so both sides are empty or zero. There are
finitely many intersections, so choose one real upper bound \(B\)
that works for all of them. Fix \(b_0<b<B\) and a smooth \(\chi\)

     =\bigl[ x\chi'(x)-\chi(x)\bigr]_a^b\int_{P_I}\alpha_i
     =\int_{D_I}\eta.

Its upper radial value is zero and its lower radial value is minus one.
IH includes all faces; its lateral flux vanishes by horizontal exterior

Gauss module multiplicity and lattice index in \(P_I\) are unchanged.

Multiply \eqref{eq:piece} by \((-1)^{|I|+1}\) and sum. The annuli
are exactly the intersections of the actual domains \(A_i(a,b)\).
Frozen integral inclusion--exclusion \tagg{NAG-002416} identifies the
left sum with the integral on their union, even if that union is not

\begin{proof}
The test is identically zero near zero and outside its compact annular
collar, so ordinary zero extension is valid. In coordinate
\(v=\log|T|+m\), the annulus has lattice weight one: its identity
moment map has Gauss degree and lattice index one. Frozen integration
is the ordinary real integral. The first value is
\(\int(v-m)\varphi''(v)\,dv=0\). For the second, the constant
term integrates to zero, while
\[
 \int\max(v,0)\varphi''(v)\,dv
       =\int_0^{1/4}v\varphi''(v)\,dv=\varphi(0)=1.
\]
All coefficients here are continuous on a compact interval and are
integrable by the frozen grid construction \tagg{NAG-002389}; no
measurable extension is assumed. For each fixed \(m\), cuts deeper
than \(m+1/4\) do agree with the logarithm on the support. Choosing
\(m\) arbitrarily large disproves a uniform threshold.
\end{proof}

proved above and uniqueness of finite signed Radon measures give

\( |\nu|(E)=\sup\sum_j|\nu(E_j)|\), the supremum over finite Borel
partitions of \(E\). If \(\nu=\nu^+-\nu^-\) with finite positive
measures, this supremum is at most \(\nu^+(E)+\nu^-(E)\).

disjoint decomposition proves the subadditive inequality; combining

Thus all variations here are finite. The triangle inequality on
every finite partition gives the variation inequality for a finite
sum. A closed embedding identifies the Borel sigma-algebra of its

\( |(i_i)_*\nu|=(i_i)_*|\nu|\). These facts prove

proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
First let \(X\) be affinoid. Proposition~\ref{fnd:nag002966:component-support} makes
\(\eta_i=i_i^*\eta\) an admissible compact interior test on \(X_i\),
with \(\dd\eta_i=i_i^*(\dd\eta)\). Equations
\eqref{eq:logsplit}, \eqref{fnd:nag002981:supplied-rpl}, and \eqref{eq:cartier}, in that
order, give
\[
 L_f(\dd\eta)
 =\sum_i m_i L_{f_i}(\dd\eta_i)
 =\sum_i m_i\int_{D_i}\eta_i|_{D_i}
 =\int_D\eta|_D.
\]
The sign is unchanged: pullback preserves the order \(d'd''\), the
middle equality uses precisely the positive-sign normalization in
RPL, and all weights are positive integer lengths. RPL is the sole
use of a scalar PL identity in this proof.

For general \(X\), put \(C=\Supp\eta\). Choose finitely many
affinoid neighbourhoods \(V_j\) and ordinary opens
\[
 C\subseteq\bigcup_j O_j,\qquad
 O_j\subseteq\Int_{\rm top}(V_j,X)\cap\Int(X/K).
\]
These choices exist by goodness and compactness. By
\tagg{NAG-001630} and relative-interior composition
\tagg{NAG-001704}, each \(O_j\) lies in \(\Int(V_j/K)\).
Use \tagg{NAG-002428} to choose compact ordinary smooth
\(\rho_j\) supported in \(O_j\), with sum one near \(C\).
The forms \(\eta_j=\rho_j\eta\) then have compact support in
\(\Int(V_j/K)\), and \(\eta=\sum_j\eta_j\) as ordinary sections,
so \(\dd\eta=\sum_j\dd\eta_j\) exactly. Apply the affinoid
argument separately to each \(V_j\) and its own minimal primes and
generic lengths. This uses no global finite component decomposition.
Locality of the native integral and of
Proposition~\ref{prop:measure}, and the frozen effective Cartier
gluing in \tagg{NAG-002772}, identify the local pairings with their
zero extensions. Adding finitely many identities proves
\eqref{fnd:nag002981:conditional-equation}. There is no unexamined assertion that an arbitrary
affinoid restriction preserves analytic-interior support.
\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Conditional reduction beyond \(S_1\); F8CR-P]
\label{fnd:nag002981:conditional-reduction}
Let \(X\) be good, Hausdorff, and pure of analytic dimension \(n\geq1\),
let \(f\) be a regular analytic function, and let
\(\eta\in\cA_{X,c}^{n-1,n-1}\) have support in \(\Int(X/K)\).
Assume ZP\(_{\rm loc}\) on the finitely many affinoid neighbourhoods
used below, and RPL on their reduced irreducible components. Then
\begin{equation}\label{fnd:nag002981:conditional-equation}
              L_f(\dd\eta)=\int_{\divis_X(f)}\eta.
\end{equation}
In particular, after those inputs are reviewed and admitted, the
ambient \(S_1\) hypothesis is unnecessary for this scalar identity.
This is a scoped implication, not an unconditional assertion of
Poincar\'e--Lelong, continuity of a current, or a boundary trace formula.
\end{theorem}

proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Actual intersections and inherited purity are the frozen
\tagg{NAG-002411}/\tagg{002413} statements. Sectionwise injectivity of
$f$ and quotient/domain comparison give the actual regular element
and zero quotient on each $V_I$. The invoked ZP conclusion supplies
its pure dimension when nonempty; this is the only pending geometric
step in H1. Apply \hyperref[thm:analyticserre]{ST-A} to $\OO_U$ on each good affinoid
domain $W\subseteq V_I$. Its analytic stalk comparison and its
all-primes affinoid criterion give $S_1$ for $\OO(W)$. This is H2
for every such $W$, not merely $S_1$ for one chosen chart ring.
The restricted $g_{i(I)}$ are units, so H3 holds. Their rank need not
be maximal; no immersion or boundary separation is an extra premise.

For $D_I\ne\varnothing$, \hyperref[thm:product]{RC-P} now gives a bound $H_I$ for the exact
restricted tuple, with the actual coefficient sheaf $\OO_{D_I}$.
Apply it at the two parameters $-b<-a$, requiring $-b>H_I$.
It gives the product interval $[-b,-a]$ in the coordinate
$-\log|f|$. The map $(w,y)\mapsto(w,-y)$ is unimodular; it preserves
top calibrated weights, takes the interval to $[a,b]$, and preserves
the saturated product lattice with weight-one last factor. This gives
\eqref{eq:CP}. No geometric product of analytic spaces is
constructed or needed.

If $D_I=\varnothing$, compactness of $V_I$ gives
$m_I=\min_{V_I}|f|>0$. Choose $B<\log m_I$ so these annuli are empty.
There are finitely many nonempty intersections and finitely many chosen

units \emph{on an actual common overlap}, before taking the minimum.
For a joint tuple, pull the chosen horizontal form back by the coordinate
projection to its original tuple; it represents the same ordinary form.
No unit has been extended outside its original domain. No threshold
uniform over every possible future chart or over a test-space bounded
set is asserted. This proves the finite-family assertion.
\end{proof}

For a linear scalar functional TT, the seminorm |T||T| is continuous for the defining final topology as soon as every |TQi||TQ_i| is continuous. The fixed order-zero estimates give exactly this. Frozen transfers the same conclusion to ordinary compatible coefficient presentations. We do not infer it from continuity on individual tests or from an unspecified topology.

For the differential assertion fix one input stage. On finitely many smaller ordinary neighbourhoods covering $\Supp\chi$, represent χ\chi in fixed unit tuples and adjoin gg. A fixed finite partition on that support writes d′(Qiα)=d′χ∧tg*α+χtg*(d′α)d'(Q_i\alpha)=d'\chi\wedge t_g^*\alpha+\chi t_g^*(d'\alpha) as a finite sum of output cutoff stages composed with linear maps of coefficient spaces. In these fixed joint coordinates each map uses only fixed smooth coefficients and first derivatives of α\alpha. On every compact set its order-mm seminorm is bounded by a constant times an input order-m+1m+1 seminorm on the projected compact set. The same argument treats d″d''; multiplication by a fixed smooth function requires order mm only. The support of a derivative is contained in the support of its input, so the partitions just chosen cover the output as well. Testing against any continuous seminorm of the output final topology proves continuity. Extension by zero sends a cutoff stage in an open subspace to the identical stage in UU. For cutoff restriction, use the same finite refinement inside WW around the compact support of the product. This proves its continuity without claiming that unrestricted restriction preserves compactness.

Formula [fnd:nag003002:dual-equation] now gives continuous functionals by composition. The signs at the two successive degrees show anticommutation and square-zero from those identities on tests. proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
For a linear scalar functional \(T\), the seminorm \(|T|\) is
continuous for the defining final topology as soon as every
\(|TQ_i|\) is continuous. The fixed order-zero estimates give exactly
this. Frozen \tagg{NAG-002473} transfers the same conclusion to
ordinary compatible coefficient presentations. We do not infer it
from continuity on individual tests or from an unspecified topology.

For the differential assertion fix one input stage. On finitely many
smaller ordinary neighbourhoods covering \(\Supp\chi\), represent
\(\chi\) in fixed unit tuples and adjoin \(g\). A fixed finite
partition on that support writes
\[
 d'(Q_i\alpha)=d'\chi\wedge t_g^*\alpha+\chi t_g^*(d'\alpha)
\]
as a finite sum of output cutoff stages composed with linear maps of
coefficient spaces. In these fixed joint coordinates each map uses
only fixed smooth coefficients and first derivatives of \(\alpha\).
On every compact set its order-\(m\) seminorm is bounded by a constant
times an input order-\(m+1\) seminorm on the projected compact set.
The same argument treats \(d''\); multiplication by a fixed smooth
function requires order \(m\) only. The support of a derivative is
contained in the support of its input, so the partitions just chosen
cover the output as well. Testing against any continuous seminorm of
the output final topology proves continuity. Extension by zero sends
a cutoff stage in an open subspace to the identical stage in \(U\).
For cutoff restriction, use the same finite refinement inside \(W\)
around the compact support of the product. This proves its continuity
without claiming that unrestricted restriction preserves compactness.

Formula \eqref{fnd:nag003002:dual-equation} now gives continuous functionals by composition.
The signs at the two successive degrees show anticommutation and
square-zero from those identities on tests. For degree zero,
\[
 (d'd''T)(\eta)=(d''T)(d'\eta)
                 =-T(d''d'\eta)=T(d'd''\eta).
\]
Finally Lemma~\ref{fnd:nag002995:smooth-pairing} is exactly the asserted compatibility
with a smooth scalar weight. No topological dual convergence is
needed for this calculation.
\end{proof}

statement.html:

On these ordinary test spaces, d′d', d″d'', multiplication by a fixed ordinary smooth function, and extension by zero from an ordinary open subspace are continuous. So is cutoff restriction η↦(ρη)|W\eta\mapsto(\rho\eta)|_W when ρ\rho has compact support in an ordinary open WW.

Put $\mathcal D^{p,q}(U)=(\E^{n-p,n-q}(U),\tau_{\rm cut})'$, the continuous real dual. For T∈𝒟p,qT\in\mathcal D^{p,q}, define (d′T)(η)=(−1)p+q+1T(d′η),(d″T)(η)=(−1)p+q+1T(d″η).(d'T)(\eta)=(-1)^{p+q+1}T(d'\eta),\qquad (d''T)(\eta)=(-1)^{p+q+1}T(d''\eta). These are well-defined continuous functionals, satisfy square-zero and anticommutation, and for a degree (0,0)(0,0) pairing satisfy (ⅆT)(η)=T(ⅆη)(\dd T)(\eta)=T(\dd\eta). statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Internal continuity and differentials; F8MG-T]
\label{fnd:nag003002:topology}
The pairings in Proposition~\ref{prop:orderzero} are continuous for
\(\tau_{\rm cut}=\tau_{\rm ord}\). On these ordinary test spaces,
\(d'\), \(d''\), multiplication by a fixed ordinary smooth function,
and extension by zero from an ordinary open subspace are continuous.
So is cutoff restriction \(\eta\mapsto(\rho\eta)|_W\) when
\(\rho\) has compact support in an ordinary open \(W\).

Put \(\mathcal D^{p,q}(U)=(\E^{n-p,n-q}(U),\tau_{\rm cut})'\),
the continuous real dual. For \(T\in\mathcal D^{p,q}\), define
\begin{equation}\label{fnd:nag003002:dual-equation}
 (d'T)(\eta)=(-1)^{p+q+1}T(d'\eta),\qquad
 (d''T)(\eta)=(-1)^{p+q+1}T(d''\eta).
\end{equation}
These are well-defined continuous functionals, satisfy square-zero
and anticommutation, and for a degree \((0,0)\) pairing satisfy
\((\dd T)(\eta)=T(\dd\eta)\). In particular
\(\dd T_h=T_{\dd h}\) for ordinary smooth \(h\) on \(U\).
\end{proposition}

proof.html: Propositions [prop:orderzero] and [fnd:nag003002:topology] give the continuous dual memberships. Theorems [thm:meromorphic] and [fnd:nag002997:green-pairing] give equality on every test of the relevant bidegree. The degree-zero identity in [fnd:nag003002:dual-equation] turns these into [fnd:nag003004:current-equations], with no appeal to a dense smaller test class. The earlier transformation laws are equalities of these same functionals, hence also equalities in the continuous dual. For ordinary gluing, compact tests use finitely many local pieces; the cutoff restrictions are continuous by Proposition [fnd:nag003002:topology]. Agreement on overlap tests and the product-partition argument give uniqueness and independence. This proves gluing of the pairings, not a pullback of arbitrary currents by arbitrary analytic maps.

proof.html:
Use the comparator definitions above. The preform space is the filtered colimit over charts and affine refinements. On a compact domain DD, every chart gg has a compact finite polyhedral actual image g(D)g(D). In the present analytic setting this property follows by taking a finite affinoid refinement on which the coordinates of gg are rational affine combinations of logarithms of analytic units. Such a refinement follows from the generated G-sheaf of affine functions and the analytic-domain site; compactness makes it finite. Each actual moment image is finite polyhedral by NAG-002358. Its affine image, and the finite union of these images, are finite polyhedral. Compact analytic domains have finite affinoid refinements by the quasi-net domain definition and NAG-001609.

If the preform sf*αs_f^*\alpha is zero on a compact domain DD, the filtered-colimit zero criterion gives a refining chart gg and an affine map π\pi with sf=π∘gs_f=\pi\circ g, on which π*α\pi^*\alpha is zero. Restrict its target to g(D)g(D). The latter maps onto sf(D)s_f(D), so Lemma [lem:poly] gives α|sf(D)=0\alpha|_{s_f(D)}=0. Zero in the polyhedral quotient has precisely this meaning: its null sheaf is defined by all-cell tangential vanishing. The converse is represented by the chart with target sf(D)s_f(D) itself.

The kernel of passage to the associated G-sheaf consists of sections that vanish on a G-cover. A G-cover of compact CC admits a finite refinement by compact domains: at each point take finitely many compact domains whose union is a relative neighborhood, and extract finitely many of these neighborhoods by compactness. Compositions of such refinements are covers by NAG-001609. For a zero section we thus have finitely many compact domains DiD_i covering CC on which the preform is zero. The preceding argument gives vanishing on every sf(Di)s_f(D_i), and Lemma [lem:poly] gives vanishing on their union sf(C)s_f(C). This proves [fnd:nag003074:compact-kernel]. The argument never replaces a G-cover by an ordinary cover of its individual members.

Now let ω\omega be an ordinary CLD germ at xx. The ordinary comparator definition gives an ordinary open neighborhood OO and one tropical chart g:O→Eg:O\to E representing it. By the ordinary chart definition, the coordinates of gg are affine for the specified ordinary affine structure. Each coordinate is, on an ordinary neighborhood of xx, a rational multiple of the logarithmic norm of an analytic unit plus a real constant. Intersect these finitely many ordinary neighborhoods. Thus g=L∘sfg=L\circ s_f for one analytic unit tuple and a rational-affine map LL. These rational coefficients belong to LL; no roots of units are taken.

The form on the polyhedral target of gg has an ambient smooth representative near g(x)g(x) by the quotient definition of a superform on the chart target. Shrink OO by the inverse image of that real neighborhood, and pull the representative back by LL. This gives the asserted ordinary local moment presentation. Choose an ordinary affinoid neighborhood inside this OO, using the basis established in NAG-002424. Conversely, units on an affinoid representative restrict to units on its ordinary interior, so they produce ordinary CLD forms there. Formula [fnd:nag003074:compact-kernel], applied to the difference on the actual joint tuple, says that equality of CLD germs is exactly the project relation on a smaller ordinary affinoid neighborhood. proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Use the comparator definitions above. The preform space is the filtered colimit over charts and affine refinements. On a compact domain $D$, every chart $g$ has a compact finite polyhedral actual image $g(D)$. In the present analytic setting this property follows by taking a finite affinoid refinement on which the coordinates of $g$ are rational affine combinations of logarithms of analytic units. Such a refinement follows from the generated G-sheaf of affine functions and the analytic-domain site; compactness makes it finite. Each actual moment image is finite polyhedral by \hyperref[v037:globaltrop:finiteimage]{NAG-002358}. Its affine image, and the finite union of these images, are finite polyhedral. Compact analytic domains have finite affinoid refinements by the quasi-net domain definition and \hyperref[fnd:generalnetdomaincalculus]{NAG-001609}.

If the preform $s_f^*\alpha$ is zero on a compact domain $D$, the filtered-colimit zero criterion gives a refining chart $g$ and an affine map $\pi$ with $s_f=\pi\circ g$, on which $\pi^*\alpha$ is zero. Restrict its target to $g(D)$. The latter maps onto $s_f(D)$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:poly} gives $\alpha|_{s_f(D)}=0$. Zero in the polyhedral quotient has precisely this meaning: its null sheaf is defined by all-cell tangential vanishing. The converse is represented by the chart with target $s_f(D)$ itself.

The kernel of passage to the associated G-sheaf consists of sections that vanish on a G-cover. A G-cover of compact $C$ admits a finite refinement by compact domains: at each point take finitely many compact domains whose union is a relative neighborhood, and extract finitely many of these neighborhoods by compactness. Compositions of such refinements are covers by \hyperref[fnd:generalnetdomaincalculus]{NAG-001609}. For a zero section we thus have finitely many compact domains $D_i$ covering $C$ on which the preform is zero. The preceding argument gives vanishing on every $s_f(D_i)$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:poly} gives vanishing on their union $s_f(C)$. This proves \eqref{fnd:nag003074:compact-kernel}. The argument never replaces a G-cover by an ordinary cover of its individual members.

Now let $\omega$ be an ordinary CLD germ at $x$. The ordinary comparator definition gives an ordinary open neighborhood $O$ and one tropical chart $g:O\to E$ representing it. By the ordinary chart definition, the coordinates of $g$ are affine for the specified ordinary affine structure. Each coordinate is, on an ordinary neighborhood of $x$, a rational multiple of the logarithmic norm of an analytic unit plus a real constant. Intersect these finitely many ordinary neighborhoods. Thus $g=L\circ s_f$ for one analytic unit tuple and a rational-affine map $L$. These rational coefficients belong to $L$; no roots of units are taken.

The form on the polyhedral target of $g$ has an ambient smooth representative near $g(x)$ by the quotient definition of a superform on the chart target. Shrink $O$ by the inverse image of that real neighborhood, and pull the representative back by $L$. This gives the asserted ordinary local moment presentation. The ambient lift is local near the image of the chosen point.

Choose an ordinary affinoid neighborhood inside this $O$, using the basis established in \hyperref[v037:forms:germsheaf]{NAG-002424}. Conversely, units on an affinoid representative restrict to units on its ordinary interior, so they produce ordinary CLD forms there. Formula \eqref{fnd:nag003074:compact-kernel}, applied to the difference on the actual joint tuple, says that equality of CLD germs is exactly the project relation on a smaller ordinary affinoid neighborhood. It proves well-definedness, injectivity and surjectivity of $c$ on every stalk. The local constructions agree under restriction, hence give the asserted sheaf isomorphism.
\end{proof}

NAG-003074.title: Compact faithfulness and ordinary presentation

proof.html:
For [C,f,α][C,f,\alpha] at xx, restrict to a common ordinary open neighbourhood of xx where the units are defined and the chosen finite comparison relations hold. Apply simultaneous replacement there to all their tuples in one list. The resulting ordinary open VV lies inside the ordinary interior of the one actual compact affinoid witness. Write the algebraic replacement as gg on UU. The actual joint image of (f,g)(f,g) on the new compact witness lies in the diagonal because of [eq:norm]. To compare two choices, restrict to one ordinary neighbourhood contained in the interiors of both compact witnesses, where the original tuples, both algebraic replacements and the relation are defined. Wedges and d′,d″d',d'' are applied to the same ambient smooth forms and commute with affine pullback. The equalities of norms remain true after composition with $h^\an$ on an actual compact affinoid witness inside that source neighbourhood. Use the ordinary moment pullback there. proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
For $[C,f,\alpha]$ at $x$, restrict to a common ordinary open neighbourhood of $x$ where the units are defined and the chosen finite comparison relations hold. Apply \mbox{\hyperref[prop:approx]{simultaneous replacement}} there to all their tuples in one list. The resulting ordinary open $V$ lies inside the ordinary interior of the one actual compact affinoid witness. Write the algebraic replacement as $g$ on $U$. The actual joint image of $(f,g)$ on the new compact witness lies in the diagonal because of \eqref{eq:norm}. Its two coordinate projections agree on points and tangent vectors. Therefore their pullbacks of $\alpha$ agree in both exterior factors on every cell and face, also after adjoining further coordinates. This is the \mbox{\hyperref[lem:diagonal]{diagonal relation}}.

Factor $t_g=F_g\circ t_U$ by the \mbox{\hyperref[prop:torus]{actual algebraic unit lattice}} and represent the output on the \mbox{\hyperref[prop:intrinsic]{intrinsic chart}} $V$ by $F_g^*\alpha$. A zero input relation remains tangentially zero after the simultaneous replacement on its compact witness, by the same diagonal argument. Its restriction to $V$ is zero, and pullback by the integral affine character map preserves all-face tangential vanishing. Thus $\Phi$ descends through the relation defining $\A_{\rm mom}$.

To compare two choices, restrict to one ordinary neighbourhood contained in the interiors of both compact witnesses, where the original tuples, both algebraic replacements and the relation are defined. Put all of them in the finite tuple before applying \mbox{\hyperref[prop:approx]{simultaneous replacement}}. Proposition~\ref{prop:intrinsic} supplies a chart contained in the intersection of the two algebraic opens. The diagonal argument and affine pullback make the outputs equal there. This proves choice independence and gluing. \mbox{\hyperref[prop:torus]{Changing basis lifts}} translates the character map and the ambient representative by inverse translations, giving the same germ.

There is an inverse $\Psi:\A_{\rm alg}\to\A_{\rm mom}$: restrict the actual algebraic unit tuple to an \mbox{\hyperref[v037:forms:germsheaf]{ordinary affinoid neighbourhood}} inside its chart. A tangential zero relation stays zero on that actual compact subimage. On a \mbox{\hyperref[prop:intrinsic]{common intrinsic refinement}}, both character maps compare on the same compact witness and hence give the same joint-image germ. Hence $\Psi$ is well-defined. \mbox{\hyperref[lem:diagonal]{The joint diagonal}} gives $\Psi\Phi=1$ on an ordinary affinoid neighbourhood inside $V$: the two representations on it use $f$ and $g$ with equal norms. For $\Phi\Psi=1$, use the original intrinsic basis units in the finite tuple for \mbox{\hyperref[prop:approx]{simultaneous replacement}} taken within the original algebraic open. On the smaller intrinsic chart the two affine coordinate maps give the same points of the original tropical image, by equality of the norms on the compact witness. Their restrictions to each cell tangent therefore agree, so their pullbacks of the original form agree. This proves the other identity. \mbox{\hyperref[fnd:nag003074:compact-faithfulness]{Compact faithfulness and ordinary presentation}} supply $c$.

Wedges and $d',d''$ are applied to the same ambient smooth forms and commute with affine pullback. Their preservation of all-face tangential relations follows from \mbox{\hyperref[v037:forms:finitecoverfaithfulness]{tangential preservation}} on the actual joint polyhedral images. For an algebraic morphism $h:X'\to X$ between objects of the common category, choose a source ordinary neighbourhood in $(h^\an)^{-1}(V)$, where $V$ is the target ordinary open inside the compact witness. statement.html: There is a canonical isomorphism of ordinary sheaves of bigraded differential real algebras $$\A_{\rm CLD}\xleftarrow[\sim]{\ c\ }\A_{\rm mom} \xrightarrow[\sim]{\ \Phi\ }\A_{\rm alg}.$$ On a moment representative, Φ\Phi is obtained by the single simultaneous replacement [eq:norm] and pullback along the integral affine character map of Proposition [prop:intrinsic]. It is independent of the replacement, the compact witness, the chosen algebraic chart, and the lifts of a unit-lattice basis. The maps commute with ordinary restriction and with algebraic pullbacks. They preserve ordinary supports exactly.

NAG-003078.title: Norm replacement gives the ordinary algebraic sheaf

proof.html:
The original universal kernel tests every compatible algebraic morphism and chart. The identity test detects all-face tangential vanishing: the chart has its actual canonical support, finite pure structure and strictly positive top weights, so a nonzero tangential coefficient on a maximal cell would have a nonzero local pairing. Continuity gives vanishing on its faces. Conversely, the compatible-chart test pulls back tangential vanishing along the induced integral affine map on each actual compatible chart, after a refinement carrying each source cell into a target cell. This gives zero in every test kernel with the stated actual supports and weights.

Thus the smooth chart quotient is exactly the quotient used for $\A_{\rm alg}$. Proposition [prop:intrinsic] supplies a cofinal system of local intrinsic refinements at each point. A zero germ in GK is witnessed, after ordinary sheafification and the filtered chart colimit, by a smaller ordinary neighbourhood with a compatible chart where its smooth representative belongs to the universal kernel. Pass to a common intrinsic refinement inside this neighbourhood and inside the original chart. The preceding kernel equality makes it zero in $\A_{\rm alg}$. This proves injectivity on stalks. Every locally smooth representative lies in the image by construction. This proves the displayed isomorphism and its asserted image, rather than inferring injectivity from the mere existence of a map. Naturality follows from the actual character pullback on compatible source charts. Wedges and d′,d″d',d'' descend from the identical ambient operations on the all-face quotient by tangential preservation.

NAG-003080.title: Map to the original universal quotient

proof.html:
Fix an external stage. By (i)–(ii) its finite restriction map takes values continuously in a fixed intrinsic compatible-tuple space JsJ_s, with the same support and ordinary gluing equations. By (iii), the native gluing map on its ambient preimage descends to a continuous map from JsJ_s to (E,τa)(E,\tau_a), as in the proof of Proposition [prop:finalcompare]. The composite is the identity on that external stage. Its final property proves continuity from external tests to native tests.

Conversely fix QiQ_i. Use the fixed external stage of (ii). On its refining charts the variable coefficient is the pullback of η\eta under a fixed affine projection, multiplied by a fixed smooth cutoff coefficient. The product and chain rules bound every tangential seminorm by finitely many ambient seminorms of the same order. The resulting linear map into this external stage is continuous, and its glued form is QiηQ_i\eta. The final property of τa\tau_a gives the opposite continuous identity. A homeomorphism preserves bounded sets, so the strong-dual conclusion follows. This last implication uses the full topological match, not just equality of fixed-test pairings.
proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Fix an external stage. By (i)--(ii) its finite restriction map takes
values continuously in a fixed intrinsic compatible-tuple space
$J_s$, with the same support and ordinary gluing equations.
By (iii), the native gluing map on its ambient preimage descends to a
continuous map from $J_s$ to $(E,\tau_a)$, as in the proof of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finalcompare}. The composite is the identity on
that external stage. Its final property proves continuity from external
tests to native tests.

Conversely fix $Q_i$. Use the fixed external stage of (ii). On its
refining charts the variable coefficient is the pullback of $\eta$
under a fixed affine projection, multiplied by a fixed smooth cutoff
coefficient. The product and chain rules bound every tangential
seminorm by finitely many ambient seminorms of the same order.
The resulting linear map into this external stage is continuous, and
its glued form is $Q_i\eta$. The final property of $\tau_a$ gives the
opposite continuous identity. A homeomorphism preserves bounded sets,
so the strong-dual conclusion follows. This last implication uses the
full topological match, not just equality of fixed-test pairings.
\end{proof}

statement.html:
Let $E_{\rm ext}$ be an ordinary compact-test space with chart/support final topology of the intrinsic type described above. Assume:

  1. There is a specified algebraic identification with the native ordinary test sheaf, compatible with local moment pullbacks, nullity, restriction, ordinary gluing and support. The support family is the same compact subsets of the chosen UU, not compact sets meeting an ambient analytic boundary.

  2. On every fixed external chart/support stage, the compact support has a finite cover by ordinary interiors of compact affinoid refinements, with fixed unit moments and finite polyhedral images. Restriction to those images is continuous for the intrinsic seminorms. Fixed affine coordinate changes, including reflection between log\log and −log-\log, induce the indicated pullbacks. Conversely a native cutoff presentation, after adjoining fixed cutoff moments, is represented by one fixed external stage.

  3. On each finite refinement needed in (ii), the coefficient quotient map onto the relevant intrinsic compatible-tuple space is strict (a quotient map). This follows, for example, from [eq:reverse], or from the supported extension in Proposition [f8it:sector-extension] when that is the exact sector in use.

Then the identification is a homeomorphism for τa\tau_a and the external final topology. Under these hypotheses the strong-dual conclusions of Theorem [thm:log] transfer, with the same underlying bounded sets. statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[A scoped intrinsic adaptation]\label{prop:adapt}
Let $E_{\rm ext}$ be an ordinary compact-test space with chart/support
final topology of the intrinsic type described above. Assume:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item There is a specified algebraic identification with the native
ordinary test sheaf, compatible with local moment pullbacks, nullity,
restriction, ordinary gluing and support. The support family is the same
compact subsets of the chosen $U$, not compact sets meeting an ambient
analytic boundary.
\item On every fixed external chart/support stage, the compact support
has a finite cover by ordinary interiors of compact affinoid
refinements, with fixed unit moments and finite polyhedral images.
Restriction to those images is continuous for the intrinsic seminorms.
Fixed affine coordinate changes, including reflection between $\log$
and $-\log$, induce the indicated pullbacks. Conversely a native
cutoff presentation, after adjoining fixed cutoff moments, is
represented by one fixed external stage.
\item On each finite refinement needed in (ii), the coefficient
quotient map onto the relevant intrinsic compatible-tuple space is
strict (a quotient map). This follows, for example, from
\eqref{eq:reverse}, or from the supported extension in
Proposition~\ref{f8it:sector-extension} when that is the exact sector in use.
\end{enumerate}
Then the identification is a homeomorphism for $\tau_a$ and the
external final topology. Under these hypotheses the strong-dual
conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:log} transfer, with the same underlying
bounded sets. Without (iii) only the native-to-external continuity
provided by the coefficient restriction argument is obtained from
these assumptions.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proposition}[Finite strong-dual transfer; F8NM-S]\label{prop:strong}
Suppose \(V=\cM(A)\) is pure of dimension \(n\),
\(U\subseteq\Int(V/K)\) is ordinary open, and
\(j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow U\) are its finitely many restricted reduced
components with the original weights \(m_i\).
Let \(T_{M,i},T_i\) be continuous functionals on the corresponding
native test spaces, and define
\(D_M=\sum_i m_i(j_i)_*(T_{M,i}-T_i)\).
For every \(\tau_a\)-bounded set \(B\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:strong}
 \sup_{\alpha\in B}|D_M(\alpha)|
 \leq\sum_i m_i\sup_{\beta\in j_i^*B}|(T_{M,i}-T_i)(\beta)|.
\end{equation}
Thus component strong convergence implies ambient strong convergence.
Uniform eventual equality on each component bounded set also transfers.

For a globally represented ambient regular quotient \(f=a/b\) on
\(U\), the native logarithmic pairings and the smooth truncations
\(u_M=\ell_M(a)-\ell_M(b)\) have exactly this decomposition, with
\(D_M=T_{f,M}-L_f\). The conclusion is conditional on the component
strong-convergence premise in the stated topology.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
In (a), every class has the unique module form
\(a(t)+e c\), with \(a\in K\langle t\rangle\) and \(c\in K\).
The nilradical is \((e)\), the underlying space is the pure disc,
and \(\operatorname{ann}(e)=(t,e)\) is an embedded associated prime.
At the minimal prime \((e)\), \(t\) is invertible and kills \(e\),
so the generic length is one. But
\(A/(t)=K[e]/(e^2)\) has length two at the rigid origin; the reduced
component quotient is \(K\). An ordinary scalar cutoff equal to one
near that interior point detects the difference of the two
zero-dimensional quotient pairings. Since \(te=0\) with \(e\ne0\),
\(t\) is not a Cartier equation. It also cannot be a unit of the
ambient total quotient ring: if \(t(c/d)=1\) with \(d\) regular,
then \(tc=d\), and multiplication by \(e\) contradicts regularity
of \(d\). Componentwise meromorphic invertibility does not solve this.

In (b), the torsion summand has zero generic top weight, so the native
logarithmic pairing away from \(t=0\) is exactly that for the structure
sheaf. The reviewed reduced-disc scalar identity evaluates to one on
a compact interior scalar test equal to one at zero. On the proposed
right side, \(F/tF=K\oplus K\), giving two. The kernel of multiplication
by \(t\) on \(F\) is \(K\); its length is one. The numerical correction
\(2-1=1\) illustrates the missing kernel term, but no general
Euler-characteristic formula or coherent-module PL theorem is claimed
here. Such a theorem needs its own module-regularity or homological
multiplicity input and analytic comparison.

For (c), take a nontrivially valued field and a constant unit \(u\)
with \(c=\log|u|\ne0\). On the trivial line over a disc use
\(e_j=u e_i\), \(h_i=0\), \(h_j=-c\), and the section \(s=t e_i\).
Then \(f_i=t\), \(f_j=t/u\). For a constant truncation \(\lambda_M\)
with value \(-M\) sufficiently deep at \(-\infty\), the proposed
local potentials differ by
\[
 (h_j-\lambda_M(\log|f_j|))
 -(h_i-\lambda_M(\log|f_i|))
 =\lambda_M(v)-\lambda_M(v-c)-c,
 \qquad v=\log|t|.
\]
Near zero both truncated logarithms are \(-M\), so the difference is
\(-c\ne0\). The untruncated expressions agree exactly. A chosen
partition may construct another family, but its gluing and convergence
must be specified rather than inferred from local frame formulae.
\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[Three failures of broader formulations; F8NM-E]
\label{prop:obstructions}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)},leftmargin=*]
\item In \(A=K\langle t,e\rangle/(e^2,te)\), the element \(t\) is
nonzero on the sole reduced component but is an ambient zero-divisor.
The ambient quotient \(A/(t)\) has length two, whereas the component
quotient has length one and the ambient generic weight is one.
Thus this weakening cannot recover the full quotient cycle.
\item Even for the reduced disc \(A=K\langle t\rangle\), an arbitrary
full-support coherent module \(F=A\oplus A/(t)\) cannot be inserted
with right side \(F/tF\) in the scalar formula. Its generic top weight
is one, but \(F/tF\) has length two. The function \(t\) is ambient
regular but not \(F\)-regular.
\item For a smooth metrized line bundle, constant truncation of local
\(\log|f_i|\) does not in general glue to a frame-independent smooth
potential, even when the untruncated potential and its current glue.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We first give a fixed-stage domination argument, also used below. Fix $Q_i$, put $C=\supp\chi$ and $L=t_f(V)$, and choose $0\leq\rho\leq1$ of compact support in $\Int_{\rm top}(V,X)$, equal to one on an ordinary neighborhood of $C$, using \NAG{002428} with one open set. Let $M=\sup|\chi|$ and set
\[
 \Theta=\frac1{d!}\left(\sum_{k=1}^N d'x_k\wedge d''x_k\right)^d,
 \qquad \theta_i=M\,\ext(\rho t_f^*\Theta).
\]
The form $\theta_i$ is compact and positive. The factor $1/d!$ in this auxiliary domination form makes its restriction the Gram square; it does not change the normalization of any Chern product. If $N<d$ all forms in this stage are zero.

In the remaining case write an ambient top restriction in the basis of $\Lambda^d\R^N$. For the projected tangent vector $v$, its value is $v^{\mathsf t}A_\eta v$ in the positive top convention, whereas $\Theta$ gives $|v|^2$. The antisymmetric part of $A_\eta$ contributes zero. The elementary finite-matrix inequality $|v^{\mathsf t}A_\eta v|\leq c_{N,d}p_{L,0}(\eta)|v|^2$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nag003151:domination}
 c_{N,d}p_{L,0}(\eta)\theta_i+Q_i\eta\ \geq0,
 \qquad
 c_{N,d}p_{L,0}(\eta)\theta_i-Q_i\eta\ \geq0.
\end{equation}
These inequalities hold on every actual top tangent plane in a common moment refinement: its projection to the $f$-coordinates supplies $v$. Rank drop gives $v=0$, so introduces no exception. On $C$, $\rho=1$ and $|\chi|\leq M$; off $C$, $Q_i\eta=0$. This also verifies the inequalities where the extra moments presenting $\chi$ or $\rho$ are needed.

Positivity and finiteness of \NAG{002425} therefore give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:integralbound}
 |I_{X,\F}(Q_i\eta)|
 \leq c_{N,d}\left(\int_{X,\F}\theta_i\right)p_{L,0}(\eta).
\end{equation}
The coefficient seminorm is continuous, and all objects except $\eta$ were fixed beforehand. Finality in \NAG{002473} proves continuity. This argument uses the actual coherent integral, so its whole-module multiplicities are not replaced by reduced or separable ones.

Take an ordinary open \(U\subseteq\Int(X/K)\). It is good and
Hausdorff, and it is pure of the same dimension by the affinoid
neighbourhood basis and Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:puritylocality}.
Thus the preceding construction applies to \(U\) and the coherent
restriction \(\F|_{U_G}\).

For any ordinary test \(\psi\) compactly supported in \(U\),
write \(S=\supp_U\psi\). This set is compact in \(X\) and closed
there since \(X\) is Hausdorff. The ordinary smooth moment sheaf of
Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:germsheaf} glues \(\psi\) on \(U\)
with zero on \(X\setminus S\). The glued section is \(\ext\psi\)
and its support is \(S\) in \(X\). Both differentials are local,
so they commute with this zero extension and have support
contained in \(S\). For a top-degree \(\psi\), choose the finitely
many affinoid carriers in the compact integral theorem inside
\(U\), with ordinary interiors covering \(S\). They present the
same section and restricted coherent sheaf in \(U\) and in \(X\).
The compact-neighbourhood independence of
Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:compactintegral} gives
\[
  I_{U,\F|_U}(\psi)=I_{X,\F}(\ext\psi).
\]
This is the restriction identity for the current already constructed.

Now let \(\beta\in\E^{d-1,d}(U)\) and
\(\gamma\in\E^{d,d-1}(U)\). In \(X\), their zero extensions
are compact ordinary tests of the same bidegrees, with
support contained in \(\Int(X/K)\). The \(d'\) and \(d''\)
limbs of Theorem~\ref{f7gg:global} apply, respectively,
to exactly these two tests with the original coefficient sheaf
\(\F\). The transpose sign in both cases is
\((-1)^{2d+1}=-1\). Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (d'I_{U,\F|_U})(\beta)&=-\int_{X,\F}d'(\ext\beta)=0,\\
 (d''I_{U,\F|_U})(\gamma)&=-\int_{X,\F}d''(\ext\gamma)=0 .
\end{aligned}
\]

\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Closed integration on interior tests]\label{f9si:start}
Let $X$ be good, Hausdorff, and pure of analytic dimension $d\geq1$, and let $\F$ be coherent on $X_G$. The native functional
\[
 I_{X,\F}(\alpha)=\int_{X,\F}\alpha
 \quad(\alpha\in\E^{d,d}(X))

\(-I_{V,\mathcal O_V}(d'j^*\beta)=0\).
On a compact \((r,r-1)\)-test \(\gamma\) it is
\(-I_{V,\mathcal O_V}(d''j^*\gamma)=0\).

statement.tex:
\begin{theorem}[Closed component currents with full generic lengths]\label{f9si:cycle}
Let $j:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of good Hausdorff analytic spaces, let $Y$ be pure of analytic dimension $r\geq1$, and let $U\subseteq\Int(X/K)$ be ordinary open. Put $V=j^{-1}U$. Then
\[
 j_*I_Y(\alpha)=\int_V j^*\alpha,
 \qquad \alpha\in\E^{r,r}(U),
\]
defines a closed current of bidimension $(r,r)$, with support contained in $j(Y)\cap U$. If $X$ is pure $n$-dimensional its bidegree is $(n-r,n-r)$. Finite supplied real linear combinations of these currents, and supplied locally finite such combinations with one fixed component dimension $r$, are closed with the same degree convention.

For a pure affinoid $X=\mathcal M(A)$ of dimension $n\geq1$, let $\mathfrak q_i$ be its minimal primes, $X_i=\mathcal M(A/\mathfrak q_i)$, and $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$. Then, on interior tests,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nag003154:cycle}
 I_X=\sum_i m_i(j_i)_*I_{X_i},\qquad
 m_i=\length_{A_{\mathfrak q_i}}A_{\mathfrak q_i}.
\end{equation}
These are the full generic lengths. No general coherent-module component formula is asserted here.
\end{theorem}

proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
The ordinary open \(U\) is good and Hausdorff and is pure of dimension
\(n\) by the affinoid neighbourhood basis and
Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:puritylocality}. The derivatives
of a test \(\alpha\) have support in \(\supp\alpha\).
Theorem~\ref{f9si:mult} applied to the pure space \(U\)
constructs \(J_u\) on its compact top tests. By \NAG{003135},
\(\DD\) is continuous on tests and has the positive double
transpose. Hence the displayed formula is \(T_u(\alpha)=J_u(\DD\alpha)\)
and defines a continuous current. Locality and ordinary-open
extension are those of the actual top-form measures in \NAG{002970}.

For an ordinary smooth $h$ and $\alpha$ as above, apply the exact interior Stokes theorem \NAG{002577} to $h\,d''\alpha$ and $d'h\wedge\alpha$, extended by zero. Both have compact interior support and the required degrees. The identities are
\[
 0=\int d'h\wedge d''\alpha+\int h\DD\alpha,
 \qquad
 0=-\int\DD h\wedge\alpha-\int d'h\wedge d''\alpha.
\]
Thus the double-transpose sign is positive and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ibp}
 T_h(\alpha)=\int_U(\DD h)\wedge\alpha.
\end{equation}
This uses neither scalar PL nor a pending current comparison.

Let $w$ be a convex piece. Its smooth approximants from \eqref{eq:softmax}, or the unchanged smooth convex function, give for every fixed test
\begin{equation}\label{eq:firstlimit}
 |T_{w_\epsilon}(\alpha)-T_w(\alpha)|
 \leq\epsilon\log m\,|\mu_{U,\DD\alpha}|(U)
\end{equation}
for a maximum with $m$ entries, and zero error for an unchanged smooth piece. On any actual $n$-dimensional tangent plane, the pullback Hessian of $w_\epsilon$ is positive semidefinite. Diagonalizing it, or writing it as a sum of nonnegative rank-one terms, shows that $(\DD w_\epsilon)\wedge\alpha$ has nonnegative top coefficient whenever $\alpha$ is nonnegative on $(n-1)$-planes. Each rank-one term tests the restriction of $\alpha$ to the complementary hyperplane; a zero or rank-deficient term contributes zero. Positivity of \NAG{002425} and \eqref{eq:ibp} therefore prove $T_{w_\epsilon}(\alpha)\geq0$. Passage through \eqref{eq:firstlimit} proves the same for $T_w$.


Theorem~\ref{f9tf:measure} now supplies the stated supported
signed measures and multipliers for each convex piece. The
fixed local decomposition \eqref{eq:decomp} gives the signed
sum by linearity of the defining formula. On overlaps the
current agrees by the formula, and the measures agree by their
uniqueness on smooth scalar tests. For a compact test one uses
a finite compact partition as in Theorem~\ref{f9tf:measure}.
This supplies the corresponding local signed bounds and the
continuous multipliers for the general \(u\). Closedness follows
from \(\DD d'=0=\DD d''\) on the two complementary bidegrees.

Off \(Z_u\) each indicated maximum is locally affine in its
unit moments, and so the local smooth \(\DD u\) vanishes.
The integration-by-parts identity \eqref{eq:ibp} gives
vanishing there for \(T_u\). The support intersection for
its scalar measure follows from Theorem~\ref{f9tf:measure}.

For the component equalities, take the ordinary interior open
in the pure affinoid \(Y\) and its inverse images in the reduced
components \(Y_i\). The component purity part of \NAG{002966}
applies with the regular unit \(1\), and its closed-support part
puts every inverse image of an interior test support compactly in
the true interior of the component. The closed-pullback clause
\NAG{003106} applies to the respective ordinary test spaces
and commutes with both differentials and hence with \(\DD\).
The restricted potentials stay in the same local class by
pullback of the unit moments and the ordinary smooth pieces.
Use \eqref{eq:measure-split} of \NAG{002973} on the zero
extension of \(\DD\alpha\) to \(Y\). Pullback commutes with
these zero extensions by locality. With the ordinary-open
locality of \NAG{002970}, the measure identity is on the actual
opens. Integrating \(u\) against it proves the first equality
in \eqref{eq:nag003179:components}, with precisely the original
lengths \(m_i\).

For the second equality, apply this current equality to
\(h\alpha\) for each ordinary smooth scalar \(h\) on the
ambient open. Its pullback is \((h|_{Y_i})j_i^*\alpha\),
so the signed measures on both sides give the same pairings
with all such \(h\). They are finite and supported in the
same ambient compact carrier, and the closed embeddings
preserve the Radon property by the comparison in \NAG{002973}.
The uniqueness assertion of Theorem~\ref{f9tf:measure} gives
the signed measure equality.
\end{proof}

proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{f9tf:measure} constructs $vT_u$ as a current. Continuous test differentiation and \eqref{eq:dual} give \eqref{eq:two}; the exterior differential identities make it closed. Bilinearity and locality follow from uniqueness of scalar measures. It suffices to prove symmetry locally on an ordinary open where both decompositions are fixed: a finite compact partition then proves equality on every test in $U$.

Choose the smooth approximants $u_\epsilon,v_\epsilon$ there. For $\alpha\in\E^{n-2,n-2}$ put $\beta=\DD\alpha$. Theorem~\ref{f9tf:convergence} gives
\[
 R(u,v)(\alpha)=\lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}
       \int v_\epsilon\,d\nu_{u_\epsilon,\DD\alpha},
\]
and gives the analogous limit with $u,v$ reversed. For smooth $u_\epsilon$, uniqueness in \eqref{eq:scalar} and \eqref{eq:ibp} identify the measure here with the frozen measure of
$(\DD u_\epsilon)\wedge\DD\alpha$.
Set $B=\DD u_\epsilon$, so $B$ is smooth and $d'$- and $d''$-closed. Apply \NAG{002577} to the compact interior-supported tests
$v_\epsilon B\wedge d''\alpha$ and $d'v_\epsilon\wedge B\wedge\alpha$.
Their degrees are $(n-1,n)$ and $(n,n-1)$, and the two resulting identities give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:nag003190:smoothproduct}
 \int v_\epsilon B\wedge\DD\alpha
 =\int (\DD v_\epsilon)\wedge B\wedge\alpha.
\end{equation}
There is a plus sign: $B$ has total degree two, while $d'v_\epsilon$ has degree one. The two $(1,1)$-forms on the right commute. Thus the two smooth ordered pairings are equal for every $\epsilon$. Both of their limits have just been proved, so \eqref{eq:interchange} follows. This is a tested simultaneous limit, not automatic symmetry of weak limits.

For convex pieces the smooth Hessians are positive semidefinite. Expanding each into rank-one nonnegative terms, their product paired with a test nonnegative on $(n-2)$-planes has nonnegative top coefficient. Dependent rank-one terms vanish. The native positive integral and the proved limit give positivity of $R$. Fixed finite signed decompositions yield the asserted local signed sum, without claiming all model metrics are positive.

The first description in \eqref{eq:two} has support in $\supp T_u$, since multiplication and differentiation cannot enlarge it. Symmetry gives containment in $\supp T_v$ as well. The remaining support assertion follows from \eqref{eq:support}. Integrating $v$ against the measure equality in \eqref{eq:nag003179:components} and using the commuting closed-immersion pullback for $\DD\alpha$ proves the component formula for $R$.

For a change of frame $e'=ge$, the potential changes by $-\log|g|$. This is an ordinary affine unit-moment function with zero $\DD$, so \eqref{eq:ibp} gives $T_{-\log|g|}=0$. Linearity and symmetry show that adding it in either slot changes $R$ by zero. Local currents therefore agree on every overlap; the finite-partition gluing described in the conventions gives the global current. The supplied root metric has potential $1/e_i$ times its power-metric potential. Bilinearity proves the exact factor $1/(e_1e_2)$, without altering $|\cdot|$, extracting field roots, or inserting a factorial.
\end{proof}

proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
At the centre of $x$, choose a model frame $a$ of $\mathcal A$. Write the generating sections as $s_j=b_ja$. The elements $b_j$ generate the unit ideal in the model local ring, so there are local $c_j$ with $\sum c_jb_j=1$. Pull back to $\mathcal H(x)^\circ$. All $|b_j(x)|$ and $|c_j(x)|$ are at most one, and the displayed identity forces $\max_j|b_j(x)|=1$. Since $\|a\|=1$, this gives $\max_j\|s_j(x)\|=1$ at every analytic point, with no reducedness assumption.

In any ordinary analytic frame $e$, write $s_j=f_je$. Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:generatednorm}
 -\log\|e\|=\log\max_j|f_j|.
\end{equation}
The maximum is finite, positive, and continuous, since the sections generate the generic line. At a fixed point, omit every index whose value is strictly below the maximum; the strict gaps persist on a smaller ordinary neighborhood. The remaining $f_j$ have nonzero values there and can be made analytic units on a smaller neighborhood. Explicitly, on an affinoid neighborhood choose a positive real lower bound strictly below their values at the point; the Laurent domain imposing those lower bounds contains an ordinary neighborhood, and its rational algebra contains the inverses. The actual arbitrary-radius rational-domain constructions \NAG{001576}, \NAG{001577} justify this restriction. Equation~\eqref{eq:generatednorm} is therefore a maximum of unit logarithms on that ordinary neighborhood.

Tensoring norms and taking positive roots in the supplied model identifications give a difference of two such potentials divided by $e_i$, up to an affine unit logarithm from a frame change. Hence it lies in $\PP$ and is continuous. Theorems~\ref{f9tf:first} and~\ref{f9tf:two} apply. This proves the criterion from the supplied generating data; it does not invoke a general existence theorem for presentations \eqref{eq:modelquotient}.

For the example, the torus is good Hausdorff by \NAG{001707}, \NAG{001713}. Its Laurent boxes are integral of analytic dimension $n$ by \NAG{002294}, and their affinoid domains are pure by \NAG{002293}. Strict inequalities in a larger Laurent box give absolute-interior witnesses in its norm-admissible presentation; the compatibility of the general interior definition in \NAG{001630} gives a boundaryless torus. A compact tropical support has compact inverse image in a closed Laurent box. In the standard model, $X_{0,i}$ has norm one on $|z_i|\leq1$ and $X_{1,i}$ has norm one on $|z_i|\geq1$. Hence $-\log\|X_{1,i}\|=\max(0,t_i)$.

On a larger Laurent box containing the entire support in its strict interior, the identity coordinate moment map has saturated lattice index one. Its entire Gauss fibre algebra, after tensoring with its Gauss field, is that field itself. Thus \NAG{002362} gives weight one, and the selected \hyperref[fnd:nag002405:global-finite-module-chain-weights]{chain and weights} and \hyperref[fnd:nag002405:finite-cell-functional]{finite-cell functional} give the coordinate native top integral as the ordinary lattice-normalized integral, with the convention of \NAG{002389}. No fibre or inseparable factor is discarded.

Use $w_\epsilon(t)=\epsilon\log(1+e^{t/\epsilon})$. Its second derivative
\[
 k_\epsilon(t)=\frac{e^{t/\epsilon}}{\epsilon(1+e^{t/\epsilon})^2}
\]
is nonnegative, has integral one, and satisfies
$\int_{|t|>\delta}k_\epsilon(t)\,dt\leq2e^{-\delta/\epsilon}$.
The smooth pairing in \eqref{eq:nag003190:smoothproduct} is therefore
$\int\psi(t)k_\epsilon(t_i)k_\epsilon(t_j)\,dt$.
The one-variable fundamental theorem, iterated integration from \NAG{002389}, uniform continuity of $\psi$ on a compact box and the displayed tail bound show that its limit is \eqref{eq:coordinate}. Theorem~\ref{f9tf:convergence} identifies this limit with the native two-factor current already defined on all tests. This coordinate calculation calibrates it; it does not define the current only on radial tests. When $i=j$, the smooth form $\DD w_{i,\epsilon}$ has only the pair $d't_i\wedge d''t_i$, so its square is zero. The same all-test limit proves $R(w_i,w_i)=0$. The corresponding one-factor approximate-identity calculation gives $T_{w_i}(\beta)=1$, hence the stated value $-1$ for the dual model metric.
\end{proof}

Its actual bounded-frame norm has, in every ordinary analytic local frame, a potential locally equal to a maximum of finitely many logarithms of analytic units. Then its metric satisfies the hypotheses of Theorems [f9tf:first]–[f9tf:two], on all native tests. The statement does not require a reduced special fibre or assert positivity of the quotient metric. The cycle pushforward of each [Ỹj][\widetilde Y_j] is [Yj][Y_j]: the function fields agree, so its degree is one. Apply supported projection successively to the actual pulled factors along rjr_j and then along $Y_j\hookrightarrow\cY$. At each step the source support is contained in the inverse image of the next prescribed support. The signed construction gives the difference of the two factor operations, including the case where a restriction vanishes identically. Taking degrees on the proper supported special fibres and summing with the original multiplicities mjm_j gives the same degree as on the full cycle of $\cY$. Linearity and Theorem [f9be:degree] give [eq:weighted].

The full finite flat cycle shows that every YjY_j dominates $\cX$ and is horizontal, with generic component Xj=(Yj)LX_j=(Y_j)_L integral and of dimension dd. Its finite generic map to XX gives this dimension, and XjX_j is the corresponding reduced component of XLX_L. Each YjY_j is proper and integral, and is flat over R′R': its coordinate domains are torsion free over the DVR, and a torsion-free module over a PID is a directed union of its finite free submodules, hence is flat.

For XjX_j, use the actual inverse images of the SiS_i. Their total intersection is empty, and restriction of the actual line identifications and signed presentations gives the identified aia_i-th powers on XjX_j. Both factor sections remain nonzero at its generic point by dominance. On the integral XjX_j their zero divisors are effective Cartier and lie in the respective prescribed supports. Their difference gives the positive-power presentation required by the acquisition criterion. For a point of $X_j^{\an}$, compose its valuation-ring centre on YjY_j with $Y_j\hookrightarrow\cY$. By the proper-centre argument this is the centre on $\cY$; the same frames and generic identifications give the same aia_i-th root norms.

When XjX_j is normal, model independence applies in dimension d≥2d\geq 2 to this YjY_j calculation and to any computing model in the specified class for the same identified XjX_j, with the same metrics, sections and generic supports. The preceding proper pushforward identifies the summand on Ỹj\widetilde Y_j with that on YjY_j, even when rjr_j changes the generic fibre birationally. In the normal integral case XLX_L has one reduced component of generic multiplicity one, so this same computation is its model-independent value.

Finally every analytic point xx of XX has a point above it in $X_L^{\an}$. Indeed ℋ(x)⊗KL\mathcal H(x)\otimes_K L is a nonzero finite algebra over ℋ(x)\mathcal H(x). The residue field of a maximal ideal of that algebra is finite over ℋ(x)\mathcal H(x) and has its unique extending absolute value by finite extension of norms. proof.tex:
\begin{proof}
The cycle pushforward of each $[\widetilde Y_j]$ is $[Y_j]$:
the function fields agree, so its degree is one.
Apply \mbox{\hyperref[ex68:support:eq:projection]{supported projection}} successively to the actual pulled factors along $r_j$ and then along $Y_j\hookrightarrow\cY$. At each step the source support is contained in the inverse image of the next prescribed support. The \mbox{\hyperref[f9sc:signed]{signed construction}} gives the difference of the two factor operations, including the case where a restriction vanishes identically. Taking degrees on the proper supported special fibres and summing with the original multiplicities $m_j$ gives the same degree as on the full cycle of $\cY$. Linearity and
Theorem~\ref{f9be:degree} give \eqref{eq:weighted}.

The \mbox{\hyperref[f9be:transfer]{full finite flat cycle}} shows that every
\(Y_j\) dominates \(\cX\) and is horizontal, with generic component
\(X_j=(Y_j)_L\) integral and of dimension \(d\). Its finite generic
map to \(X\) gives this dimension, and \(X_j\) is the corresponding
reduced component of \(X_L\). Each \(Y_j\) is proper and integral,
and is flat over \(R'\): its coordinate domains are torsion free
over the DVR, and a torsion-free module over a PID is a directed
union of its finite free submodules, hence is flat.

For \(X_j\), use the actual inverse images of the \(S_i\). Their
total intersection is empty, and restriction of the actual line
identifications and signed presentations gives the identified
\(a_i\)-th powers on \(X_j\). Both factor sections remain nonzero
at its generic point by dominance. On the integral \(X_j\) their
zero divisors are effective Cartier and lie in the respective
prescribed supports. Their difference gives the positive-power
presentation required by the \mbox{\hyperref[f9mi:criterion]{acquisition criterion}}. For a point of \(X_j^{\an}\), compose its valuation-ring
centre on \(Y_j\) with \(Y_j\hookrightarrow\cY\). By the
\mbox{\hyperref[fnd:nag003203:proper-centre]{proper-centre argument}} this is the
centre on \(\cY\); the same frames and generic identifications
give the same \(a_i\)-th root norms.

When \(X_j\) is normal, \mbox{\hyperref[f9mi:independence]{model independence}}
applies in dimension \(d\geq 2\) to this \(Y_j\) calculation and
to any computing model in the specified class for the same
identified \(X_j\), with the same metrics, sections and generic
supports. The preceding proper pushforward identifies the
summand on \(\widetilde Y_j\) with that on \(Y_j\), even when
\(r_j\) changes the generic fibre birationally. In the normal
integral case \(X_L\) has one reduced component of generic
multiplicity one, so this same computation is its
model-independent value.

Finally every analytic point \(x\) of \(X\) has a point above it in
\(X_L^{\an}\). Indeed \(\mathcal H(x)\otimes_K L\) is a nonzero finite
algebra over \(\mathcal H(x)\). The residue field of a maximal ideal
of that algebra is finite over \(\mathcal H(x)\) and has its unique
extending absolute value by \mbox{\hyperref[fnd:finiteextensionnorms]{finite extension of norms}}.
Its restriction to \(L\) is the specified extending norm. Choose an affine
open \(\operatorname{Spec}B\subset X\) at the scheme point of \(x\).
The map from \(B\otimes_K L\) into this valued field defines an actual
point of the \mbox{\hyperref[fnd:affineanalytificationconstruction]{affine analytification}}
above \(x\), by restriction of its seminorm to \(B\).
Apply Lemma~\ref{f9be:pullback} to each of the two downstairs systems.
Their actual pulled-back norm values at the chosen lift are their
downstairs norm values at \(x\) through the same generic line
identifications. Equality at every upstairs point therefore gives
downstairs equality at every \(x\). Apply
\mbox{\hyperref[f9mi:independence]{model independence}} in the inherited
downstairs class with the identical \((X,L_i,s_i,S_i)\). This gives
equality of their supported values.
\end{proof}

statement.tex:
\begin{corollary}[Permitted computations upstairs]\label{f9be:descent}
Write $[\cY]=\sum_j m_j[Y_j]$ with reduced irreducible components
$Y_j$. For each $j$, let
$r_j:\widetilde Y_j\to Y_j$ be a supplied proper birational map
from an integral proper flat $R'$-scheme.
Use all actual pulled-back data and supports. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:weighted}
 J_R(\cX)=
 \sum_j m_j\,\frac{\lambda_L}{A}
       \deg_{k'}\bigl(I_{j,0}\cdots I_{j,d}
                                  [\widetilde Y_j]\bigr).
\end{equation}
There is no assertion here that the supplied modifications exist.

If the reduced generic components of $X_L$ are normal, each summand
may instead be computed on any computing model in the class of
\texttt{f9mi:independence} with those pulled-back metrics, sections
and generic supports. In particular, when $X_L$ is normal integral,
its model-independent value equals the downstairs value.

For two downstairs systems with the same $(X,L_i,s_i,S_i)$ in the
inherited model-independent class, equality of their pulled-back
root model norms at every point of $X_L^{\an}$ implies equality of
their downstairs supported values.
\end{corollary}

statement.html: Suppose, in addition to the preceding algebraic data, that a good Hausdorff pure dd-dimensional KK-analytic space UU, a coherent module ℱ\mathcal F and an ordinary smooth compactly supported (d,d)(d,d)-form α\alpha are supplied, together with a proved identity $$J_R(\cX)=\int_{U/K,\mathcal F}\alpha .$$ Let the upstairs analytic datum be its actual scalar pullback. Then for every finite L/KL/K as above, $$J_{R'}(\cY)= \int_{U_L/L,p^*\mathcal F}p^*\alpha,\qquad J_{\cY/R}= \int_{(U_L)_{[K]}/K,p^*\mathcal F}p^*\alpha .$$
statement.tex:
\begin{proposition}[A supplied smooth realization]\label{f9be:smoothscope}
Suppose, in addition to the preceding algebraic data, that a good
Hausdorff pure $d$-dimensional $K$-analytic space $U$, a coherent
module $\mathcal F$ and an ordinary smooth compactly supported
$(d,d)$-form $\alpha$ are supplied, together with a proved identity
\[
                 J_R(\cX)=\int_{U/K,\mathcal F}\alpha .
\]
Let the upstairs analytic datum be its actual scalar pullback.
Then for every finite $L/K$ as above,
\[
 J_{R'}(\cY)=
       \int_{U_L/L,p^*\mathcal F}p^*\alpha,\qquad
 J_{\cY/R}=
       \int_{(U_L)_{[K]}/K,p^*\mathcal F}p^*\alpha .
\]
\end{proposition}
