\begin{proof}
Write \(F=\widetilde{\mathcal H(x)}^{\rm gr}\),
\(k=\widetilde K^{\rm gr}\), and \(R=\mathscr R(X,x)\). For a
valuation locus \(P\) in \(\mathscr P_k(F)\) and homogeneous elements
\(a_i\) of \(F\), write \(P\{a_i\}\) for the valuations in \(P\)
whose rings contain all \(a_i\). By affineness write
\(R=\mathscr P_k(F)\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m\}\) with nonzero
homogeneous \(\alpha_i\). Set \(r_i=\deg(\alpha_i)\).
Replace \(X\) by a compact separated analytic neighbourhood
as supplied by Proposition~\ref{fnd:gradedgermseparation}.
An ordinary neighbourhood within this representative is also
an ordinary neighbourhood in the original space.

First consider a cover of the germ by two good subdomain germs with
reductions \(R\{\lambda\}\) and \(R\{\lambda^{-1}\}\), where
\(\lambda\in F\) is nonzero and homogeneous and \(t=\deg(\lambda)\).
Choose affinoid representatives \(Y\) and \(Z\) that are
ordinary neighbourhoods of \(x\) \emph{within their respective
subdomain germs}. We will shrink each only by neighbourhoods in
that side. Such shrinkings leave the union a neighbourhood in \(X\):
on each original side a relative neighbourhood contains the
intersection with an ambient ordinary neighbourhood of \(x\);
intersect the two ambient neighbourhoods with an open set contained
in the original union. This is the topological part of
Lemma~\ref{fnd:nettopologyboundedgluing}. All finite unions of
the affinoid pieces used below are analytic domains in the chosen
separated representative by Proposition~\ref{fnd:generalnetdomaincalculus}
and the affinoid quasi-net definition. Indeed their compact pieces are closed
there, and at each point the pieces containing it cover a relative
neighbourhood in the union after removing the finitely many pieces
that omit the point. This gives the required affinoid quasi-net
in the domain definition.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{The actual overlap.}
By Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedweierstrassgerm}, after shrinking the
two sides lift \(\lambda\) to units \(f\) on \(Y\) and \(g\)
on \(Z\). Lift \(\alpha_i\) to functions \(f_i\) on \(Y\).
These initials lie in the same \(F\), by the completed-residue-field
comparison for domain inclusions
(Corollary~\ref{fnd:domainresiduefields}). Impose \(|f|\leq t\) and
\(|f_i|\leq r_i\) on \(Y\), and \(|g^{-1}|\leq t^{-1}\)
on \(Z\). The active Weierstrass reduction formula gives the
original reduction for each cut in its side. The good-germ
domain classification, applied with the whole reduction of that
side, gives an ordinary neighbourhood. The cuts are actual affinoid domains by the rational quotient
formulas of Theorems~\ref{fnd:generalizedrationalpoints}
and~\ref{fnd:generalizedrationaluniversal}.

Their intersection is affinoid by
Lemma~\ref{fnd:separatedaffinoidintersections}. On it
\(|f(x)-g(x)|<t\), where the difference is evaluated in the
common completed residue field. Remove the portion where
\(|f-g|\geq t\) by shrinking both sides. More precisely choose
an open neighbourhood of \(x\) in the intersection on which
\(|f-g|<t\), lift this open set to an ambient open set and take
affinoid ordinary neighbourhoods in both sides inside it.
The new affinoid intersection \(W_0\) is compact, so
\(\sup_{W_0}|f-g|<t\). The opposite bounds on \(f\) and \(g\)
give \(|f|=|g|=t\) there. The reduced image of \(W_0\) is
\(R\{\lambda,\lambda^{-1}\}\) by the intersection identity
of Theorem~\ref{fnd:allgradedgermreduction}. It is also the
reduction of \(Y\{|f^{-1}|\leq t^{-1}\}\) and of
\(Z\{|g|\leq t\}\). By
Theorem~\ref{fnd:goodgermdomainclassification} these equalities
give equality of subdomain germs within each side. Choose
affinoid ordinary neighbourhoods \(Y_1\subset Y\) and
\(Z_1\subset Z\) on which the equalities hold, so that
\[
 A_Y=Y_1\cap Z=Y_1\{|f^{-1}|\leq t^{-1}\},\qquad
 A_Z=Y\cap Z_1=Z_1\{|g|\leq t\}.
\]

Choose a strict rational neighbourhood \(W'\) of \(x\) in
\(W_0\) contained in \(Y_1\cap Z_1\), using
Lemma~\ref{fnd:strictrationalinteriorneighborhood} on the
ordinary neighbourhood \(Y_1\cap Z_1\) in \(W_0\).
Write its finitely many inequalities as
\(|u_a|\leq c_a\) and \(|v_b|\geq d_b\), all strict at \(x\).
The map from either side \(Y_1\) or \(Z_1\) to the corresponding
overlap algebra has dense image: on the actual Weierstrass
quotient (Theorems~\ref{fnd:generalizedrationalpoints}
and~\ref{fnd:generalizedrationaluniversal}), polynomials in the adjoined function are already
restrictions from the side and their Tate-series truncations
are dense. Approximate the restrictions of the \(u_a,v_b\)
from each side in its own overlap norm with errors strictly
below \(c_a,d_b\), respectively. Cut each side by the resulting
inequalities. Bounded point evaluations and the ultrametric
inequality show that the cuts meet \(A_Y\) and \(A_Z\) in exactly
\(W'\). The cut inequalities are still strict at \(x\), so both
new affinoid domains are ordinary neighbourhoods in their
respective sides. The affinoid upper and lower cuts here are
successive actual rational quotients (for an upper bound use
denominator \(1\), and for a positive lower bound use numerator
\(1\)). Thus the two new sides, again denoted by \(Y\) and \(Z\),
have the actual common overlap
\[
 W=Y\cap Z=Y\{|f|\geq t\}=Z\{|g|\leq t\}=W'.
\]
For example, the left annulus is the intersection of the left
cut with \(A_Y\), hence is \(W'\), and \(W'\) is also contained
in the right cut. The right annulus is checked using \(A_Z\).
The rational quotient maps give these identifications as analytic
domains, with the same ring of analytic functions on \(W\).

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Relative presentations.}
Write \(B=\mathcal O(Y)\), \(C=\mathcal O(Z)\), and
\(D=\mathcal O(W)\). Since \(f\) is a unit on \(Y\), choose
\(0<p<t\) with \(\rho_B(f^{-1})<p^{-1}\), where \(\rho\)
denotes the spectral seminorm. The upper bounds on \(f_i,f\)
and the bound on \(f^{-1}\) give the bounded map
\[
 P_B=K\{r^{-1}T,t^{-1}S,pS^{-1}\}\longrightarrow B,
 \qquad (T_i,S)\longmapsto(f_i,f).
\]
Here Theorem~\ref{fnd:generalizedpointwisepowerbound} and
Proposition~\ref{fnd:powerboundedsubstitution} apply to these actual
functions,
including at an equality of a bound. The evaluated graded
image of \(P_B\) contains \(k[\alpha_i,\lambda]\).
The evaluated image of \(B\) is finitely generated over \(k\)
by the
\hyperref[fnd:gradedfixedabsolutepresentation]{fixed absolute presentation result}.
Its valuation locus is \(R\{\lambda\}\);
Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedvaluationintegrality} makes it
finite over \(k[\alpha_i,\lambda]\), and hence over the
intermediate evaluated image of \(P_B\). The selected
\hyperref[fnd:gradedrelativepointevaluation]{relative point criterion}
now gives an admissible presentation
\(P_B\{a^{-1}U\}\twoheadrightarrow B\) with coordinates
\(u_j\) satisfying \(|u_j(x)|<a_j\).
Proposition~\ref{fnd:closedweightedpresentation} identifies this
relative presentation with the corresponding absolute
weighted Laurent presentation, with the extra coordinates
included.

Give \(D\) the quotient norm from the left boundary
presentation, obtained by imposing \(|f^{-1}|\leq t^{-1}\)
and keeping the same other weights. Density of \(C\to D\)
for its actual Weierstrass overlap is valid for this norm:
the initially given overlap Banach norms are equivalent by
the affinoid-domain identifications. Choose \(g_i,g'\in C\)
with \(\|f_i-g_i\|_D<r_i\) and \(\|f-g'\|_D<t\).
On all of \(W\), \(|g'-g|<t\) and \(|g_i|\leq r_i\).
Choose \(\sup_W |g'-g|<e<t\), and cut \(Z\) by
\(|g'-g|\leq e\). This contains \(W\) and is an ordinary
neighbourhood of \(x\). On this cut the ratio \((g'-g)/g\)
has spectral bound \(e/t<1\). The power bound gives
convergence of the geometric inverse, so \(g'\) is a unit
and has the same pointwise modulus as \(g\). It keeps the
same right annulus; replace \(g\) by \(g'\).
The \(g_i\) have initials \(\alpha_i\) at \(x\).
Impose \(|g_i|\leq r_i\) on the right. These cuts contain
\(W\) and have full reduction in the right germ, hence are
ordinary neighbourhoods there. The actual common overlap
and both annular equations are unchanged.

Take \(q>t\) with \(q>\rho_C(g)\) on the new right side.
Apply the right-hand relative-point calculation to
\[
 P_C=K\{r^{-1}T,q^{-1}S,tS^{-1}\}\longrightarrow C,
 \qquad (T_i,S)\longmapsto(g_i,g).
\]
The inverse coordinate gives \(\lambda^{-1}\) in degree
\(t^{-1}\), and the degree-\(q\) direct coordinate evaluates to
zero. The same fixed-absolute, integral-criterion and intermediate
graded-image argument gives an admissible presentation
\(P_C\{b^{-1}V\}\twoheadrightarrow C\), with coordinates
\(v_\ell\) satisfying \(|v_\ell(x)|<b_\ell\).
These are precisely the two separately signed relative-point
applications.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Matching the extra coordinates.}
In the same left quotient norm on \(D\), use the two dense
restriction maps to choose \(u'_j\in C\), \(v'_\ell\in B\)
with
\[
 \|u_j-u'_j\|_D<a_j,\qquad \|v'_\ell-v_\ell\|_D<b_\ell .
\]
Cut \(Y\) by \(|v'_\ell|\le b_\ell\) and \(Z\) by
\(|u'_j|\le a_j\). The original coordinate bounds on the
overlap and these strict differences show that both cuts
contain the entire \(W\). The same inequalities and strictness
of the original coordinates at \(x\) give strictness at \(x\)
for these cuts. Thus they are ordinary neighbourhoods on their
respective sides. They preserve the common overlap \(W\)
and the two exact annular descriptions.

Adjoining the cut coordinates through the actual Weierstrass
quotients gives the two bounded norm-strict epimorphisms of
Theorem~\ref{fnd:doublelaurentaffinoidgluing}, with coordinate
lists \((f_i,u_j,v'_\ell)\) and \((g_i,u'_j,v_\ell)\)
of respective common weights \((r_i,a_j,b_\ell)\), and with
annulus bounds \(p<t<q\). Indeed the two relative presentations
are admissible, and adjoining variables and using the actual
cut relations preserves this property by the coefficientwise
quotient comparison. The left boundary map onto \(D\)
still takes each old variable to its old restriction. Every
old lift is a lift in the augmented free Laurent algebra of
the same norm, so the new left quotient norm on \(D\) is
at most the old one. All strict coordinate differences
therefore hold in the norm required by the gluing theorem.
That theorem makes the union affinoid. The neighbourhood
argument at the start shows that this union is an ordinary
affinoid neighbourhood of \(x\) in \(X\).

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Reduction to the two-chart case.}
Take a finite affinoid subdomain-germ cover of \((X,x)\)
in the compact separated representative. Its reductions
are affine opens in \(R\) in the common \(F\). By adjoining
finite homogeneous generators to those for \(R\), write them
as loci \(R\{\lambda_{i1},\ldots,\lambda_{ie_i}\}\).
Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedrzlaurentrefinement} gives a finite
subordinate cover by all the sign cells
\(R\{\mu_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,\mu_n^{\epsilon_n}\}\).
In a good chart containing a given cell's reduction, lift
the \(\mu_j^{\epsilon_j}\) to functions and impose the active
Weierstrass inequalities. Lemma~\ref{fnd:gradedweierstrassgerm}
identifies the resulting affinoid subdomain germ's reduction
with that cell. These good lifted subdomains cover by
Theorems~\ref{fnd:allgradedgermreduction}
and~\ref{fnd:allgermdomainclassification}.
We induct on the number \(n\) of coordinates in such a sign
cover of an affine-reduction germ. Each sign locus contains the
valuation with ring \(F\) and is therefore nonempty.
For \(n=0\) the single good subdomain has full reduction,
so by classification it is the full germ and supplies an
ordinary affinoid neighbourhood. For \(n>0\), the lifted
subdomains grouped by the first sign have unions with
reductions \(R\{\mu_1\}\) and \(R\{\mu_1^{-1}\}\).
They are subdomain germs, as in finite unions in the
classification, and the other signs give each a cover with
\(n-1\) functions. Induction makes both subdomain germs
good in their own topology. The two-chart argument applied
to these two germs then gives an ordinary affinoid
neighbourhood in the whole germ. This completes the induction.
\end{proof}

                   \mathcal I_{M,f}(\alpha)
                              =\sum_\sigma m_\sigma\int_\sigma\alpha.
\]

All cells with nonzero weights are compact polytopes:
the actual moment image is \hyperref[fnd:boundedspectrumcompact]{compact}, and the complex is
finite. Consequently the integral is a finite sum of
the integrals constructed in
Lemma~\ref{v037:integration:polyhedralcalculus}.

proof.html:
Theorem [v037:globaltrop:finiteimage] gives a finite polyhedral image of dimension at most dd and a finite boundary image of dimension at most d−1d-1. At a point in the relative interior of a dd-cell, the whole moment fibre is therefore interior, and the local image is contained in that cell’s affine dd-plane. \(\mathcal O(V)/I_V\) of Corollary~\ref{fnd:generalizedaffinoidquotients},
with restriction as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{fnd:closedimmersiontargetglocal}. The cutoff support and
pullback of germs use Theorem~\ref{v037:forms:germsheaf}.
For a cutoff stage \(Q=(V,f,\Omega,\chi)\) on \(X\), its inverse
image \(W=Y\times_XV\) is the actual affinoid closed subspace of
\(V\). The pulled-back tuple is a unit tuple. Closedness of the
immersion makes \(j^{-1}\Supp\chi\) compact, and continuity gives
\[
 j^{-1}\Int_{\rm top}(V,X)\subseteq\Int_{\rm top}(W,Y).
\]
Hence \(j^*\chi\) is an admissible cutoff on \(Y\), and
\[
 j^*Q\eta=Q_{(W,f|_W,\Omega,j^*\chi)}\eta.
\]
The empty inverse image gives zero. This is a continuous single-stage
factorization, so finality proves pullback continuity.
\NAG{002966} gives the analytic-interior support and differential
statements. Applying this argument to the base-changed closed immersion
\(j^{-1}U\hookrightarrow U\) gives the restricted assertion.
\end{proof}

proof.html: For two given formal arrows with actual compatible generic charts, equality of their generic maps gives equality of their formal point maps by specialization surjectivity and contraction. At a formal source point, choose a common target affine neighborhood of its image and a source affine neighborhood mapping there under both arrows. proof.tex:
For two given formal arrows with actual compatible generic charts,
equality of their generic maps gives equality of their formal point
maps by specialization surjectivity and contraction. At a formal
source point, choose a common target affine neighborhood of its image
and a source affine neighborhood mapping there under both arrows.
The two pullback homomorphisms agree after inverting \(\pi\).
The coefficient ring of the source is \(\pi\)-torsion-free, so the
homomorphisms agree there integrally. The arrows agree on this affine
cover and hence on the source.
